questions.question: The Maximum Zero Fuel Mass is the mass of the aeroplane with no usable fuel on board. It is a limitation which is:
choices: governed by the requirements of the centre of gravity limits and the structural limits of the aeroplane.
tabulated in the Flight Manual against arguments of airfield elevation and temperature.
governed by the traffic load to be carried. It also provides protection from excessive 'wing bending'.
listed in the Flight Manual as a fixed value. It is a structural limit.
questions.answerText: listed in the Flight Manual as a fixed value. It is a structural limit.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 033-9583A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 page 20) For the medium range twin jet the datum point is located
choices: 540 cm forward of the front spar.
on the nose of the aeroplane.
at the leading edge of the Mean Aerodynamic Chord (MAC).
540 inches forward of the front spar.
questions.answerText: 540 inches forward of the front spar.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: In order to provide an adequate "buffet boundary" at the commencement of the cruise a speed of 1.3Vs is used. At a mass of 120000 kg this is a CAS of 180 knots. If the mass of the aeroplane is increased to 135000 kg the value of 1.3Vs will be
choices: increased to 191 knots, drag will increase and air distance per kg of fuel will decrease.
unaffected as Vs always occurs at the same angle of attack.
increased to 191 knots, drag will decrease and air distance per kg of fuel will increase.
increased to 202 knots but, since the same angle of attack is used, drag and range will remain the same.
questions.answerText: increased to 191 knots, drag will increase and air distance per kg of fuel will decrease.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following alternatives corresponds to zero fuel mass?
choices: Operating mass plus passengers and cargo.
Take-off mass minus fuel to destination and alternate.
The mass of an aeroplane with no usable fuel.
Operating mass plus load of passengers and cargo.
questions.answerText: The mass of an aeroplane with no usable fuel.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annexes 031-6564A and 031- 6564B or Loading Manual SEP1 Figure 2.4) With respect to a single-engine piston powered aeroplane, determine the zero fuel moment (lbs.In./100) in the following conditions: Basic Empty Mass: 2415 lbs. Arm at Basic Empty Mass: 77,9 In. Cargo Zone A: 350 lbs. Baggage Zone B: 35 lbs. Pilot and front seat passenger : 300 lbs (total)
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-12268A) Using the data given in the Load & Trim sheet, determine from the following the correct values for the take off mass and the position of the centre of gravity at that mass if the fuel index correction to be applied is given as - 0.9
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane, which is scheduled to fly an oceanic sector, is due to depart from a high altitude airport in the tropics at 1400 local time. The airport has an exceptionally long runway. Which of the following is most likely to be the limiting factor(s) in determining the take - off mass ?
choices: altitude and temperature of the departure airfield.
questions.answerText: altitude and temperature of the departure airfield.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The Maximum Zero Fuel Mass is a structural limiting mass. It is made up of the aeroplane Dry Operational mass plus
choices: traffic load and crew standard mass.
traffic load, unuseable fuel and crew standard mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11227A) An aeroplane, whose specific data is shown in the annex, has a planned take-off mass of 200 000 kg, with its centre of gravity (C.G.) located at 15.38 m rearward of the reference point, representing a C.G. location at 30 % MAC (Mean Aerodynamic Cord). The current cargo load distribution is: front cargo: 6 500 kg; rear cargo: 4 000 kg. For performance purposes, the captain decides to reset the value of the centre of gravity location to 33 % MAC. The front and rear cargo compartments are located at a distance of 15 m and 25 m from the reference point respectively. After the transfer operation, the new cargo load distribution is:
choices: front cargo: 9 260 kg; rear cargo: 1 240 kg
front cargo: 3 740 kg; rear cargo: 6 760 kg
front cargo: 6 760 kg; rear cargo: 3 740 kg
front cargo: 4 550 kg; rear cargo: 5 950 kg
questions.answerText: front cargo: 3 740 kg; rear cargo: 6 760 kg
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11257A and 031- 11257B ) The planned take-off mass of a turbojet aeroplane is 190 000 kg, with its centre of gravity located at 29 % MAC (Mean Aerodynamic Cord) . Shortly prior to engine start, the local staff informs the flight crew that 4 000 kg must be unloaded from cargo 4. After the handling operation, the new centre of gravity location in % MAC will be:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Calculate the centre of gravity in % MAC (mean aerodynamic chord) with following data: Distance datum - centre of gravity: 12.53 m Distance datum - leading edge: 9.63 m Length of MAC: 8 m
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11275A and 031-11275B.) A turbojet aeroplane has a planned take-off mass of 190 000 kg. After loading, its centre of gravity is at 38% MAC, beyond the limits. The captain decides to redistribute cargo between cargo compartments 1 and 4 to obtain a new CG at 31% MAC. What should the new cargo distribution be?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The Dry Operating Mass of an aeroplane includes :
choices: Fuel and passengers baggage and cargo.
Crew and crew baggage, catering, removable passenger service equipment, potable water and lavatory chemicals.
questions.answerText: Crew and crew baggage, catering, removable passenger service equipment, potable water and lavatory chemicals.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-12272A.) An operator's loading manual gives standard passenger masses that include hand baggage. The manifest and the standard mass for hold baggage are shown below. Using these values and the appendix, calculate the mass of freight loaded in hold 1 that makes up the remainder of the traffic load.
choices: no cargo can be loaded in hold number 1
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annexes 031-11069A and 031- 11069B) Contrary to the forecast given in the LOAD and TRIM sheet, cargo compartment 1 is empty. The take-off centre of gravity in MAC % (Mean Aerodynamic Chord) will be located at:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Standard masses may be used for the computation of mass values for baggage if the aeroplane
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane is performance limited to a landing mass of 54230 kg. The Dry Operating Mass is 35000 kg and the zero fuel mass is 52080 kg. If the take-off mass is 64280 kg the useful load is
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The operator of an aircraft equipped with 50 seats uses standard masses for passengers and baggage. During the preparation of a scheduled flight a group of passengers present themselves at the check-in desk, it is apparent that even the lightest of these exceeds the value of the declared standard mass.
choices: the operator is obliged to use the actual masses of each passenger
the operator should use the individual masses of the passengers or alter the standard masss
the operator may use the standard masses for the load and balance calculation without correction
the operator may use the standard masses for the balance but must correct these for the load calculation
questions.answerText: the operator should use the individual masses of the passengers or alter the standard masss
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Given: Maximum structural take-off mass= 146 900 kg Maximum structural landing mass= 93 800 kg Maximum zero fuel mass= 86 400 kg Trip fuel= 27 500 kg Block fuel= 35 500 kg Engine starting and taxi fuel = 1 000 kg The maximum take-off mass is equal to:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: In determining the Dry Operating Mass of an aeroplane it is common practice to use 'standard mass' values for crew. These values are
choices: flight crew (male) 88 kg. (female) 75 kg., cabin crew 75 kg. each. These include an allowance for hand baggage.
flight crew (male) 88 kg. (female) 75 kg., cabin crew 75 kg. each. These do not include an allowance for hand baggage.
flight crew 85 kg., cabin crew 75 kg. each. These are inclusive of a hand baggage allowance.
flight crew 85 kg., cabin crew 75 kg. each. These do not include a hand baggage allowance.
questions.answerText: flight crew 85 kg., cabin crew 75 kg. each. These are inclusive of a hand baggage allowance.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The maximum certificated take - off mass is :
choices: a take - off limiting mass which is governed by the gradient of climb after reaching V2 .
limited by the runway take off distance available. It is tabulated in the Flight Manual.
a structural limit which may not be exceeded for any take - off.
a take - off limiting mass which is affected by the aerodrome altitude and temperature.
questions.answerText: a structural limit which may not be exceeded for any take - off.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The maximum zero-fuel mass: 1- is a regulatory limitation 2- is calculated for a maximum load factor of +3.5 g 3- is due to the maximum permissible bending moment at the wing root 4- imposes fuel dumping from the outer wings tank first 5- imposes fuel dumping from the inner wings tank first 6- can be increased by stiffening the wing The combination of correct statements is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The maximum zero fuel mass is a mass limitation for the:
choices: allowable load exerted upon the wing considering a margin for fuel tanking
total load of the fuel imposed upon the wing
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-9643 A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.14) The following data relates to a planned flight of an aeroplane - Dry Operational mass 60520 kg Performance limited take-off mass 92750 kg Performance limited landing mass 72250 kg Maximum Zero Fuel mass 67530 kg Fuel on board at take-off - Trip fuel 12500 kg Contingency and final reserve fuel 2300 kg Alternate fuel 1700 kg Using this data, as appropriate, calculate the maximum traffic load that can be carried.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-9604 A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.11) The aeroplane has a mass of 61 000 kg in the cruise. The range of safe CG positions, as determined from the appropriate graph in the loading manual, is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The Take-off Mass of an aeroplane is 66700 kg which includes a traffic load of 14200 kg and a usable fuel load of 10500 kg. If the standard mass for the crew is 545 kg the Dry Operating Mass is
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The centre of gravity location of the aeroplane is normally computed along the:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Assume: Aeroplane gross mass: 4750 kg Centre of gravity at station: 115.8 What will be the new position of the centre of gravity if 100 kg is moved from the station 30 to station 120?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The determination of the centre of gravity in relation to the mean aerodynamic chord:
choices: consists of defining the centre of gravity longitudinally in relation to the length of the mean aerodynamic chord and the leading edge
consists of defining the centre of gravity longitudinally in relation to the length of the mean aerodynamic chord and the trailing edge
consists of defining the centre of gravity longitudinally in relation to the position of the aerodynamic convergence point
consists of defining the centre of gravity longitudinally in relation to the position of the aerodynamic centre of pressure
questions.answerText: consists of defining the centre of gravity longitudinally in relation to the length of the mean aerodynamic chord and the leading edge
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11246A and 031- 11246B) The planned take-off mass of an aeroplane is 180 000 kg, with its centre of gravity located at 31 % MAC (Mean Aerodynamic Cord). Shortly prior to engine start, the local staff informs the crew that an additional load of 4 000 kg must be loaded in cargo 1. After loading this cargo, the new centre of gravity location will be:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The empty mass of an aeroplane, as given in the weighing schedule, is 61300 kg. The operational items (including crew) is given as a mass of 2300 kg. If the take-off mass is 132000 kg (including a useable fuel quantity of 43800 kg) the useful load is
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The centre of gravity of a body is that point
choices: through which the sum of the forces of all masses of the body is considered to act.
where the sum of the moments from the external forces acting on the body is equal to zero.
where the sum of the external forces is equal to zero.
which is always used as datum when computing moments.
questions.answerText: through which the sum of the forces of all masses of the body is considered to act.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-9608 A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.9) Referring to the loading manual for the transport aeroplane, the maximum running load for the aft section of the forward lower deck cargo compartment is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: For the purpose of completing the Mass and Balance documentation, the Traffic Load is considered to be equal to the Take-off Mass
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The centre of gravity of an aeroplane
choices: may only be moved if permitted by the regulating authority and endorsed in the aeroplane's certificate of airworthiness.
is in a fixed position and is unaffected by aeroplane loading.
must be maintained in a fixed position by careful distribution of the load.
can be allowed to move between defined limits.
questions.answerText: can be allowed to move between defined limits.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-9644 A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.14) Aeroplane Dry Operating mass 85000 kg Performance limited take-off mass 127000 kg Performance limited landing mass 98500 kg Maximum zero fuel mass 89800 kg Fuel requirements for flight - Trip fuel 29300 kg Contingency and final reserve fuel 3600 kg Alternate fuel 2800 kg. The maximum traffic load that can be carried on this flight is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-1580A) A jet aeroplane, with the geometrical characteristics shown in the appendix, has a take-off weight (W) of 460 000 N and a centre of gravity (point G on annex) located at 15.40 m from the zero reference point. At the last moment the station manager has 12 000 N of freight added in the forward compartment at 10 m from the zero reference point. The final location of the centre of gravity, calculated in percentage of mean aerodynamic chord AB (from point A), is equal to:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane is loaded with its centre of gravity towards the rear limit. This will result in :
choices: a reduced fuel consumption as a result of reduced drag.
a reduction in power required for a given speed.
an increased risk of stalling due to a decrease in tailplane moment
questions.answerText: an increased risk of stalling due to a decrease in tailplane moment
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: On an aeroplane with a seating capacity of more than 30, it is decided to use standard mass values for computing the total mass of passengers. If the flight is not a holiday charter, the mass value which may be used for an adult is
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Allowed traffic load is the difference between :
choices: allowed take off mass and basic mass
allowed take off mass and operating mass
allowed take off mass and basic mass plus trip fuel
questions.answerText: allowed take off mass and operating mass
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11247A and 031-11247B.) A turbojet aeroplane has a corrected dry operating mass of 110 100 kg, basic corrected index 118.6, take-off mass 200 000 kg, and CG at 32% MAC. The initial cargo distribution is shown below; all other cargo compartments are empty. Cargo is to be redistributed between compartments 1 and 4 to achieve a take-off CG of 35% MAC. What will the new loads in compartments 1 and 4 be?
choices: 1 000 kg in cargo 1; 3 000 kg in cargo 4
2 500 kg in cargo 1; 1 500 kg in cargo 4
3 000 kg in cargo 1; 1 000 kg in cargo 4
2 000 kg in cargo 1; 2 000 kg in cargo 4
questions.answerText: 2 500 kg in cargo 1; 1 500 kg in cargo 4
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031 11634A) Maximum allowed take-off mass limit: 37 200kg Dry operating mass: 21 600 kg Take-off fuel: 8 500 kg Passengers on board: male 33, female 32, children 5 Baggages: 880 kg The company uses the standard passenger mass systems (see annex) allowed by regulations. The flight is not a holiday charter. In these conditions, the maximum cargo that may be loaded is
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Fuel loaded onto an aeroplane is 15400 kg but is erroneously entered into the load and trim sheet as 14500 kg. This error is not detected by the flight crew but they will notice that
choices: V1 will be reached sooner than expected
the aeroplane will rotate much earlier than expected.
speed at un-stick will be higher than expected
questions.answerText: speed at un-stick will be higher than expected
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Prior to departure an aeroplane is loaded with 16500 litres of fuel at a fuel density of 780 kg/m³. This is entered into the load sheet as 16500 kg and calculations are carried out accordingly. As a result of this error, the aeroplane is
choices: lighter than anticipated and the calculated safety speeds will be too high
lighter than anticipated and the calculated safety speeds will be too low
heavier than anticipated and the calculated safety speeds will be too high
heavier than anticipated and the calculated safety speeds will be too low.
questions.answerText: lighter than anticipated and the calculated safety speeds will be too high
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The standard mass for a child is
choices: 35 kg for holiday charters and 38 kg for all other flights.
30 kg for holiday charters and 35 kg for all other flights.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11619A ) A helicopter's basic mass is 1 100 kg and the longitudinal CG-position is at 3.10 m. Determine the longitudinal CG position in the following conditions : - pilot and front passenger : 150 kg - rear passengers : 150 kg - fuel : 500 kg
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-9596 A or Loading Manual MRJT 1 Figure 4.11) At the maximum landing mass the range of safe CG positions, as determined from the appropriate graph in the loading manual, is:
choices: Forward limit 8.0% MAC aft limit 27.2% MAC
Forward limit 8.6% MAC aft limit 27.0% MAC
Forward limit 8.0% MAC aft limit 26.8% MAC
Forward limit 7.4% MAC aft limit 27.0% MAC
questions.answerText: Forward limit 7.4% MAC aft limit 27.0% MAC
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: In cruise, an extreme aft longitudinal center of gravity:
choices: moves away the cyclic stick from its forward stop and increases the stress in the rotor head
brings the cyclic stick closer to its forward stop and decreases the stress in the rotor head
moves away the cyclic stick from its forward stop and decreases the stresses in the head rotors
brings the cyclic stick closer to its forward stop and increases the stress in the rotor head
questions.answerText: brings the cyclic stick closer to its forward stop and increases the stress in the rotor head
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annexes 031-11205A and 031-11205B.) A turbojet aeroplane has a corrected dry operating mass of 110 100 kg, basic corrected index 118.6, take-off mass 200 000 kg, and CG at 32% MAC. The initial cargo distribution is shown below; all other cargo compartments are empty. For performance reasons, the captain wants a take-off CG of 34% MAC. Which cargo transfer is required?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Given an aeroplane with: Maximum Structural Landing Mass: 68000 kg Maximum Zero Fuel Mass: 70200 kg Maximum Structural Take-off Mass: 78200 kg Dry Operating Mass : 48000 kg Scheduled trip fuel is 7000 kg and the reserve fuel is 2800 kg, Assuming performance limitations are not restricting, the maximum permitted take-off mass and maximum traffic load are respectively:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: The centre of gravity of an aeroplane is at 25% of the Mean Aerodynamic Chord. This means that the centre of gravity of the aeroplane is situated at 25% of the length of:
choices: the mean aerodynamic chord in relation to the datum
the aeroplane in relation to the leading edge
the mean aerodynamic chord in relation to the leading edge
the mean aerodynamic chord in relation to the trailing edge
questions.answerText: the mean aerodynamic chord in relation to the leading edge
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Given: Dry Operating Mass= 29 800 kg Maximum Take-Off Mass= 52 400 kg Maximum Zero-Fuel Mass= 43 100 kg Maximum Landing Mass= 46 700 kg Trip fuel= 4 000 kg Fuel quantity at brakes release= 8 000 kg The maximum traffic load is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The maximum intensity floor loading for an aeroplane is given in the Flight Manual as 650 kg per square metre. What is the maximum mass of a package which can be safely supported on a pallet with dimensions of 80 cm by 80 cm?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane with a two wheel nose gear and four main wheels rests on the ground with a single nose wheel load of 500 kg and a single main wheel load of 6000 kg. The distance between the nose wheels and the main wheels is 10 meter. How far is the centre of gravity in front of the main wheels?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Moment (balance) arms are measured from a specific point to the body station at which the mass is located. That point is known as
choices: the centre of gravity of the aeroplane.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The total mass of the aeroplane including crew, crew baggage; plus catering and removable passenger equipment; plus potable water and lavatory chemicals but excluding usable fuel and traffic load, is referred to as:
choices: Aeroplane Prepared for Service ( APS) Mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: A jet transport has the following structural limits: -Maximum Ramp Mass: 63 060 kg -Maximum Take Off Mass: 62 800 kg -Maximum Landing Mass: 54 900 kg -Maximum Zero Fuel Mass: 51 300 kg The aeroplane's fuel is loaded accordance with the following requirements: -Taxi fuel: 400 kg -Trip fuel: 8400 kg -Contingency & final reserve fuel: 1800 kg -Alternate fuel: 1100 kg If the Dry Operating Mass is 34930 kg, determine the maximum traffic load that can be carried on the flight if departure and landing airfields are not performance limited.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-12273A) From the data contained in the attached appendix, the maximum allowable take - off mass and traffic load is respectively :
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The total mass of an aeroplane is 9000 kg. The centre of gravity (cg) position is at 2.0 m from the datum line. The aft limit for cg is at 2.1 m from the datum line. What mass of cargo must be shifted from the front cargo hold (at 0.8 m from the datum) to the aft hold (at 3.8 m), to move the cg to the aft limit?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The zero fuel mass of an aeroplane is always:
choices: The maximum take-off mass minus the take-off fuel mass.
The take-off mass minus the take-off fuel mass.
The take-off mass minus the wing fuel mass.
The take-off mass minus the fuselage fuel mass.
questions.answerText: The take-off mass minus the take-off fuel mass.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11250A, 031-11250B and 031-11250C) Knowing that: . Dry operating mass: 110 000 kg . Basic index: 119.1 . Number of passengers: 335 distributed as shown in the annex (75 kg per PAX) . Cargo load + luggage: 9 500 kg distributed as shown in the annex. . Fuel: 40 000 kg Stages (1) to (7) and (11) having already been calculated, the centre of gravity in % MAC (Mean Aerodynamic Cord) for zero fuel mass is located at:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Considering only structural limitations, on very short legs with minimum take-off fuel, the traffic load is normally limited by:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: An aeroplane has its centre of gravity located 7 metres from the datum line and it has a mass of 49000 N. The moment about the datum is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Given the following information at take-off, calculate the landing centre of gravity. The flight time is 2 hours, the estimated fuel flow is 1050 litres per hour, and the average oil consumption is 2.25 litres per hour. The specific density of fuel is 0.79 kg/L and the specific density of oil is 0.96 kg/L.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: 'Standard Mass' as used in the computation of passenger load establish the mass of a child as
choices: 35 kg irrespective of age provided they occupy a seat.
35 kg only if they are over 2 years old and occupy a seat.
35 kg for children over 2 years occupying a seat and 10 kg for infants (less than 2 years) not occupying a seat.
35 kg for children over 2 years occupying a seat and 10 kg for infants (less than 2 years) occupying a seat.
questions.answerText: 35 kg irrespective of age provided they occupy a seat.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: Determine the Zero Fuel Mass for the following single engine aeroplane. Given : Standard Empty Mass : 1764 lbs Optional Equipment : 35 lbs Pilot + Front seat passenger : 300 lbs Cargo Mass : 350 lbs Ramp Fuel = Block Fuel : 60 Gal. Trip Fuel : 35 Gal. Fuel density : 6 lbs/Gal.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: In mass and balance calculations the "index" is:
choices: the moment divided by a constant.
a location in the aeroplane identified by a number.
an imaginary vertical plane or line from which all measurements are taken.
the range of moments the centre of gravity (cg) can have without making the aeroplane unsafe to fly.
questions.answerText: the moment divided by a constant.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option A as correct.

questions.question: The take-off mass of an aeroplane is 117 000 kg, comprising a traffic load of 18 000 kg and fuel of 46 000 kg. What is the dry operating mass?
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: The take-off mass of an aeroplane is 141000 kg. Total fuel on board is 63000 kg including 14000 kg reserve fuel and 1000 kg of unusable fuel. The traffic load is 12800 kg. The zero fuel mass is:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Mass for individual passengers (to be carried on an aeroplane) may be determined from a verbal statement by or on behalf of the passengers if the number of
choices: passenger seats available is less than 6.
passenger seats available is less than 20.
questions.answerText: passenger seats available is less than 6.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: To measure the mass and CG-position of an aircraft, it should be weighed with a minimum of:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: The Maximum Take-off Mass is equal to the maximum mass when leaving the ramp.
The Basic Empty Mass is equal to the mass of the aeroplane excluding traffic load and useable fuel but including the crew.
The Maximum Landing Mass of an aeroplane is restricted by structural limitations, performance limitations and the strength of the runway.
The Maximum Zero Fuel Mass ensures that the centre of gravity remains within limit s after the uplift of fuel.
questions.answerText: The Maximum Landing Mass of an aeroplane is restricted by structural limitations, performance limitations and the strength of the runway.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.question: When establishing the mass breakdown of an aeroplane, the empty mass is defined as the sum of the:
choices: basic mass plus special equipment mass
standard empty mass plus specific equipment mass plus trapped fluids plus unusable fuel mass
empty mass dry plus variable equipment mass
basic mass plus variable equipment mass
questions.answerText: standard empty mass plus specific equipment mass plus trapped fluids plus unusable fuel mass
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option B as correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to affect the range of centre of gravity positions on an aeroplane?
choices: The need to maintain a low value of stalling speed.
The need to minimise drag forces and so improve efficiency.
Elevator and tailplane (horizontal stabiliser) effectiveness in all flight conditions.
questions.answerText: Elevator and tailplane (horizontal stabiliser) effectiveness in all flight conditions.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: A flight has been made from London to Valencia carrying minimum fuel and maximum traffic load. The following are the aeroplane's structural limits: -Maximum Ramp Mass: 69 900 kg -Maximum Take Off Mass: 69 300 kg -Maximum Landing Mass: 58 900 kg -Maximum Zero Fuel Mass: 52 740 kg The performance limited take off mass at Valencia is 67 330 kg. The landing mass at London is not performance limited. questions.question: The loaded centre of gravity (cg) of an aeroplane is 713 mm aft of datum. The mean aerodynamic chord lies between station 524 mm aft and 1706 mm aft. The cg expressed as % MAC (mean aerodynamic chord) is:

questions.question: (For this question use appendix 031-11605A) Without the crew, the weight and the CG-position of the aircraft are 7 000 kg and 4,70m. - the mass of the pilot is 90 kg - the mass of the copilot is 75 kg - the mass of the flight engineer is 90 kg With this crew on board, the CG-position of the aircraft will be:
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: The maximum certificated taxi (or ramp) mass is that mass to which an aeroplane may be loaded prior to engine start. It is :
choices: a value which varies with airfield temperature and altitude. Corrections are listed in the Flight Manual.
a value which varies only with airfield altitude. Standard corrections are listed in the Flight Manual.
a value which is only affected by the outside air temperature. Corrections are calculated from data given in the Flight Manual.
a fixed value which is listed in the Flight Manual.

questions.question: (For this question use annex 031-11251A , 031-11251B and 031-11251C) Knowing that: . Dry operating mass: 110 000 kg . Basic index: 119.1 . Number of passengers: 185 distributed as shown in the annex (75 kg per PAX) . Cargo load + luggage: 14 000 kg distributed as shown in the annex. . Fuel: 42 000 kg Stages (1) to (7) and (11) having already been calculated, the centre of gravity in % MAC (Mean Aerodynamic Cord) for zero fuel mass is located at:

questions.question: At the flight preparation stage, the following parameters in particular are available for determining the mass of the aircraft: 1- Dry operating mass 2- Operating mass Which statement is correct:
choices: The operating mass is the mass of the aeroplane without take-off fuel.
The dry operating mass includes take-off fuel.
The operating mass includes the traffic load.
The dry operating mass includes fixed equipment needed to carry out a specific flight.
questions.answerText: The dry operating mass includes fixed equipment needed to carry out a specific flight.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: Given an aeroplane with: Maximum Structural Landing Mass: 125000 kg Maximum Zero Fuel Mass: 108500 kg Maximum Structural Take-off Mass: 155000 kg Dry Operating Mass: 82000 kg Scheduled trip fuel is 17000 kg and the reserve fuel is 5000 kg. Assuming performance limitations are not restricting, the maximum permitted take-off mass and maximum traffic load are respectively:

Shortly prior to engine start, the local staff informs the flight crew that an additional load of 4 000 kg must be loaded in cargo 4. After loading this cargo, the new centre of gravity location will be:

questions.question: With reference to mass and balance calculations (on an aeroplane) a datum point is used. This datum point is :
choices: a point near the centre of the aeroplane. It moves longitudinally as masses are added forward and aft of its location.
a point from which all balance arms are measured. The location of this point varies with the distribution of loads on the aeroplane.
a fixed point from which all balance arms are measured. It may be located anywhere on the aeroplane's longitudinal axis or on the extensions to that axis.
the point through which the sum of the mass values (of the aeroplane and its contents) is assumed to act vertically.
questions.answerText: a fixed point from which all balance arms are measured. It may be located anywhere on the aeroplane's longitudinal axis or on the extensions to that axis.
questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option C as correct.

questions.explanation: The answer sheet in the source PDF marks option D as correct.

questions.question: When was the Society of Aeronautical Engineers of the Philippines (SAEP) formed?
questions.explanation:
The Society of Aeronautical Engineers of the Philippines (SAEP) was formed on April 28, 1950. It was established by 15 individuals headed by Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara of FEATI University.

The organization played an important role in advancing the aeronautical engineering profession in the Philippines and later contributed to efforts toward establishing legislation regulating the profession.

💡 Memory Hook:
SAEP → 28-04-1950

🎯 Board Tip:
When memorizing the historical timeline, associate SAEP's formation with the earliest date: 1950.

questions.question: How many individuals initially formed the Society of Aeronautical Engineers of the Philippines (SAEP)?
questions.explanation:
SAEP was formed by 15 individuals headed by Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara of FEATI University.

The formation of the organization marked an important step in the development and advancement of the aeronautical engineering profession in the Philippines.

💡 Memory Hook:
SAEP = 15 Founders.

🎯 Board Tip:
The number 15 is a specific historical fact and can easily become a direct recall question.

questions.question: Who headed the group of individuals who formed the Society of Aeronautical Engineers of the Philippines (SAEP)?
questions.explanation:
SAEP was formed by 15 individuals headed by Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara of FEATI University on April 28, 1950.

Do not confuse Dr. Zara with the individuals who later composed the first Board of Aeronautical Engineering. The first Board was constituted much later, in 1982.

💡 Memory Hook:
Zara → SAEP Formation.

Albano → First Board Chairman.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question asks who headed the formation of SAEP, the answer is Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara.

questions.question: What was the primary mission of the Society of Aeronautical Engineers of the Philippines (SAEP)?
choices: To regulate all foreign airlines operating in the Philippines.
To develop and advance the Aeronautical Engineering profession toward its recognition in the international aviation industry.
To issue airworthiness certificates to aircraft.
questions.answerText: To develop and advance the Aeronautical Engineering profession toward its recognition in the international aviation industry.
questions.explanation:
The stated mission of SAEP was to develop and advance the Aeronautical Engineering profession toward its recognition in the international aviation industry.

This mission is important because SAEP's historical efforts were connected with the eventual establishment of legislation regulating the practice of aeronautical engineering in the Philippines.

The organization itself should not be confused with regulatory authorities such as CAAP or economic regulators such as CAB.

💡 Memory Hook:
SAEP → Develop + Advance + Recognize.

🎯 Board Tip:
SAEP is a professional organization. Its mission concerns the development and recognition of the profession, not the direct regulation of civil aviation operations.

questions.question: When was the Philippine Aeronautical Decree, Presidential Decree No. 1570, enacted?
questions.explanation:
Presidential Decree No. 1570, otherwise known as the Philippine Aeronautical Decree, was enacted on June 11, 1978.

The need for a law regulating the practice of aeronautical engineering became strongly felt in the late 1960s as the profession and available aeronautical engineering jobs increased tremendously.

Through the efforts of SAEP, PD 1570 was eventually enacted.

💡 Memory Hook:
PD 1570 → 11-06-1978.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse PD 1570 with RA 776:
• RA 776 → 1952
• PD 1570 → 1978
• RA 9497 → 2008

questions.question: What is the commonly cited name of Presidential Decree No. 1570?
choices: Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines
questions.explanation:
Presidential Decree No. 1570 is identified as the 'Philippine Aeronautical Decree.' It was enacted on June 11, 1978 through efforts associated with the development and advancement of the aeronautical engineering profession.

💡 Memory Hook:
PD 1570 = PAED = Philippine Aeronautical Decree.

🎯 Board Tip:
When you see 'Philippine Aeronautical Decree,' immediately associate it with PD 1570.

questions.question: Why was legislation regulating the practice of aeronautical engineering strongly needed in the Philippines during the late 1960s?
choices: Because the number of airports had completely disappeared.
Because aeronautical engineering and the jobs available for aeronautical engineers had increased tremendously.
Because all foreign airlines were prohibited from operating.
Because the Civil Aeronautics Authority had already been abolished.
questions.answerText: Because aeronautical engineering and the jobs available for aeronautical engineers had increased tremendously.
questions.explanation:
The need for a law regulating the practice of aeronautical engineering was strongly felt in the late 1960s because aeronautical engineering and the jobs available for aeronautical engineers had increased tremendously.

This development created a greater need for formal regulation of the profession.

💡 Memory Hook:
More Engineers + More Jobs → Need for Regulation.

🎯 Board Tip:
The question is testing the historical reason behind the movement toward PD 1570, not the details of civil aviation regulation.

questions.question: When was the first Board of Aeronautical Engineering constituted?
questions.explanation:
The first Board of Aeronautical Engineering was constituted on April 6, 1982.

It had Brig. Gen. Recaredo R. Albano as its Chairman, with Engrs. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr. and Teofilo P. Alberto as Members.

This occurred several years after PD 1570 was enacted in 1978.

💡 Memory Hook:
1982 → First Board.

🎯 Board Tip:
Keep the sequence straight:
PD 1570 → 1978
First Board → April 6, 1982
First Licensure Exam → July 1983

questions.question: Who served as Chairman of the first Board of Aeronautical Engineering?
questions.explanation:
The first Board of Aeronautical Engineering was constituted on April 6, 1982, with Brig. Gen. Recaredo R. Albano serving as Chairman.

The other members identified by  were Engr. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr. and Engr. Teofilo P. Alberto.

Do not confuse Brig. Gen. Albano with Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara. Zara headed the group that formed SAEP in 1950, while Albano later chaired the first Board.

💡 Memory Hook:
Albano → First Board Chairman.
Zara → SAEP Founder/Leader.

🎯 Board Tip:
Name-matching questions are easy points if you associate each person with their historical role.

questions.question: Who were the members of the first Board of Aeronautical Engineering aside from its Chairman?
choices: Engrs. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr. and Teofilo P. Alberto
Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara and Engr. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr.
Brig. Gen. Recaredo R. Albano and Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara
Engrs. Teofilo P. Alberto and Dr. Gregorio Y. Zara
questions.answerText: Engrs. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr. and Teofilo P. Alberto
questions.explanation:
The first Board of Aeronautical Engineering consisted of Brig. Gen. Recaredo R. Albano as Chairman and Engrs. Timoteo A. Cordova, Jr. and Teofilo P. Alberto as Members.

The Board was constituted on April 6, 1982.

💡 Memory Hook:
First Board = Albano + Cordova + Alberto.

🎯 Board Tip:
Memorize the three names together as a single historical set.

questions.question: When was the first Aeronautical Engineering licensure examination conducted?
questions.explanation:
The first Aeronautical Engineering licensure examination was conducted in July 1983 by the first Board of Aeronautical Engineering.

Successful examinees subsequently took their oath in November of the same year.

💡 Memory Hook:
July → Exam.
November → Oath.

🎯 Board Tip:
The two dates are easily confused. Remember the sequence:
First Board → April 1982
First Exam → July 1983
Oath Taking → November 1983

questions.question: When did successful examinees from the first Aeronautical Engineering licensure examination take their oath?
questions.explanation:
The successful examinees from the first Aeronautical Engineering licensure examination took their oath in November 1983, the same year that the first licensure examination was conducted.

The examination itself was conducted in July 1983.

💡 Memory Hook:
July = Test.
November = Oath.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question asks for the first licensure examination, answer July 1983. If it asks for the oath taking, answer November 1983.

questions.question: In what year was the SAEP renamed the Society of Aerospace Engineers of the Philippines and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission?
questions.explanation:
In March 1984, the SAEP was renamed the Society of Aerospace Engineers of the Philippines and was registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) with new Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws.

The organization was subsequently accredited by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) as the national professional organization of aeronautical engineers on April 30, 1984.

💡 Memory Hook:
1984 → Rename + SEC + PRC Accreditation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the March 1984 renaming/SEC registration with the April 30, 1984 PRC accreditation.

questions.question: When was the Society of Aerospace Engineers of the Philippines accredited by the PRC as the national professional organization of aeronautical engineers?
questions.explanation:
The Society of Aerospace Engineers of the Philippines was accredited by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) as the national professional organization of aeronautical engineers on April 30, 1984.

This followed its March 1984 renaming and registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

💡 Memory Hook:
March 1984 → Rename/SEC.
April 30, 1984 → PRC Accreditation.

🎯 Board Tip:
The exact date April 30, 1984 is a potential direct-recall board question.

questions.question: Which sequence BEST represents the historical development of the Philippine aeronautical engineering profession?
choices: RA 9497 → SAEP formation → PD 1570 → First Board → First Exam
SAEP formation → RA 776 → PD 1570 → First Board → First Licensure Exam
PD 1570 → SAEP formation → RA 776 → First Exam → First Board
First Board → SAEP formation → PD 1570 → RA 9497 → First Exam
questions.answerText: SAEP formation → RA 776 → PD 1570 → First Board → First Licensure Exam
questions.explanation:
The historical timeline gives the following sequence:

• April 28, 1950 → Formation of SAEP.
• June 20, 1952 → RA 776.
• June 11, 1978 → PD 1570.
• April 6, 1982 → First Board of Aeronautical Engineering.
• July 1983 → First licensure examination.
• November 1983 → First oath taking.
• March 1984 → SAEP renamed and registered with SEC.
• April 30, 1984 → PRC accreditation.
• March 4, 2008 → RA 9497.

💡 Memory Hook:
50 → 52 → 78 → 82 → 83 → 84 → 08.

🎯 Board Tip:
Timeline questions are excellent elimination questions. First identify which event belongs to which era, then arrange them chronologically.

questions.question: What is the official title of Republic Act No. 776?
choices: Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines
questions.answerText: Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines
questions.explanation:
Republic Act No. 776 is identified as the 'Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines.' It was approved on June 20, 1952.

The Act concerns the reorganization of the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) and the Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA), defines their powers and duties, makes certain adjustments involving funds and personnel, and regulates civil aeronautics.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 → Civil Aeronautics Act.

🎯 Board Tip:
Three major laws to keep distinct:
• RA 776 → Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines.
• PD 1570 → Philippine Aeronautical Decree.
• RA 9497 → Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008.

questions.question: When was Republic Act No. 776, the Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines, approved?
questions.explanation:
Republic Act No. 776, known as the Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines, was approved on June 20, 1952.

The Act is an important part of Philippine aviation law because it provided for the reorganization of the CAB and CAA, defined their powers and duties, and regulated civil aeronautics.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 → 20-06-1952.

🎯 Board Tip:
The date can be remembered as '062052' timeline.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose and scope of Republic Act No. 776?
choices: It establishes only the professional licensure requirements for aeronautical engineers.
It reorganizes the CAB and CAA, defines their powers and duties, makes certain adjustments involving funds and personnel, and regulates civil aeronautics.
It establishes the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines and abolishes the CAB.
It regulates only international air transportation between foreign countries.
questions.answerText: It reorganizes the CAB and CAA, defines their powers and duties, makes certain adjustments involving funds and personnel, and regulates civil aeronautics.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 has several purposes: reorganization of the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) and Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA), definition of their powers and duties, certain adjustments concerning funds and personnel, and regulation of civil aeronautics.

The Act therefore has a broader civil aviation regulatory scope than merely professional licensure.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 = Reorganize + Define Powers + Adjust + Regulate.

🎯 Board Tip:
If a choice says RA 776 created CAAP, eliminate it. CAAP is associated with RA 9497, the Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008.

questions.question: Which aircraft and airmen are generally excluded from the application of RA 776, except with respect to air traffic rules?
choices: Military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and foreign countries
All Philippine civil aircraft and airmen
All foreign civil aircraft and airmen
questions.answerText: Military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and foreign countries
questions.explanation:
RA 776 shall not apply to military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and of foreign countries, except with respect to air traffic rules.

This is an important distinction in the scope of the Civil Aeronautics Act.

💡 Memory Hook:
Military → Generally excluded.
Air Traffic Rules → Exception.

🎯 Board Tip:
Watch for the phrase 'except with respect to air traffic rules.' That exception is what makes the correct answer more precise than simply saying military aviation is completely excluded.

questions.question: Under RA 776, what is meant by 'air transportation'?
choices: Only the movement of passengers by aircraft.
Service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.
Only the movement of cargo between airports.
Navigation of aircraft exclusively for military purposes.
questions.answerText: Service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines air transportation as the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.

The definition is broad because it covers three major categories: persons, property, and mail.

💡 Memory Hook:
Air Transportation = People + Property + Mail.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a definition question gives a list of persons, property, and mail transported by aircraft, recognize it as 'air transportation.'

questions.question: Under RA 776, which term refers to a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width and designated or approved as suitable for air commerce or air transportation?
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines an airway as a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width on the surface of the earth and designated or approved by the Administrator as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.

Do not confuse an airway with a landing field. A landing field is a locality on land or water adapted for aircraft landing and takeoff.

💡 Memory Hook:
Airway = Air Path.
Landing Field = Landing Place.

🎯 Board Tip:
Definitions involving a 'path through navigable airspace' point directly to AIRWAY.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST identifies the principal regulatory function of the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB)?
choices: Regulating the technical airworthiness of aircraft and issuing airworthiness certificates.
Regulating the economic aspect of air transportation and exercising supervision and control over air carriers and related entities.
Licensing aeronautical engineers and administering their professional licensure examinations.
Investigating aircraft accidents and determining the airworthiness of damaged aircraft.
questions.answerText: Regulating the economic aspect of air transportation and exercising supervision and control over air carriers and related entities.
questions.explanation:
The CAB is primarily concerned with the ECONOMIC aspect of air transportation. It specifically gives the Board general supervision, regulation, and control over air carriers, general sales agents, cargo sales agents, and airfreight forwarders, including their property, property rights, equipment, facilities, and franchise.

This is an important distinction because CAB should not be confused with the authority responsible for technical aviation safety and airworthiness functions.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Airworthiness certification is not identified as the CAB's primary function in this section.
• Professional licensure belongs to the aeronautical engineering regulatory system.
• Accident investigation is not the economic regulatory function described for CAB.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = Commerce / Business side of aviation.

🎯 Board Tip:
When you see 'ECONOMIC ASPECT of air transportation,' immediately think CAB.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the entities specifically identified in the description of the CAB's general supervision, regulation, and control?
questions.explanation:
The CAB has general supervision, regulation, and control over air carriers, general sales agents, cargo sales agents, and airfreight forwarders, together with their property, property rights, equipment, facilities, and franchise.

Aeronautical engineering schools are not included in that specific list.

This is a classic EXCEPT/NOT question. Every choice except one belongs to the group specifically stated in the applicable material.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB → Carriers + Sales Agents + Forwarders.

🎯 Board Tip:
For 'NOT' questions, first identify the complete list from memory before looking for the odd choice.

questions.question: A domestic air carrier seeks authorization to engage in air transportation in the Philippines. Which instrument is the CAB authorized to issue for this purpose?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)
questions.answerText: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)
questions.explanation:
The CAB is authorized to issue Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) to domestic carriers.

The same material distinguishes this from the Foreign Air Carrier's Permit (FACP), which is associated with foreign carriers.

The question is deliberately testing the distinction between economic authorization and technical/operational certification.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• FACP is for foreign carriers.
• AOC is an operational certification and is not the CPCN identified in the CAB section.
• An Airworthiness Certificate concerns the airworthiness of an aircraft, not the CAB's economic authorization of a domestic carrier.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic → CPCN.
Foreign → FACP.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question says DOMESTIC CARRIER and asks what CAB issues, look for CPCN.

questions.question: Which pairing is CORRECT under the description of CAB-issued authorizations?
choices: Domestic carrier — Foreign Air Carrier's Permit (FACP)
Foreign carrier — Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) without presidential approval
Domestic carrier — Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)
questions.answerText: Domestic carrier — Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)
questions.explanation:
The CAB is authorized to issue CPCNs to domestic carriers and Foreign Air Carrier's Permits (FACP) to foreign carriers.

It further states that in the case of foreign air carriers, the CPCN shall be issued with the approval of the Philippine President.

Therefore, the domestic carrier → CPCN pairing is the only completely correct pairing among the choices.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN → Domestic.
FACP → Foreign.

🎯 Board Tip:
Be careful with choices that contain a familiar acronym but attach it to the wrong type of carrier.

questions.question: A foreign air carrier intends to obtain a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity under the applicable provisions. Whose approval is specifically required?
choices: The Chairman of the CAB alone
The Director General of CAAP alone
questions.explanation:
The applicable provision states that, in the case of FOREIGN AIR CARRIERS, the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) shall be issued with the approval of the Philippine President.

The question is testing a qualification attached specifically to foreign air carriers.

💡 Memory Hook:
Foreign CPCN → President's Approval.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not overlook the word 'foreign.' A question may present the general CPCN rule and then add this special requirement.

questions.question: Under the summary of RA 776, which statement BEST describes a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)?
choices: A certificate confirming that an aircraft meets applicable airworthiness requirements.
A permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.
A license issued exclusively to Filipino aeronautical engineers.
A permit authorizing only the operation of an aircraft for non-commercial purposes.
questions.answerText: A permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.
questions.explanation:
CPCN is a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity and describes it as a permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.

The wording is important: CPCN concerns authorization to engage in air commerce and/or transportation. It is not an aircraft airworthiness certificate.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN = Permission to ENGAGE in Air Commerce/Transportation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Watch the subject of the certificate. Airworthiness concerns the aircraft; CPCN concerns authorization to engage in air commerce and/or transportation.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the composition of the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) is CORRECT?
choices: The CAB is composed of five members, including a Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
The CAB is composed of seven members, all appointed by the President.
The CAB is composed of three members: a Chairman and two members.
The CAB is composed of five members, all drawn exclusively from the aeronautical engineering profession.
questions.answerText: The CAB is composed of five members, including a Chairman and Vice-Chairman.
questions.explanation:
The CAB has FIVE members. The Chairman is the DOTC Secretary or representative, while the Vice-Chairman is the Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation. The remaining members include the PAF Commanding General and two appointees.

The composition therefore cannot be reduced to three members, nor is the Board composed exclusively of aeronautical engineers.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = 5.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse CAB's five-member composition with the seven-member Board associated with CAAP under RA 9497.

questions.question: Which individual occupies the position of Vice-Chairman of the CAB?
choices: The Secretary of the DOTC or representative
The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
The Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force
questions.answerText: The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
questions.explanation:
The CAB composition identifies the DOTC Secretary or representative as Chairman and the Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation as Vice-Chairman.

The PAF Commanding General is listed as one of the members rather than the Vice-Chairman.

💡 Memory Hook:
Chairman → DOTC Secretary.
Vice-Chairman → Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Questions may deliberately place the PAF Commanding General in the Vice-Chairman position. Read the role, not merely the person's agency.

questions.question: A CAB meeting is being conducted under the quorum requirement stated. Which situation satisfies the minimum quorum?
choices: Two members are present, but neither the Chairman nor Vice-Chairman is present.
One member and the Chairman are present.
Two members and the Chairman are present.
questions.answerText: Two members and the Chairman are present.
questions.explanation:
The quorum of the CAB is TWO MEMBERS plus EITHER the Chairman OR the Vice-Chairman.

Therefore, two members together with the Chairman satisfy the stated requirement.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Two members without the Chairman or Vice-Chairman do not satisfy the requirement.
• One member plus the Chairman is insufficient because two members are required.
• The Chairman alone obviously does not satisfy the requirement.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB Quorum = 2 + C/VC.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'two members + either C or VC' is worth memorizing exactly. The Chairman or Vice-Chairman is NOT counted as one of the two required members in this wording.

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes the CAB's quorum requirement from a simple majority rule?
choices: Any two persons connected with the CAB automatically constitute a quorum.
The quorum specifically requires two members together with either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
The Chairman alone constitutes a quorum because he is the presiding officer.
The Vice-Chairman and one member always constitute a quorum.
questions.answerText: The quorum specifically requires two members together with either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
questions.explanation:
The applicable provision gives a specific quorum formula for the CAB: TWO MEMBERS + EITHER THE CHAIRMAN OR VICE-CHAIRMAN.

This is more precise than simply saying that a majority of the Board is required. The composition and required presence of the Chairman or Vice-Chairman are both relevant.

💡 Memory Hook:
Not just '2' → 2 Members + C/VC.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a law provides an exact quorum formula, memorize the formula rather than trying to infer it from the total number of Board members.

questions.question: A company does not operate aircraft itself but, under authority from an airline, sells or offers air transportation and arranges such transportation. Under the definitions, which term BEST describes this company?
questions.explanation:
A GENERAL SALES AGENT is a person who is not a bona fide employee of an air carrier and who, pursuant to authority from an airline, sells or offers for sale air transportation or negotiates for, advertises, provides, furnishes, contracts, or arranges for such transportation.

The key clue is that the activity involves air transportation generally and is performed pursuant to authority from an airline.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Cargo Sales Agent specifically deals with air transportation of CARGO.
• An Airfreight Forwarder is an indirect air carrier that assembles/consolidates property and utilizes a direct air carrier for all or part of the transportation.
• A Domestic Air Carrier is an air carrier that is a citizen of the Philippines.

💡 Memory Hook:
GSA = General Sales of Air transportation.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question emphasizes an agent selling or arranging air transportation under an airline's authority, think GSA.

questions.question: Which circumstance MOST clearly distinguishes a cargo sales agent from a general sales agent under the definitions?
choices: The cargo sales agent must directly operate the aircraft used for transportation.
The cargo sales agent deals specifically with the sale or arrangement of air transportation of cargo.
The cargo sales agent must be a bona fide employee of the air carrier.
The cargo sales agent is responsible for issuing airworthiness certificates.
questions.answerText: The cargo sales agent deals specifically with the sale or arrangement of air transportation of cargo.
questions.explanation:
A CARGO SALES AGENT is a person who does not directly operate an aircraft for air transportation or air commerce and who, as principal or agent, sells or offers for sale air transportation of CARGO or negotiates for, solicits, advertises, provides, furnishes, contracts, or arranges for such cargo transportation.

The word CARGO is the major distinction being tested.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• The definition specifically says the cargo sales agent does NOT directly operate the aircraft.
• The person is specifically described as not being a bona fide employee of an air carrier.
• Airworthiness certification is not the function described.

💡 Memory Hook:
Cargo Sales Agent = Sells the CARGO transportation, not the aircraft.

🎯 Board Tip:
GSA → air transportation generally.
Cargo Sales Agent → air transportation of cargo specifically.

questions.question: An entity receives property from customers, consolidates multiple shipments, performs break-bulk and distribution operations, and uses the services of a direct air carrier for all or part of the transportation. Which classification BEST fits the entity?
questions.explanation:
An AIRFREIGHT FORWARDER is an indirect air carrier that, in the ordinary course of its undertaking, assembles and consolidates property or provides for such consolidation, performs or provides for break-bulk and distribution operations involving consolidated shipments, and is responsible for transportation from the point of receipt to the point of destination while utilizing a direct air carrier for all or part of that transportation.

The critical clues are CONSOLIDATION, BREAK-BULK/DISTRIBUTION, and USE OF A DIRECT AIR CARRIER.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• A General Sales Agent sells or arranges air transportation pursuant to authority from an airline.
• A Cargo Sales Agent sells or arranges transportation specifically for cargo but does not fit the consolidation/direct-carrier relationship described here.
• A Domestic Air Carrier is an air carrier that is a Philippine citizen.

💡 Memory Hook:
Forwarder = Consolidate → Forward → Direct Carrier.

🎯 Board Tip:
When you see consolidation + break-bulk + direct air carrier, think AIRFREIGHT FORWARDER.

questions.question: Which CAB authorization is specifically associated with FOREIGN air carriers?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)
questions.explanation:
The CAB is authorized to issue a FOREIGN AIR CARRIER'S PERMIT (FACP) to foreign carriers.

It separately identifies CPCN as an authorization issued to domestic carriers and Letters of Authority for airfreight forwarders, general sales agents, and cargo sales agents.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic Carrier → CPCN.
Foreign Carrier → FACP.
Agents/Forwarders → Letter of Authority.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is exactly the kind of acronym-matching question where the choices are designed to make you second-guess yourself. Identify the type of entity FIRST, then identify the authorization.

questions.question: The CAB intends to authorize an airfreight forwarder, a general sales agent, and a cargo sales agent. Which instrument applies to these entities?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.explanation:
The CAB is authorized to issue LETTERS OF AUTHORITY to airfreight forwarders, general sales agents, and cargo sales agents.

This creates a useful three-way distinction:

• Domestic carriers → CPCN
• Foreign carriers → FACP
• Airfreight forwarders/GSA/cargo sales agents → Letters of Authority

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• CPCN is identified for domestic carriers.
• FACP is identified for foreign carriers.
• AOC is not the CAB authorization identified for these agents and forwarders in this section.

💡 Memory Hook:
Carrier → Certificate/Permit.
Agent → Authority.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question gives you the TYPE OF ENTITY, don't jump immediately to an acronym. Match entity → CAB authorization.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of CAB authorizations is CORRECTLY matched with the type of entity regulated?
choices: Domestic carrier — FACP; Foreign carrier — CPCN; Sales agent — Airworthiness Certificate
Domestic carrier — CPCN; Foreign carrier — FACP; Sales agents/forwarders — Letters of Authority
Domestic carrier — Letter of Authority; Foreign carrier — CPCN; Airfreight forwarder — FACP
Domestic carrier — AOC; Foreign carrier — Airworthiness Certificate; Sales agent — CPCN
questions.answerText: Domestic carrier — CPCN; Foreign carrier — FACP; Sales agents/forwarders — Letters of Authority
questions.explanation:
The applicable provisions establish three distinct CAB authorization relationships:

• CPCN → Domestic carriers.
• FACP → Foreign carriers.
• Letters of Authority → Airfreight forwarders, general sales agents, and cargo sales agents.

This question deliberately combines all three so that memorizing only one acronym is not enough.

💡 Master Memory Hook:
DOMESTIC = CPCN
FOREIGN = FACP
AGENTS/FORWARDERS = LOA

🎯 Board Tip:
When several regulatory instruments appear in the choices, classify the regulated entity first. This prevents acronym confusion.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the relationship between the CAB and the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) under RA 776?
choices: CAB is an attached agency of the DOTC.
CAB is an independent private organization affiliated with the DOTC.
CAB is a division of the Professional Regulation Commission.
CAB is a bureau directly under the Philippine Air Force.
questions.answerText: CAB is an attached agency of the DOTC.
questions.explanation:
The Civil Aeronautics Board is an ATTACHED AGENCY of the DOTC.

This is a structural classification and should not be confused with the CAB's separate regulatory role over the economic aspect of air transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB → Attached to DOTC.

🎯 Board Tip:
A question may combine organizational relationship with regulatory function. Keep the two concepts separate: DOTC attachment describes its organizational relationship; economic regulation describes its principal aviation function.

questions.question: Aside from its regulatory responsibilities, which additional function of the Civil Aeronautics Board is specifically identified?
choices: It conducts all aircraft maintenance inspections.
It issues professional licenses to aeronautical engineers.
It serves as the country's military aviation command.
questions.explanation:
The CAB performs QUASI-JUDICIAL FUNCTIONS.

This means the CAB is not merely an administrative body carrying out economic regulation; it also has functions of a judicial or adjudicatory nature within the authority granted to it.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Aircraft maintenance inspections are not identified as the CAB's function here.
• Aeronautical engineering professional licensing is not the CAB's role.
• Military aviation command is outside the described CAB function.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = Economic + Regulatory + Quasi-Judicial.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'quasi-judicial' is an easy point if you recognize it as a stated CAB function rather than assuming CAB is purely administrative.

questions.question: A Filipino-owned company wishes to operate as a domestic air carrier. Based strictly on the citizenship requirement stated, which statement is CORRECT?
choices: Domestic air commerce and transportation may be conducted by any foreign citizen with a CAB permit.
Domestic air commerce and transportation is restricted to Filipinos.
Only corporations with foreign ownership may conduct domestic air transportation.
Citizenship has no relevance to domestic air transportation under RA 776.
questions.answerText: Domestic air commerce and transportation is restricted to Filipinos.
questions.explanation:
The citizenship requirement states that DOMESTIC AIR COMMERCE AND/OR TRANSPORTATION is for FILIPINOS ONLY.

The definition section also identifies a domestic air carrier as an air carrier who is a citizen of the Philippines.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic → Filipino.

🎯 Board Tip:
Be especially careful when a question changes 'domestic air transportation' into 'international air transportation.' specifically attaches the Filipino-only requirement to DOMESTIC air commerce and/or transportation.

questions.question: Which individual or organization would MOST directly satisfy the definition of a 'domestic air carrier'?
choices: A foreign airline operating international flights to Manila.
A Philippine citizen acting as an air carrier.
A cargo sales agent arranging cargo transportation for an airline.
An airfreight forwarder consolidating shipments for a direct air carrier.
questions.answerText: A Philippine citizen acting as an air carrier.
questions.explanation:
A DOMESTIC AIR CARRIER is an air carrier who is a citizen of the Philippines.

The important point is that being involved in air transportation is not, by itself, enough. The definition combines the status of being an AIR CARRIER with Philippine citizenship.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• A foreign airline does not satisfy the stated domestic air carrier definition.
• A cargo sales agent is an intermediary and does not directly operate an aircraft for the relevant activity.
• An airfreight forwarder is an indirect air carrier with a specific consolidation function.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic Air Carrier = Air Carrier + Filipino.

🎯 Board Tip:
When definitions contain multiple elements, make sure the answer satisfies ALL of them—not just one.

questions.question: Under RA 776, which activity would MOST clearly fall under the definition of 'air commerce' even if no passenger or cargo is being transported for hire?
choices: Navigation of an aircraft solely for recreational flying with no business purpose.
Navigation of an aircraft in furtherance of a business.
Walking between two airport terminals to board an aircraft.
Maintenance of an aircraft that is permanently grounded.
questions.answerText: Navigation of an aircraft in furtherance of a business.
questions.explanation:
Under RA 776, AIR COMMERCE includes air transportation for pay or hire, the navigation of aircraft in furtherance of a business, or the navigation of aircraft from one place to another for operation in the conduct of a business.

The important trap is that air commerce is NOT limited to carrying passengers or cargo for compensation. Navigation of an aircraft in furtherance of a business is independently included.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• Recreational flying without a business purpose does not satisfy the stated business element.
• Walking between terminals is not aircraft navigation.
• Ground maintenance is not navigation of an aircraft.

💡 Memory Hook:
Air Commerce = Aircraft + Business.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not reduce 'air commerce' to 'carrying passengers for money.' several alternative activities that can fall within the definition.

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes 'air commerce' from 'air transportation' under the definitions provided in RA 776?
choices: Air commerce is limited to passenger carriage, while air transportation is limited to cargo.
Air commerce includes navigation in furtherance of business, while air transportation refers to the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail by aircraft.
Air commerce applies only to foreign operations, while air transportation applies only to domestic operations.
Air commerce concerns aircraft maintenance, while air transportation concerns aircraft registration.
questions.answerText: Air commerce includes navigation in furtherance of business, while air transportation refers to the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail by aircraft.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 gives related but distinct definitions. AIR TRANSPORTATION means the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft. AIR COMMERCE is broader in wording and includes air transportation for pay or hire as well as navigation of aircraft in furtherance of a business or for operation in the conduct of a business.

The key distinction is that air commerce can involve business-related aircraft navigation even beyond the simple carriage definition.

💡 Memory Hook:
Transportation = What is carried.
Commerce = Business involving aircraft.

🎯 Board Tip:
