When two legal definitions look similar, look for the extra element. Here, BUSINESS NAVIGATION is the important addition for air commerce.

questions.question: An aircraft carries passengers and mail on a scheduled flight. Which RA 776 definition is MOST directly describing the service being performed?
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines AIR TRANSPORTATION as the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.

The scenario specifically describes the carriage of passengers and mail by aircraft, directly matching this definition.

Air commerce is a broader concept that includes air transportation for pay or hire and other business-related aircraft navigation.

💡 Memory Hook:
Persons + Property + Mail → Air Transportation.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question focuses on what is being carried by aircraft, 'air transportation' is usually the key definition.

questions.question: Which of the following would qualify as an 'aircraft radio station' under the definition in RA 776?
choices: A radio station located inside an airport terminal.
A radio station installed on board an aircraft.
A ground-based radio station used to communicate with aircraft.
A radio station used exclusively for broadcasting aviation news.
questions.answerText: A radio station installed on board an aircraft.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines an AIRCRAFT RADIO STATION as a radio station on board any aircraft.

The phrase 'on board any aircraft' is the decisive clue.

💡 Memory Hook:
Aircraft Radio Station = Radio ON the Aircraft.

🎯 Board Tip:
Don't overthink this definition. The location of the radio station is the key distinguishing feature.

questions.question: An approved route through navigable airspace has a specified width on the Earth's surface and has been designated as suitable for air transportation. Under RA 776, what is this route called?
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines an AIRWAY as a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width on the surface of the Earth and designated or approved by the Administrator as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.

The key clues are:
• Path through navigable airspace.
• Specified width.
• Designated or approved by the Administrator.
• Suitable for air commerce or air transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
Airway = Approved Air Path.

🎯 Board Tip:
The word 'route' alone is not enough. Look for the legal definition involving navigable airspace and specified width.

questions.question: Which of the following entities would satisfy the definition of a 'citizen of the Philippines' for purposes of RA 776?
choices: A corporation organized under Philippine law in which only 40% of the voting interest is Philippine-owned.
A Philippine corporation whose directing head and two-thirds of its Board of Directors are Filipino citizens, with 60% of voting interest owned or controlled by Filipino citizens.
A foreign corporation with a Philippine branch office but without the required Filipino ownership.
A partnership in which only some of the partners are Filipino citizens.
questions.answerText: A Philippine corporation whose directing head and two-thirds of its Board of Directors are Filipino citizens, with 60% of voting interest owned or controlled by Filipino citizens.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 provides a specific definition of 'citizen of the Philippines.' For a corporation or association, it must be created or organized under Philippine law, its directing head and two-thirds or more of its Board of Directors and other managing officers must be Philippine citizens, and 60% of the voting interest must be owned or controlled by Philippine citizens.

The question is tricky because satisfying only ONE of these requirements is insufficient.

💡 Memory Hook:
Corporate Filipino Citizenship → Philippine organization + Filipino management + 60% voting interest.

🎯 Board Tip:
For definition questions involving citizenship, look for the answer that satisfies ALL stated elements, not merely Philippine incorporation.

questions.question: A partnership consists entirely of individual Filipino citizens. Based on the definition provided in RA 776, which statement is MOST accurate?
choices: It cannot qualify as a citizen of the Philippines because only corporations may qualify.
It qualifies as a citizen of the Philippines under the stated definition.
It qualifies only if at least 60% of its partners are Filipino citizens.
It qualifies only if two-thirds of its partners are Filipino citizens.
questions.answerText: It qualifies as a citizen of the Philippines under the stated definition.
questions.explanation:
A 'citizen of the Philippines' may include a partnership of which EACH MEMBER is an individual who is a citizen of the Philippines.

Notice the difference from the corporate requirement. The 60% voting-interest requirement belongs to the corporation or association criteria stated; it is not the test given for a partnership.

💡 Memory Hook:
Partnership → ALL partners Filipino.
Corporation → 60% voting interest + management requirements.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not automatically apply the corporation's 60% rule to every type of organization.

questions.question: Which person BEST fits the definition of a 'flight radio operator' under RA 776?
choices: Any passenger who operates a handheld radio during flight.
A member of the aircraft operating crew who has been granted a radio operator's license by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator to operate an aircraft radio station.
Any ground controller who communicates with aircraft.
Any aircraft mechanic who has experience with radio equipment.
questions.answerText: A member of the aircraft operating crew who has been granted a radio operator's license by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator to operate an aircraft radio station.
questions.explanation:
A FLIGHT RADIO OPERATOR is a member of the operating crew of an aircraft who is granted a radio operator's license by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator to operate an aircraft radio station.

Two elements are especially important:
1. The person is a member of the operating crew.
2. The person has the required radio operator's license.

💡 Memory Hook:
Flight Radio Operator = Crew + License + Aircraft Radio.

🎯 Board Tip:
Experience with radios is not enough. The definition specifically requires the person's operating-crew status and the license granted by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator.

questions.question: Which situation BEST satisfies the definition of a 'landing field' under RA 776?
choices: A major airport equipped with passenger terminals and maintenance hangars.
A locality on land or water adapted for aircraft landing and takeoff, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by that airway.
Any open field that can theoretically accommodate an aircraft regardless of its location.
A radio facility used by aircraft while approaching an airport.
questions.answerText: A locality on land or water adapted for aircraft landing and takeoff, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by that airway.
questions.explanation:
A LANDING FIELD is any locality on water or land adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by the airway.

Importantly, the definition states that this remains a landing field whether or not facilities are provided for shelter, servicing, repair, or receiving/discharging passengers or cargo.

💡 Memory Hook:
Landing Field = Land/Water + Landing/Takeoff + Along Airway.

🎯 Board Tip:
The presence of terminal or maintenance facilities is NOT the defining requirement. The location and adaptation for aircraft landing/takeoff are more important.

questions.question: A landing field has no facilities for aircraft shelter, servicing, repair, or handling passengers and cargo. Does this alone prevent it from being considered a 'landing field''s definition?
choices: Yes, because all landing fields must have aircraft maintenance facilities.
Yes, because passenger handling facilities are mandatory.
No, because the definition expressly allows a landing field to exist whether or not such facilities are provided.
No, but only if the field is located outside an airway.
questions.answerText: No, because the definition expressly allows a landing field to exist whether or not such facilities are provided.
questions.explanation:
A landing field may qualify whether or not facilities are provided for the shelter, servicing, or repair of aircraft, or for receiving or discharging passengers or cargo.

Therefore, the absence of these facilities does not by itself remove the locality from the definition.

💡 Memory Hook:
Landing Field ≠ Necessarily Full Airport Facilities.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic legal-definition trap: don't add requirements that the definition itself does not impose.

questions.question: Under RA 776, 'reasonable charges' are primarily intended to ensure what?
choices: The maximum possible profit for the operator of an air navigation facility.
A just and reasonable return on the capital invested, while considering specified costs and non-aeronautical revenue.
Uniform charges regardless of construction, operation, or maintenance costs.
Charges determined solely by the number of passengers carried.
questions.answerText: A just and reasonable return on the capital invested, while considering specified costs and non-aeronautical revenue.
questions.explanation:
REASONABLE CHARGES are those which ensure a just and reasonable return on the capital invested, taking into consideration the cost of construction, operation and maintenance and non-aeronautical revenue of the affected air navigation facility. The charges shall be uniform.

The important concept is BALANCE: the charge is not simply designed to maximize profit. It considers investment, costs, and non-aeronautical revenue while ensuring a just and reasonable return.

💡 Memory Hook:
Reasonable Charges = Reasonable Return + Relevant Costs + Non-aeronautical Revenue.

🎯 Board Tip:
The word 'maximum' is a red flag here. The provision says JUST AND REASONABLE return—not maximum profit.

questions.question: Which factor is specifically considered when determining 'reasonable charges' for an air navigation facility under the definition?
choices: The personal income of each passenger using the facility.
The cost of construction, operation and maintenance of the facility.
The nationality of every aircraft crew member.
The age of the aircraft using the facility.
questions.answerText: The cost of construction, operation and maintenance of the facility.
questions.explanation:
The definition specifically includes the cost of CONSTRUCTION, OPERATION, and MAINTENANCE when determining reasonable charges. It also mentions non-aeronautical revenue of the affected air navigation facility.

💡 Memory Hook:
COM = Construction + Operation + Maintenance.

🎯 Board Tip:
For definition questions involving charges, look for the economic factors explicitly listed in the source rather than choosing a generic aviation-related expense.

questions.question: Under RA 776, which person is MOST accurately described as an 'Administrator'?
choices: The Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications
The Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board
The Director General of the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines
questions.explanation:
Section 3 of RA 776 defines 'Administrator' as the Civil Aeronautics Administrator.

The important trap is that the term is a defined term in the Act. It should not automatically be interpreted as referring to the head of whichever aviation authority exists today.

Why the other choices are incorrect:
• The DOTC Secretary is identified separately in the CAB organizational structure.
• The CAB Chairman is a different position.
• The Director General belongs to the later CAAP framework established under RA 9497.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 → Administrator = Civil Aeronautics Administrator.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a statute explicitly defines a capitalized term, use the statutory definition rather than substituting a modern equivalent.

questions.question: Which statement is MOST consistent with the statutory definition of 'air commerce' under RA 776?
choices: It refers exclusively to the carriage of passengers for compensation.
It includes air transportation for pay or hire and certain navigation of aircraft conducted in furtherance of a business.
It refers exclusively to military navigation of aircraft between airports.
It applies only when both passengers and cargo are carried simultaneously.
questions.answerText: It includes air transportation for pay or hire and certain navigation of aircraft conducted in furtherance of a business.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines 'air commerce' broadly. It includes air transportation for pay or hire, navigation of aircraft in furtherance of a business, and navigation of aircraft from one place to another for operation in the conduct of a business.

The statutory definition therefore goes beyond passenger carriage. Business-related aircraft navigation may fall within air commerce even when the scenario does not simply describe passengers being transported for compensation.

💡 Memory Hook:
Air Commerce = Transportation + Business Navigation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Watch for the words 'in furtherance of a business.' They are a major clue that the statutory definition of air commerce is being tested.

questions.question: An aircraft is flown from one location to another specifically so that it may be used in conducting a business. Under RA 776, which classification BEST applies?
questions.explanation:
RA 776 expressly includes the navigation of aircraft from one place to another for operation in the conduct of a business within the definition of air commerce.

The aircraft does not have to be carrying passengers or cargo for the scenario to fall within this portion of the definition.

💡 Memory Hook:
Business Purpose + Aircraft Navigation = Air Commerce.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is the type of question where the examiner removes the obvious words 'pay or hire.' Look for the alternative statutory basis: navigation in furtherance of a business.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST satisfies the statutory definition of 'air transportation' under RA 776?
choices: The operation of an aircraft solely for maintenance testing.
The service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.
The designation of a route through navigable airspace.
The operation of a radio station aboard an aircraft.
questions.answerText: The service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines air transportation as the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.

The phrase 'in whole or in part' is important. The statutory definition does not require the aircraft to perform the entire transportation of the person, property, or mail.

💡 Memory Hook:
Air Transportation = Persons + Property + Mail.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the choice contains persons, property, or mail being carried by aircraft, it is probably targeting the statutory definition of air transportation.

questions.question: Which statement about the statutory definition of an 'airway' under RA 776 is CORRECT?
choices: Any visible aircraft flight path automatically constitutes an airway.
An airway is a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width and designated or approved as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.
An airway is any locality on land or water adapted for aircraft landing.
An airway refers exclusively to an aircraft's radio communication frequency.
questions.answerText: An airway is a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width and designated or approved as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines an airway as a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width on the surface of the Earth and designated or approved by the Administrator as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.

Several elements must be present in the definition: navigable airspace, specified width, and designation or approval for suitable air commerce or air transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
Airway = Navigable Airspace + Specified Width + Approved/Designated.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse an airway with a landing field. One describes a path through airspace; the other describes a locality adapted for landing and takeoff.

questions.question: A locality on land is suitable for aircraft landing and takeoff and is situated along an airway between airports connected by that airway. No facilities for shelter, servicing, repair, or passenger handling are provided. Under RA 776, which statement is MOST accurate?
choices: It cannot be a landing field because passenger facilities are mandatory.
It cannot be a landing field because maintenance facilities are mandatory.
It may still qualify as a landing field because such facilities are not required by the definition.
It automatically becomes an airport because it is located along an airway.
questions.answerText: It may still qualify as a landing field because such facilities are not required by the definition.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines a landing field as a locality on water or land adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by the airway. The definition expressly provides that this applies whether or not facilities are provided for shelter, servicing, or repair of aircraft, or for receiving or discharging passengers or cargo.

💡 Memory Hook:
Landing Field ≠ Full Facilities Required.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic statutory-wording trap. Do not add a requirement that the law expressly says is unnecessary.

questions.question: Which combination contains ONLY elements expressly associated with the RA 776 definition of a 'citizen of the Philippines' for a corporation or association?
choices: Philippine organization, Filipino directing head, at least two-thirds Filipino Board and managing officers, and 60% Filipino-controlled voting interest
Philippine organization, Filipino president only, and 51% Filipino voting interest
Foreign organization, Filipino majority of employees, and 60% Filipino customers
Philippine organization, one Filipino director, and 40% Filipino voting interest
questions.answerText: Philippine organization, Filipino directing head, at least two-thirds Filipino Board and managing officers, and 60% Filipino-controlled voting interest
questions.explanation:
For a corporation or association, RA 776's definition requires that it be created or organized under Philippine law; its directing head and two-thirds or more of its Board of Directors and other managing officers must be Philippine citizens; and 60% of the voting interest must be owned or controlled by Philippine citizens.

The key challenge is that the statutory definition contains MULTIPLE requirements. Meeting only the ownership requirement is not enough.

💡 Memory Hook:
Philippine Organization + Filipino Management + 60% Voting Interest.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a legal definition has several conditions connected together, treat them as a checklist. One missing element can make the choice incorrect.

questions.question: Under the definition of 'citizen of the Philippines' in RA 776, which partnership qualifies based on the stated criterion?
choices: A partnership in which every member is an individual who is a Philippine citizen
A partnership in which exactly 60% of the partners are Philippine citizens
A partnership in which the managing partner is Filipino regardless of the citizenship of the other partners
A partnership registered in the Philippines regardless of the citizenship of its members
questions.answerText: A partnership in which every member is an individual who is a Philippine citizen
questions.explanation:
RA 776 includes within its definition of 'citizen of the Philippines' a partnership of which EACH MEMBER is an individual who is a citizen of the Philippines.

This is distinct from the corporate or association requirements, which include the 60% voting-interest condition and Filipino management requirements.

💡 Memory Hook:
Partnership → Every Member Filipino.
Corporation → 60% Voting Interest + Filipino Management.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not transfer the corporation's requirements to partnerships. The statutory definition treats the organizational forms differently.

questions.question: Which person would NOT satisfy the complete statutory definition of a 'flight radio operator' under RA 776 merely by possessing extensive radio experience?
choices: A licensed member of an aircraft operating crew authorized to operate an aircraft radio station
A member of an aircraft operating crew who has been granted the required radio operator's license
A radio technician who is highly experienced but is neither a member of the aircraft operating crew nor granted the required radio operator's license
A member of the operating crew holding the required radio operator's license
questions.answerText: A radio technician who is highly experienced but is neither a member of the aircraft operating crew nor granted the required radio operator's license
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines a flight radio operator as a member of the operating crew of an aircraft who has been granted a radio operator's license by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator to operate an aircraft radio station.

Therefore, technical experience alone does not satisfy the complete definition. The statutory elements include operating-crew status and the required license.

💡 Memory Hook:
Flight Radio Operator = Crew + License.

🎯 Board Tip:
Legal definitions often contain multiple qualifying conditions. Experience, training, or job title alone may not be enough.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes 'reasonable charges' under the definition provided in RA 776?
choices: Charges calculated solely to maximize the operator's profit.
Charges intended to ensure a just and reasonable return on capital invested, considering specified costs and non-aeronautical revenue, and which shall be uniform.
Charges determined exclusively by passenger volume and aircraft weight.
Charges that may vary without restriction according to the preference of the facility operator.
questions.answerText: Charges intended to ensure a just and reasonable return on capital invested, considering specified costs and non-aeronautical revenue, and which shall be uniform.
questions.explanation:
RA 776 defines reasonable charges as those that ensure a just and reasonable return on the capital invested, taking into consideration the cost of construction, operation and maintenance and the non-aeronautical revenue of the affected air navigation facility. The definition further states that the charges shall be uniform.

The important trap is the difference between a JUST AND REASONABLE RETURN and maximum profit.

💡 Memory Hook:
Reasonable Charges = Reasonable Return + Costs + Non-aeronautical Revenue + Uniformity.

🎯 Board Tip:
Whenever you see 'maximum profit' in a choice, be suspicious. The statutory language is centered on a 'just and reasonable return.'

questions.question: How many members compose the Civil Aeronautics Board under Section 5 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 5 of RA 776 provides for a five-member Civil Aeronautics Board.

The composition includes:
• Chairman — Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications or his representative.
• Vice-Chairman — Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation.
• Member — Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force.
• Two additional members appointed as provided by the law.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = 5 members.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the five-member CAB with the later CAAP Board structure. A question may deliberately place the numbers side by side.

questions.question: Who serves as Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board under the composition provided in RA 776?
choices: The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
The Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force
The Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications or his representative
questions.answerText: The Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications or his representative
questions.explanation:
Under Section 5 of RA 776, the Chairman of the CAB is the Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications or his representative.

The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation serves as Vice-Chairman, while the Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force is one of the members.

💡 Memory Hook:
DOTC Secretary → Chairman.
Assistant Secretary → Vice-Chairman.
PAF Commanding General → Member.

🎯 Board Tip:
The choices are intentionally all high-level aviation/government positions. Focus on the POSITION assigned to the role.

questions.question: Who occupies the Vice-Chairman position of the CAB under Section 5 of RA 776?
choices: The Secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications
The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
The Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force
questions.answerText: The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
questions.explanation:
Section 5 identifies the Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation as the Vice-Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board.

The Chairman is the DOTC Secretary or representative, while the Commanding General of the Philippine Air Force is one of the Board members.

💡 Memory Hook:
Chairman = Secretary.
Vice-Chairman = Assistant Secretary.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic role-swapping trap. Several choices belong to the CAB composition, but only one is assigned to the Vice-Chairman position.

questions.question: Where is the principal office of the Civil Aeronautics Board located under Section 6 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 6 of RA 776 identifies METRO MANILA as the principal office of the Civil Aeronautics Board.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB → Principal Office → Metro Manila.

🎯 Board Tip:
Location questions are usually easy points, but be careful when the choices contain major Philippine aviation locations such as Clark or Cebu.

questions.question: How is a quorum of the Civil Aeronautics Board established under Section 6 of RA 776?
choices: By the presence of any two members.
By the presence of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman only.
By the presence of two members together with either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
By the presence of a simple majority of all five members regardless of who is present.
questions.answerText: By the presence of two members together with either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.
questions.explanation:
Section 6 provides that the quorum of the CAB consists of TWO MEMBERS plus EITHER THE CHAIRMAN OR THE VICE-CHAIRMAN.

This is more specific than simply saying 'a majority.' The statutory requirement identifies both the number of members and the required presence of either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB Quorum = 2 + C/VC.

🎯 Board Tip:
The examiner may offer 'three members' as a tempting answer. The number alone is not enough—the composition of those three matters.

questions.question: The Executive Director of the CAB is absent, as is the Deputy Executive Director. Who may designate an Officer-in-Charge under the provision summarized for Section 7?
questions.explanation:
Under the personnel provision summarized for Section 7, in the absence of both the Executive Director and Deputy Executive Director, the Chairman may designate an Officer-in-Charge.

💡 Memory Hook:
ED + DED absent → Chairman designates OIC.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a relationship question rather than a pure definition. Identify the two absent positions first, then determine who has the authority to act.

questions.question: What position is identified as the chief executive of the Civil Aeronautics Board?
questions.explanation:
The personnel provisions identify the EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR as the Chief Executive of the Board.

The Board Secretary has a different function: recording the proceedings of the Board and taking charge of and keeping its papers.

💡 Memory Hook:
Executive Director = Chief Executive.
Board Secretary = Records.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not assume that the Chairman is automatically the 'chief executive' simply because the Chairman presides over the Board.

questions.question: What is the principal responsibility of the Board Secretary identified in the personnel provisions of RA 776?
choices: To regulate the economic aspect of air transportation.
To record the proceedings of the Board and take charge of and keep its papers.
To serve as the Chief Executive of the Board.
questions.answerText: To record the proceedings of the Board and take charge of and keep its papers.
questions.explanation:
The Board Secretary is responsible for recording the proceedings of the Board and taking charge of and keeping its papers.

This function is administrative and records-oriented. It is distinct from the regulatory authority of the Board and from the executive role of the Executive Director.

💡 Memory Hook:
Board Secretary = Proceedings + Papers.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a question describes someone maintaining official Board records, think Board Secretary rather than Executive Director.

questions.question: What is the principal regulatory focus assigned to the CAB under Section 10 of RA 776?
choices: The economic aspect of air transportation
The professional practice of aeronautical engineering
The military use of Philippine airspace
The design certification of aircraft engines
questions.answerText: The economic aspect of air transportation
questions.explanation:
Section 10 identifies the regulation of the ECONOMIC ASPECT of air transportation as a principal power and duty of the CAB.

The same provision gives the CAB general supervision, regulation, and control over air carriers, general sales agents, cargo sales agents, and airfreight forwarders, including their property, property rights, equipment, facilities, and franchise.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = Economic Regulation.

🎯 Board Tip:
This distinction is extremely important throughout Part 1. If the question is centered on the economic regulation of air transportation, CAB should immediately come to mind.

questions.question: A foreign air carrier applies for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. What additional approval does Section 10 of RA 776 require for the issuance of the CPCN in this case?
choices: Approval of the Professional Regulation Commission
Approval of the Philippine Air Force Commanding General
questions.explanation:
Section 10 provides that, in the case of FOREIGN AIR CARRIERS, the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity shall be issued with the approval of the Philippine President.

The word 'foreign' is critical. The question is testing the additional requirement attached to this particular case.

💡 Memory Hook:
Foreign CPCN → Presidential Approval.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not memorize merely 'CAB issues CPCN.' Pay attention to the special condition attached to FOREIGN air carriers.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation CPCN stand for in the context of RA 776?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.answerText: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.explanation:
CPCN stands for CERTIFICATE OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY.

Section 11 describes it as a permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN = Public Convenience + Necessity.

🎯 Board Tip:
Acronym questions can become deceptively difficult when all four choices contain aviation-related words. Expand the acronym carefully rather than guessing from familiar terms.

questions.question: What does a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity authorize under Section 11 of RA 776?
choices: A person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.
An aircraft to operate without registration markings.
An aeronautical engineer to practice the profession without a license.
A military aircraft to conduct commercial air transportation.
questions.answerText: A person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.
questions.explanation:
Section 11 defines the CPCN as a permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, whether foreign and/or domestic.

The important point is that the CPCN is an authorization concerning engagement in air commerce and/or transportation. It is not an airworthiness certificate for the aircraft and not a professional license.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN → Authorization to ENGAGE in Air Commerce/Transportation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Watch the subject being authorized. The question is not asking whether the aircraft itself is airworthy.

questions.question: Under Section 12 of RA 776, who may engage in domestic air commerce and/or transportation?
questions.explanation:
Section 12 states that DOMESTIC AIR COMMERCE AND/OR TRANSPORTATION is for FILIPINOS ONLY.

This provision must be distinguished from the broader CPCN provision, which describes authorization to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic → Filipinos Only.

🎯 Board Tip:
The existence of a CPCN does not erase the citizenship requirement. Always check whether the question specifically concerns DOMESTIC air commerce or transportation.

questions.question: A foreign carrier possesses a CPCN but intends to engage in domestic air transportation within Philippine territory. Based on the provisions being tested, which conclusion is MOST appropriate?
choices: The carrier may automatically engage in domestic transportation because it possesses a CPCN.
The carrier may engage in domestic transportation because foreign carriers are exempt from citizenship requirements.
The domestic operation remains subject to the Filipino-only requirement stated in Section 12.
The carrier may operate domestically only if its aircraft is registered in another country.
questions.answerText: The domestic operation remains subject to the Filipino-only requirement stated in Section 12.
questions.explanation:
Section 12 states that domestic air commerce and/or transportation is for Filipinos only. Therefore, the mere possession of a CPCN does not by itself remove the separate citizenship requirement applicable to domestic air commerce and/or transportation.

This question deliberately combines Sections 11 and 12. Section 11 addresses what a CPCN authorizes; Section 12 imposes the citizenship requirement for domestic air commerce and/or transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN = Authorization.
Section 12 = Citizenship restriction.

🎯 Board Tip:
When two provisions appear to overlap, do not assume one automatically cancels the other. Read each requirement independently.

questions.question: What section of RA 776 specifically deals with the conduct of proceedings before the Civil Aeronautics Board?
questions.explanation:
Section 13 of RA 776 is titled 'Conduct of Proceedings.' It begins the series of provisions governing the CAB's proceedings and is followed by provisions dealing with delegation of authority to conduct hearings, applications for permits, notice, meetings, non-appearance, depositions, hearings and records, and issuance of permits.

💡 Memory Hook:
13 → Proceedings begin.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a section-number identification question. Keep the sequence 13–24 associated with CAB proceedings and permits.

questions.question: When may a permit issued by the Civil Aeronautics Board be transferred under Section 23 of RA 776?
choices: At any time, provided the original holder agrees.
Only after the permit has been in effect for 90 days.
Only with the prior approval of the Board.
Only after approval by the Philippine President.
questions.answerText: Only with the prior approval of the Board.
questions.explanation:
Section 23 of RA 776 provides that NO permit may be transferred WITHOUT THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE BOARD.

The word 'prior' is particularly important. Approval is not something that can simply be obtained after the transfer has already occurred.

💡 Memory Hook:
Transfer → Prior Board Approval.

🎯 Board Tip:
Whenever a law says 'without prior approval,' treat the timing of the approval as part of the requirement.

questions.question: A permit holder transfers its permit to another company first and plans to request CAB approval afterward. Is this consistent with Section 23 of RA 776?
choices: Yes, because Board approval is required only before renewal.
Yes, provided the new holder meets all operating requirements.
No, because the Board's approval must be obtained before the transfer.
No, because permits can never be transferred under any circumstance.
questions.answerText: No, because the Board's approval must be obtained before the transfer.
questions.explanation:
Section 23 expressly states that no permit may be transferred WITHOUT THE PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE BOARD.

The provision does not say that permits are absolutely non-transferable. Rather, it makes prior Board approval a condition for transfer.

💡 Memory Hook:
Transfer isn't forbidden → Transfer without PRIOR approval is forbidden.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic distinction between 'prohibited' and 'conditional.' Do not convert a requirement for prior approval into an absolute prohibition.

questions.question: When does a permit issued under Section 24 of RA 776 become effective?
choices: On the date specified in the permit.
Only after approval by the Civil Aeronautics Administrator.
questions.answerText: On the date specified in the permit.
questions.explanation:
Section 24 provides that a permit shall be effective FROM THE DATE SPECIFIED THEREIN.

It continues in effect until it is suspended or revoked, or until the Board certifies that the operation under the permit has ceased, subject to the other conditions stated in the section.

💡 Memory Hook:
Permit → Effective on its specified date.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not automatically assume that a permit becomes effective on the date it is issued. The statutory wording focuses on the date specified in the permit.

questions.question: How long may a permit remain effective when the operation authorized by it has not been suspended, revoked, or otherwise terminated under Section 24 of RA 776?
choices: It continues until suspended or revoked, or until the Board certifies that the operation has ceased, subject to the statutory conditions.
It automatically expires after 25 years regardless of the circumstances.
questions.answerText: It continues until suspended or revoked, or until the Board certifies that the operation has ceased, subject to the statutory conditions.
questions.explanation:
Section 24 states that a permit becomes effective on the date specified and shall continue in effect until suspended or revoked, or until the Board certifies that the operation thereunder has ceased.

However, this does not mean a permit may be issued for an unlimited initial term. The same section separately establishes a maximum period for which a permit may be issued.

💡 Memory Hook:
Continue → Until Suspension, Revocation, or Certified Cessation.

🎯 Board Tip:
Don't confuse 'how long a permit continues' with 'the maximum period for which a permit may be issued.' They are related but distinct provisions.

questions.question: What happens when a service authorized by a permit has not been inaugurated within 90 days, according to Section 24 of RA 776?
choices: The Board may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of that service.
The permit is automatically transferred to another carrier.
The service is automatically extended for another 90 days.
questions.answerText: The Board may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of that service.
questions.explanation:
Section 24 provides that if any service authorized by a permit is not inaugurated within a period of NINETY (90) DAYS, the Board may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of that service.

Notice the wording: the Board MAY DIRECT the permit to cease to be effective to the extent of the affected service. The provision is not phrased as an automatic transfer or automatic extension.

💡 Memory Hook:
90 Days → Service Not Started → Board may terminate that portion.

🎯 Board Tip:
The word 'may' matters. Do not automatically replace discretionary authority with an automatic consequence.

questions.question: How many years is the maximum period for which a permit may be issued under Section 24 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 24 provides that NO permit shall be issued for a period of more than TWENTY-FIVE (25) YEARS.

This is a maximum issuance period, not a statement that every permit automatically lasts 25 years.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 Permit Maximum = 25 years.

🎯 Board Tip:
Watch the wording: 'shall not be issued for a period of more than 25 years.' It does NOT mean every permit is valid for exactly 25 years.

questions.question: A CAB permit is issued for exactly 25 years. Based solely on the maximum-duration provision of Section 24, which statement is correct?
choices: The issuance exceeds the statutory maximum.
The issuance is within the stated maximum because the prohibition applies only to periods longer than 25 years.
The permit is automatically invalid because all permits must be shorter than 25 years.
The permit is valid only if it is transferred within the first 90 days.
questions.answerText: The issuance is within the stated maximum because the prohibition applies only to periods longer than 25 years.
questions.explanation:
Section 24 states that NO permit shall be issued for a period of MORE THAN 25 YEARS. Therefore, exactly 25 years does not exceed the stated maximum.

The trap is the difference between '25 years' and 'more than 25 years.'

💡 Memory Hook:
25 = Allowed maximum.
>25 = Not allowed.

🎯 Board Tip:
PRC-style legal questions often hinge on one word such as 'more than,' 'less than,' 'at least,' or 'not more than.' Read numerical limits literally.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly identifies Sections 21 through 24 of RA 776?
choices: Issuance of Permit → Modification, Suspension or Revocation → Transfer of Permit → Effective Date and Duration of Permit
Application for Permit → Notice → Hearings → Transfer of Permit
Issuance of Permit → Transfer of Permit → Modification → Annual Report
Hearings and Records → Issuance of Permit → Annual Report → Duration of Permit
questions.answerText: Issuance of Permit → Modification, Suspension or Revocation → Transfer of Permit → Effective Date and Duration of Permit
questions.explanation:
The sequence of Sections 21–24 is:

• Section 21 — Issuance of Permit
• Section 22 — Modification, Suspension or Revocation
• Section 23 — Transfer of Permit
• Section 24 — Effective Date and Duration of Permit

💡 Memory Hook:
21 Issue → 22 Change/Stop → 23 Transfer → 24 Duration.

🎯 Board Tip:
Section-sequence questions are particularly useful because they test whether you understand the structure of the law rather than memorizing isolated provisions.

questions.question: What is the main subject of Section 22 of RA 776?
choices: The modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit
The composition of the Civil Aeronautics Board
The citizenship requirement for domestic air commerce
The annual report of the Board
questions.answerText: The modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit
questions.explanation:
Section 22 addresses MODIFICATION, SUSPENSION OR REVOCATION of a permit.

It follows Section 21, which concerns issuance of a permit, and precedes Section 23, which concerns transfer of a permit.

💡 Memory Hook:
21 = Issue.
22 = Modify/Suspend/Revoke.
23 = Transfer.
24 = Duration.

🎯 Board Tip:
The neighboring section numbers are easy to scramble. Memorizing the logical sequence makes these questions much easier.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 20 of RA 776?
choices: Delegation of authority to conduct hearings
questions.explanation:
Section 20 is titled 'Hearings and Records of Proceedings.' It comes immediately before Section 21, 'Issuance of Permit.'

The preceding provisions address conduct of proceedings, delegation of authority, application, notice, meetings, non-appearance, and deposition.

💡 Memory Hook:
20 → Hearings & Records.
21 → Permit Issuance.

🎯 Board Tip:
Use the progression of the procedure as a memory aid: proceedings → hearings/records → permit issuance → modification/transfer/duration.

questions.question: When a permit is involved, which action specifically requires the PRIOR approval of the Civil Aeronautics Board?
choices: Its initial existence as a legal document
questions.explanation:
Section 23 specifically provides that no permit may be transferred without the PRIOR APPROVAL of the Board.

This is narrower than saying that every action involving a permit requires prior Board approval under Section 23. The section specifically addresses TRANSFER.

💡 Memory Hook:
Section 23 = Transfer → Prior Approval.

🎯 Board Tip:
Avoid broadening a legal provision beyond its actual subject. If the question asks what Section 23 specifically controls, the answer is transfer.

questions.question: Under Section 25 of Republic Act No. 776, how is the Civil Aeronautics Administration organized?
choices: It is composed of a Board of five members and a Secretary
It is composed of one Chief, designated as Administrator, and one Deputy Chief, designated as Deputy Administrator
It is composed exclusively of the Civil Aeronautics Board and its technical divisions
It is composed of the President, Administrator, and representatives of the armed forces
questions.answerText: It is composed of one Chief, designated as Administrator, and one Deputy Chief, designated as Deputy Administrator
questions.explanation:
Section 25 deals specifically with the organization of the Civil Aeronautics Administration.

• The Administration is composed of one Chief, who is the Administrator.
• It also has one Deputy Chief, who is the Deputy Administrator.

Do not confuse this with the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB), which is a separate body with its own composition and functions.

Memory hook: CAA = Chief + Deputy Chief.

Board tip: A question may deliberately mix the composition of the CAB with that of the CAA. Keep the two organizations distinct.

questions.question: Where was the Civil Aeronautics Administration placed organizationally under Section 25 of RA 776?
choices: Under the Department of National Defense
Under the Department of Public Works and Communications
Under the Department of Commerce and Industry
questions.answerText: Under the Department of Commerce and Industry
questions.explanation:
Section 25 places the Civil Aeronautics Administration under the Department of Commerce and Industry.

This is a historical provision of RA 776. The important board-exam distinction is that the question concerns the organizational arrangement established by the statute at the time it was enacted.

Memory hook: Section 25 → CAA organization → Department of Commerce and Industry.

Board tip: Do not automatically substitute the modern government department structure when a question specifically asks about the original statutory provision of RA 776.

questions.question: Who is designated as the Chief of the Civil Aeronautics Administration under Section 25 of RA 776?
choices: The Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board
The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
questions.explanation:
Section 25 identifies the Chief of the Civil Aeronautics Administration as the Administrator.

The Deputy Chief is separately designated as the Deputy Administrator.

This creates a simple hierarchy:
• Chief → Administrator
• Deputy Chief → Deputy Administrator

Board tip: A common trap is to reverse the titles or confuse the Administrator of the CAA with the Chairman of the CAB.

questions.question: Under Section 26 of RA 776, who appoints the Civil Aeronautics Administrator?
choices: The Civil Aeronautics Board without presidential participation
The Secretary of Commerce and Industry alone
The President of the Philippines, with the consent of the Commission on Appointments
questions.answerText: The President of the Philippines, with the consent of the Commission on Appointments
questions.explanation:
Section 26 provides that the Civil Aeronautics Administrator is appointed by the President of the Philippines with the consent of the Commission on Appointments.

The trap is in the distinction between appointment and consent:
• The President makes the appointment.
• The Commission on Appointments gives its consent.

Memory hook: President appoints; Commission on Appointments consents.

Board tip: If an option says that the Commission on Appointments 'appoints' the Administrator, that reverses the roles.

questions.question: What is the principal administrative responsibility expressly assigned to the Civil Aeronautics Administrator under Section 26 of RA 776?
choices: To regulate only the economic aspect of air transportation
To administer all laws relating to civil aviation in the Philippines
To appoint all members of the Civil Aeronautics Board
To issue all Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.answerText: To administer all laws relating to civil aviation in the Philippines
questions.explanation:
Section 26 assigns the Civil Aeronautics Administrator the responsibility of administering all laws relating to civil aviation in the Philippines.

Do not confuse this with the economic regulatory functions assigned to the Civil Aeronautics Board.

The distinction is important:
• Administrator/CAA → administration of civil aviation laws and related administrative responsibilities.
• CAB → economic regulation and supervision of air carriers and related entities under its statutory authority.

Board tip: Questions may place a CAB function into an Administrator option to make the choices look plausible.

questions.question: When is the Civil Aeronautics Administrator required to submit reports concerning the activities and transactions of his office?
choices: Only when specifically ordered by the Supreme Court
Annually or as often as may be required by the head of the Department
Only once during the Administrator's entire term
Every five years regardless of circumstances
questions.answerText: Annually or as often as may be required by the head of the Department
questions.explanation:
Section 26 requires the Administrator to submit written reports concerning the activities and transactions of his office annually, or as often as may be required by the head of the Department.

The phrase 'annually or as often as may be required' is the important part.

It means the annual report is not the only possible reporting interval; additional reports may be required.

Board trap: 'Annually only' is incomplete because the law allows reports to be required more frequently.

questions.question: Who serves as the Deputy Chief of the Civil Aeronautics Administration under Section 25 of RA 776?
choices: The Executive Director of the CAB
The Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
questions.explanation:
Section 25 establishes the basic two-level organization of the Civil Aeronautics Administration:

• Chief → Administrator
• Deputy Chief → Deputy Administrator

The Executive Director and Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation belong to different organizational contexts and should not be substituted for the Deputy Administrator.

Memory hook: Administrator heads; Deputy Administrator assists as Deputy Chief.

questions.question: Under Section 27 of RA 776, who appoints the Deputy Administrator?
choices: The President of the Philippines with the consent of the Commission on Appointments
The Civil Aeronautics Administrator without further approval
The Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board
The Secretary of Commerce and Industry alone
questions.answerText: The President of the Philippines with the consent of the Commission on Appointments
questions.explanation:
Section 27 provides for the appointment of the Deputy Administrator by the President with the consent of the Commission on Appointments.

This mirrors the appointment arrangement stated for the Administrator in Section 26.

Board tip: The question may test whether you remember that both positions involve presidential appointment and Commission on Appointments consent rather than having the Administrator appoint the Deputy Administrator himself.

questions.question: What subject is addressed by Section 28 of RA 776?
choices: Authority of CAA officers to administer oaths
Appointment of members of the Civil Aeronautics Board
Issuance of Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.answerText: Authority of CAA officers to administer oaths
questions.explanation:
Section 28 is entitled 'Authority of the Officers of the Civil Aeronautics Administration to Administer Oaths.'

This is a section-identification question, but the distractors are intentionally drawn from nearby provisions of RA 776.

Memory hook:
25 → Organization
26 → Administrator
27 → Deputy Administrator
28 → Oaths

Board tip: Memorizing the sequence of sections can help when the examination gives only a short description and asks for the corresponding section.

questions.question: Which section of RA 776 specifically concerns the permanent divisions of the Civil Aeronautics Administration?
questions.explanation:
Section 29 is entitled 'Permanent Divisions.'

The neighboring sections are deliberately useful distractors:
• Section 27 → Deputy Administrator
• Section 28 → authority of CAA officers to administer oaths
• Section 29 → Permanent Divisions
• Section 31 → Temporary Personnel

Memory hook: 28 = Oaths → 29 = Permanent Divisions → 30 = Officials and Employees → 31 = Temporary Personnel.

questions.question: A board examinee is asked to distinguish Sections 29, 30, and 31 of RA 776. Which sequence is correctly matched?
choices: Section 29 – Temporary Personnel; Section 30 – Permanent Divisions; Section 31 – Officials and Employees
Section 29 – Permanent Divisions; Section 30 – Officials and Employees; Section 31 – Temporary Personnel
Section 29 – Officials and Employees; Section 30 – Temporary Personnel; Section 31 – Permanent Divisions
Section 29 – Administrator; Section 30 – Deputy Administrator; Section 31 – Oath-taking authority
questions.answerText: Section 29 – Permanent Divisions; Section 30 – Officials and Employees; Section 31 – Temporary Personnel
questions.explanation:
The correct sequence is:

• Section 29 → Permanent Divisions
• Section 30 → Officials and Employees
• Section 31 → Temporary Personnel

This is exactly the kind of neighboring-section distinction that can appear as a tricky board question.

Memory hook: Permanent → Officials → Temporary = 29 → 30 → 31.

Board tip: When several consecutive sections concern personnel and organization, do not memorize them as one block. Associate one keyword with each section number.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the title of a section appearing between Sections 25 and 32 of RA 776?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.answerText: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.explanation:
Sections 25 through 32 deal with the organization and administration of the Civil Aeronautics Administration and its officers.

The sequence includes:
• Section 25 – Organization of the Civil Aeronautics Administration
• Section 26 – The Civil Aeronautics Administrator
• Section 27 – The Deputy Administrator
• Section 28 – Authority of CAA officers to administer oaths
• Section 29 – Permanent Divisions
• Section 30 – Officials and Employees
• Section 31 – Temporary Personnel
• Section 32 – Powers and Duties of the Administrator

A Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity belongs to the provisions dealing with the Civil Aeronautics Board and permits, not this sequence.

Board tip: This is a 'NOT' question, so read every option as though it could be correct before eliminating the one that belongs to another portion of the Act.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 32 of RA 776?
choices: Powers and Duties of the Administrator
Powers and Duties of the Civil Aeronautics Board
questions.answerText: Powers and Duties of the Administrator
questions.explanation:
Section 32 is entitled 'Powers and Duties of the Administrator.'

This is an important transition in RA 776:

Sections 25–31 establish the organization, Administrator, Deputy Administrator, oath-taking authority, divisions, and personnel; Section 32 then moves into the substantive powers and duties of the Administrator.

Board tip: Do not confuse Section 32 with the CAB's powers under Section 10. Both involve aviation authority, but they belong to different statutory bodies.

questions.question: Under Section 32 of RA 776, what term refers to charges for the use of a landing strip or runway by an aircraft landing or taking off at an aerodrome?
questions.explanation:
Section 32 identifies landing fees as charges for the use of any landing strip or runway by an aircraft landing or taking off at an aerodrome.

Do not confuse this with terminal fees:
• Landing fees → use of a landing strip or runway.
• Terminal fees → charges associated with parking at or near the ramp, terminal area, or building for loading or unloading passengers or cargo.

Memory hook: Landing = runway use; Terminal = terminal/ramp parking and loading activity.

Board tip: 'Reasonable charges' is another defined term in RA 776, but it is broader and should not be substituted for the specific term 'landing fees.'

questions.question: An aircraft is charged specifically for the use of a runway while landing at an aerodrome. Under the terminology used in RA 776, what type of charge is involved?
questions.explanation:
A charge imposed for the use of a landing strip or runway by an aircraft landing or taking off is a landing fee under the terminology presented for Section 32 of RA 776.

The important clue is the phrase 'use of the landing strip or runway.'

Do not be distracted by the fact that the aircraft may also use terminal facilities. The charge described in the question is specifically tied to the runway operation.

Board tip: Look for the object of the charge. Runway → landing fee; terminal/ramp parking and loading area → terminal fee.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 33 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 33 is entitled Annual Report.

The neighboring provisions are easy to confuse:
• Section 33 → Annual Report
• Section 34 → Eligibility for Registration
• Section 35 → Application for Aircraft Registration
• Section 36 → Issuance of Certificate of Registration

Board tip: When the question asks for a section number, pay attention to whether it is asking about the requirement, the application, or the actual issuance of the certificate.

questions.question: Under Section 34 of RA 776, what is the primary subject being determined before an aircraft may qualify for registration?
questions.explanation:
Section 34 deals with Eligibility for Registration.

This section should be distinguished from Section 35, which deals with the application for aircraft registration, and Section 36, which concerns issuance of the Certificate of Registration.

Think of the sequence as:
34 → Can it qualify?
35 → Application
36 → Certificate issued
37 → Revocation

Memory hook: Eligibility comes before Application, and Application comes before Issuance.

questions.question: According to the supplied RA 776 material, which ownership status qualifies an aircraft for Philippine registration under Section 34?
choices: An aircraft owned exclusively by foreign nationals
Any aircraft temporarily located in the Philippines
Any aircraft operated by a Philippine-based company regardless of ownership
questions.explanation:
The supplied material summarizes Section 34 as requiring that only aircraft owned by Filipinos can be registered under the provision.

It also specifically notes 'No dual citizenship' in connection with the registration eligibility material.

Board tip: Do not confuse ownership eligibility under this historical RA 776 provision with the broader registration eligibility rules found in later aviation regulations. If a question specifies RA 776 Section 34, answer within that statutory framework.

questions.question: A foreign-owned aircraft is operated regularly by a Philippine company. Under the Section 34 summary in the supplied RA 776 material, which factor is decisive for registration eligibility?
choices: The location of the aircraft's principal airport
The nationality of the aircraft manufacturer
questions.explanation:
The supplied material specifically summarizes Section 34 with the statement that only aircraft owned by Filipinos can be registered.

Therefore, merely operating an aircraft in the Philippines or having a Philippine-based operator does not, by itself, satisfy the ownership condition described in this provision.

Board trap: 'Operated in the Philippines' and 'owned by Filipinos' are not interchangeable concepts.

questions.question: What document serves as evidence of nationality for international purposes and as evidence of ownership under the supplied Section 34 material?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.explanation:
The supplied material identifies the Certificate of Registration as:

• evidence of nationality for international purposes; and
• evidence of ownership.

Do not confuse this with an airworthiness certificate. An airworthiness certificate concerns the aircraft's airworthiness status, whereas the Certificate of Registration establishes the registration-related nationality and ownership evidence described here.

Board tip: Registration ≠ airworthiness. They establish different legal facts.

questions.question: Which section of RA 776 specifically addresses the application for aircraft registration?
questions.explanation:
Section 35 is 'Application for Aircraft Registration.'

The distinction is important:
• Section 34 → Eligibility for Registration
• Section 35 → Application for Aircraft Registration
• Section 36 → Issuance of Certificate of Registration
• Section 37 → Revocation

A board question may intentionally provide the correct concept but ask for the section number.

questions.question: An aircraft satisfies the ownership requirement but has not yet undergone the registration application process. Which section primarily governs the next step?
questions.explanation:
Once the issue is no longer whether the aircraft is eligible but concerns the application for registration, Section 35 becomes the relevant provision.

The sequence matters:
1. Section 34 — eligibility
2. Section 35 — application
3. Section 36 — issuance
4. Section 37 — revocation

Board tip: This is a classic process-sequence question. Do not jump directly from eligibility to issuance.

questions.question: When is the Certificate of Registration addressed under RA 776's aircraft-registration provisions?
questions.explanation:
Section 36 is entitled 'Issuance of Certificate of Registration.'

This follows the application provision in Section 35.

Sequence:
Section 34 → Eligibility
Section 35 → Application
Section 36 → Issuance
Section 37 → Revocation

Memory hook: E-A-I-R = Eligibility → Application → Issuance → Revocation.

questions.question: A Certificate of Registration has already been issued. Later, a circumstance arises that makes the aircraft ineligible for registration. What action is specifically contemplated by Section 37 of RA 776?
choices: Revocation of the Certificate of Registration
Issuance of an Air Operator Certificate
questions.answerText: Revocation of the Certificate of Registration
questions.explanation:
Section 37 concerns Revocation. The supplied material states that any Certificate of Registration may be revoked for any cause that renders the aircraft ineligible for registration.

The key trigger is not simply that the aircraft exists or changes location; it is a cause that renders the aircraft ineligible for registration.

Board tip: Watch the direction of causation: ineligibility can be a basis for revocation.

questions.question: Under Section 37 of RA 776, which circumstance may serve as a basis for revocation of a Certificate of Registration?
choices: Any cause that renders the aircraft ineligible for registration
A temporary change in flight route
questions.answerText: Any cause that renders the aircraft ineligible for registration
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 37 material expressly states that a Certificate of Registration may be revoked for any cause which renders the aircraft ineligible for registration.

The phrase 'renders the aircraft ineligible' is the important legal trigger.

Board trap: The other choices may relate to aircraft operations but do not express the specific revocation basis identified in the supplied material.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 38 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 38 is entitled 'Conveyance to Be Recorded.'

The following sections continue the recording provisions:
• Section 38 → Conveyance to Be Recorded
• Section 39 → Form of Conveyance
• Section 40 → Method of Recording
• Section 41 → Previously Unrecorded Ownership

Board tip: Sections 38–41 form a logical block dealing with recording ownership-related conveyances.

questions.question: Which section comes immediately after 'Conveyance to Be Recorded' in RA 776?
choices: Section 36 — Issuance of Certificate of Registration
questions.explanation:
Section 38 addresses the conveyance to be recorded, while Section 39 addresses its form.

This is deliberately simple in concept but tricky in sequence because Sections 38–41 are closely related.

Sequence:
38 → What conveyance is recorded
39 → Form of conveyance
40 → Method of recording
41 → Previously unrecorded ownership.

questions.question: What does Section 39 of RA 776 address?
choices: The eligibility of an aircraft for registration
The revocation of a Certificate of Registration
questions.explanation:
Section 39 is entitled 'Form of Conveyance.'

It follows Section 38, 'Conveyance to Be Recorded,' and precedes Section 40, 'Method of Recording.'

Memory hook: 38 = What is recorded; 39 = Form; 40 = Method; 41 = Previously unrecorded ownership.

questions.question: An examiner asks for the section dealing with the method by which a conveyance is recorded. What is the correct section of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 40 is entitled 'Method of Recording.'

This should not be confused with:
• Section 38 — Conveyance to Be Recorded
• Section 39 — Form of Conveyance
• Section 41 — Previously Unrecorded Ownership.

Board tip: 'Form' and 'Method' are deliberately close concepts. Form asks what the conveyance should look like; method concerns how recording is accomplished.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 41 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 41 addresses Previously Unrecorded Ownership.

This completes the sequence of provisions dealing with recording:
38 → Conveyance to Be Recorded
39 → Form of Conveyance
40 → Method of Recording
41 → Previously Unrecorded Ownership

Board tip: Section 41 is easy to confuse with Section 38 because both involve ownership/recording concepts, but their titles are different.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly arranges Sections 38 through 41 of RA 776?
choices: Form of Conveyance → Conveyance to Be Recorded → Method of Recording → Revocation
Conveyance to Be Recorded → Form of Conveyance → Method of Recording → Previously Unrecorded Ownership
Method of Recording → Form of Conveyance → Previously Unrecorded Ownership → Conveyance to Be Recorded
Previously Unrecorded Ownership → Method of Recording → Form of Conveyance → Conveyance to Be Recorded
questions.answerText: Conveyance to Be Recorded → Form of Conveyance → Method of Recording → Previously Unrecorded Ownership
questions.explanation:
The correct statutory sequence is:

• Section 38 — Conveyance to Be Recorded
• Section 39 — Form of Conveyance
• Section 40 — Method of Recording
• Section 41 — Previously Unrecorded Ownership

This is a useful sequence to memorize because the four sections form one continuous subject area.

Memory hook: RECORD → FORM → METHOD → OLD OWNERSHIP.

questions.question: What type of violation is specifically covered by the penalties in Section 42 of RA 776?
choices: Engaging in air commerce without a CPCN
Failing to renew a driver's license
Operating a foreign airline without an ICAO membership
Failing to display a runway number
questions.answerText: Engaging in air commerce without a CPCN
questions.explanation:
Section 42 is entitled 'Specific Penalties.' The supplied material specifically identifies engaging in air commerce without a CPCN as one of the violations subject to the penalties stated in that section.

The same material also identifies other violations, including operating a civil aircraft in violation of regulations relating to aeronautical safety standards and interference with air navigation.

Board tip: Do not confuse Section 42's specific penalties with Section 43's general penalty.

questions.question: A person engages in air commerce without first obtaining the required CPCN. Under the supplied RA 776 material, which provision specifically addresses the penalty for this violation?
questions.explanation:
Section 42 is the specific-penalty provision identified for persons engaging in air commerce without a CPCN.

This is different from Section 43, which is identified as the General Penalty provision.

Board trap: The fact that both Sections 42 and 43 involve penalties does not make them interchangeable. Section 42 contains specified violations and their corresponding penalties, while Section 43 provides the general penalty.

questions.question: Under the supplied Section 42 material, which of the following is included among the specifically penalized violations?
choices: Failure to file a flight plan for every domestic flight
Failure to join a recognized aviation organization
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 42 material expressly identifies interference with air navigation among the violations carrying specific penalties.

It also lists:
• engaging in air commerce without a CPCN; and
• operating a civil aircraft in violation of regulations relating to aeronautical safety standards.

Board tip: The word 'specific' matters. Section 42 identifies particular violations rather than merely stating a catch-all penalty.

questions.question: According to the supplied Section 42 material, what is the stated maximum fine for a person engaging in air commerce without a CPCN, or committing the other specifically listed violations?
questions.explanation:
The supplied reviewer material summarizes the Section 42 penalty for the specifically listed violations as a fine not exceeding ₱5,000 or imprisonment for less than one year, or both.

The listed violations include:
• engaging in air commerce without a CPCN;
• operating a civil aircraft in violation of regulations relating to aeronautical safety standards; and
• interference with air navigation.

Board tip: Do not confuse this ₱5,000 ceiling with the ₱500 general penalty identified under Section 43.

questions.question: How does the penalty described in Section 42 differ from the general penalty described in Section 43 of the supplied RA 776 material?
choices: Section 42 has a ₱5,000 maximum for specified violations, while Section 43 states a general fine not exceeding ₱500 for each violation
Section 42 has a ₱500 maximum, while Section 43 has a ₱5,000 maximum
Both sections impose exactly the same fine
Section 42 imposes imprisonment only, while Section 43 imposes a fine only
questions.answerText: Section 42 has a ₱5,000 maximum for specified violations, while Section 43 states a general fine not exceeding ₱500 for each violation
questions.explanation:
The supplied material distinguishes the two provisions:

• Section 42 → Specific Penalties, including a fine not exceeding ₱5,000 or imprisonment for less than one year, or both, for the specifically listed violations.
• Section 43 → General Penalty, with a fine not exceeding ₱500 for each violation.

This is a classic numerical trap because both provisions deal with penalties but have very different stated amounts.

Board tip: Remember 42 = specific/higher penalty; 43 = general/₱500.

questions.question: An air carrier violates a provision of RA 776 and the violation continues for several days. Under the supplied Section 42 material, what additional daily penalty may apply?
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 42 material states that an air carrier or person who violates or fails to comply with a provision of the Act may be subject to a fine not exceeding ₱5,000 per violation, with an additional fine not exceeding ₱200 per day for every day during which the default or violation continues.

The key phrase is 'for every day' the violation continues.

Board trap: Do not confuse the ₱200 daily amount with the ₱5,000 maximum fine for the violation itself.

questions.question: A continuing violation is discovered on Monday and remains uncorrected for several days. Which feature of the Section 42 penalty is most relevant?
choices: Only one fine can ever be imposed regardless of how long the violation continues
An additional fine not exceeding ₱200 per day may apply while the default or violation continues
The fine automatically becomes a criminal penalty after 24 hours
The penalty disappears if the aircraft leaves Philippine airspace
questions.answerText: An additional fine not exceeding ₱200 per day may apply while the default or violation continues
questions.explanation:
The supplied material expressly provides an additional daily fine not exceeding ₱200 for every day during which the default or violation continues.

This makes the duration of the violation legally relevant to the amount of the penalty.

Board tip: When you see 'continues' or 'every day during which,' look for a daily or continuing penalty provision.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 43 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 43 is entitled General Penalty.

This follows Section 42, which deals with Specific Penalties, and precedes Section 44, Compromise Regarding Penalty.

Memory sequence:
42 → Specific Penalties
43 → General Penalty
44 → Compromise
45 → Enforcement

Board tip: The distinction between Sections 42 and 43 is important because Section 42 identifies particular violations and Section 43 provides the general penalty.

questions.question: Under the supplied RA 776 material, what is the general fine prescribed under Section 43 for each violation?
questions.explanation:
Section 43 is identified as the General Penalty provision, with a fine not exceeding ₱500 for each violation in the supplied material. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

The major trap is the ₱5,000 amount associated with the specific penalties in Section 42.

Memory hook:
42 = specific → ₱5,000
43 = general → ₱500

Board tip: Do not automatically select ₱5,000 merely because the question concerns a violation of RA 776.

questions.question: A violation is not one of the specific offenses enumerated under Section 42, but it nevertheless falls within the general penalty provision of RA 776. Which section becomes applicable?
Which section of RA 776 provides for compromise regarding a penalty?
questions.explanation:
Section 44 is entitled Compromise Regarding Penalty. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

The neighboring provisions are:
• Section 42 → Specific Penalties
• Section 43 → General Penalty
• Section 44 → Compromise Regarding Penalty
• Section 45 → Enforcement of Orders

Board tip: The word 'compromise' is the giveaway. Do not confuse it with reconsideration under Section 47 or judicial review under Section 49.

questions.question: What is the primary subject of Section 45 of RA 776?
How are orders of the Board enforced under the supplied Section 45 material?
choices: By any of the civil remedies provided by existing law
questions.answerText: By any of the civil remedies provided by existing law

questions.question: When does Section 46 of RA 776 become relevant?
choices: When determining the effective date of orders and decisions
questions.answerText: When determining the effective date of orders and decisions
questions.explanation:
Section 46 is entitled Effective Date of Orders and Decisions. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

This provision follows Enforcement of Orders in Section 45 and precedes Reconsideration of Orders in Section 47.

Memory sequence:
45 → Enforcement
46 → Effective Date
47 → Reconsideration
48 → Finality
49 → Judicial Review
50 → Fees.

questions.question: An examinee confuses the effective date of a Board decision with the date on which the decision becomes final and conclusive. Which distinction is correct under the section sequence of RA 776?
choices: Section 46 concerns the effective date, while Section 48 concerns finality
Section 47 concerns the effective date, while Section 46 concerns finality
Section 48 concerns reconsideration, while Section 47 concerns judicial review
Section 46 concerns fees, while Section 50 concerns finality
questions.answerText: Section 46 concerns the effective date, while Section 48 concerns finality
questions.explanation:
The sections address different procedural concepts:

• Section 46 → Effective Date of Orders and Decisions
• Section 47 → Reconsideration of Orders
• Section 48 → Finality of Decision, Order or Ruling
• Section 49 → Judicial Review
• Section 50 → Fees. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

Board tip: The terms 'effective' and 'final' sound similar but are not interchangeable. The Act gives them separate sections.

questions.question: What procedural remedy is addressed by Section 47 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 47 is entitled Reconsideration of Orders. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

The sequence is important:
44 → Compromise Regarding Penalty
45 → Enforcement of Orders
46 → Effective Date of Orders and Decisions
47 → Reconsideration of Orders
48 → Finality
49 → Judicial Review

Board tip: Reconsideration comes before finality in the statutory sequence.

questions.question: A party seeks reconsideration of a Board order rather than immediately pursuing judicial review. Which section of RA 776 is directly associated with that remedy?
questions.explanation:
Section 47 specifically addresses Reconsideration of Orders. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}

Judicial review is addressed separately under Section 49.

The distinction is therefore:
• Reconsideration → Section 47
• Finality → Section 48
• Judicial Review → Section 49

Board tip: Do not treat reconsideration and judicial review as the same procedural step.

questions.question: How many days are provided in the supplied Section 48 material before a decision, order, or ruling becomes final and conclusive, unless appealed within that period?
A party does not appeal a Board decision within the period stated in Section 48 of the supplied RA 776 material. What is the stated consequence?
choices: The decision automatically becomes advisory only
The decision, order, or ruling becomes final and conclusive
The decision must automatically be reconsidered
The decision is automatically transferred to the CAB Chairman
