questions.answerText: The decision, order, or ruling becomes final and conclusive

questions.question: Under the supplied Section 48 material, what is the stated mode of appeal to the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material states that a decision, order, or ruling becomes final and conclusive after fifteen days unless appealed within that period to the Supreme Court by certiorari. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}

Board tip: This is a terminology trap. Mandamus, injunction, and habeas corpus are distinct legal remedies and should not be substituted for the term expressly identified in the supplied Section 48 material.

questions.question: Which section of RA 776 deals specifically with judicial review?
questions.explanation:
Section 49 is entitled Judicial Review. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}

It follows Section 48, Finality of Decision, Order or Ruling, and precedes Section 50, Fees.

Memory hook:
47 → Reconsider
48 → Final
49 → Review
50 → Fees.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly arranges Sections 47 through 50 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material gives the following sequence:

• Section 47 → Reconsideration of Orders
• Section 48 → Finality of Decision, Order or Ruling
• Section 49 → Judicial Review
• Section 50 → Fees. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}

This is a useful sequence because the concepts form a procedural progression.

Memory hook: Reconsider → Final → Review → Pay.

questions.question: Under the supplied Section 50 material, how much is the fee for engagement in air commerce?
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 50 material lists ₱250 as the fee for engagement in air commerce. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}

The same material lists:
• ₱100 → ratings of aviation schools and other agencies
• ₱50 → issuance of airmen's certificate

Board trap: All three amounts are close enough to invite careless selection. Associate each amount with its specific purpose.

questions.question: How much is the fee stated in the supplied Section 50 material for ratings of aviation schools and other agencies?
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 50 material states a ₱100 fee for ratings of aviation schools and other agencies. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

For comparison:
• ₱250 → engagement in air commerce
• ₱100 → ratings of aviation schools and other agencies
• ₱50 → issuance of airmen's certificate.

Memory hook: 250–100–50 = Commerce–Schools–Airmen.

questions.question: What fee is stated in the supplied Section 50 material for the issuance of an airman's certificate?
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 50 material identifies ₱50 as the fee for issuance of an airman's certificate. :contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}

The other listed amounts are:
• ₱250 → engagement in air commerce
• ₱100 → ratings of aviation schools and other agencies.

Board tip: Numerical questions are especially vulnerable to memory errors. Memorize the amount together with its purpose rather than memorizing the numbers alone.

questions.question: A student remembers that Section 50 contains three fees: ₱250, ₱100, and ₱50. Which pairing is CORRECT?
choices: ₱50 – ratings of aviation schools and other agencies
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 50 material gives the following pairings: :contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}

• ₱250 → engagement in air commerce
• ₱100 → ratings of aviation schools and other agencies
• ₱50 → issuance of airman's certificate

Only the third pairing is correct.

Board tip: This is the kind of matching trap where every distractor uses a real amount from the same section but attaches it to the wrong activity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly associated with Sections 43–50 of RA 776?
choices: Section 48 – Finality of Decision, Order or Ruling
questions.explanation:
Section 50 concerns Fees, not Judicial Review. Judicial Review is Section 49. :contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}

The correct sequence is:
43 → General Penalty
44 → Compromise Regarding Penalty
45 → Enforcement of Orders
46 → Effective Date of Orders and Decisions
47 → Reconsideration of Orders
48 → Finality
49 → Judicial Review
50 → Fees.

Board tip: When an EXCEPT/NOT question presents mostly correct section-title pairings, look for a single one shifted by one section.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 51 of RA 776 in the supplied material?
questions.explanation:
Section 51 is identified in the supplied material as OTHER FEES. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

The surrounding provisions are:
• Section 50 → preceding fee/conveyance material in the reviewer
• Section 51 → Other Fees
• Section 52 → Disposition of Receipt
• Section 53 → Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions
• Section 54 → Effectivity
• Section 55 → Appropriation
• Section 56 → Effectivity.

Board tip: The word 'Other' is important. Do not automatically associate every fee provision with the earlier general fee provision.

questions.question: Which fee is stated in the supplied material for the registration of an aircraft, regardless of type?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material states a fee of ₱50 for registration of an aircraft, regardless of type. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

The same material separately states ₱10 for registration of engines, propellers and/or appliances.

Memory hook:
Aircraft → ₱50
Engine/propeller/appliance → ₱10 each

Board trap: The ₱10 amount is intentionally placed beside the aircraft registration fee to make the numbers easy to interchange.

questions.question: How much is charged under the supplied Section 51 material for registration of an aircraft regardless of type?
An applicant registers an aircraft engine. Under the supplied Section 51 material, what registration fee applies to the engine?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material states ₱10 each for registration of engines, propellers and/or appliances. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

This differs from the ₱50 fee stated for registration of an aircraft regardless of type.

Memory hook:
Aircraft = 50
Each engine/propeller/appliance = 10.

questions.question: Which pairing is CORRECT according to the supplied Section 51 material?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material gives:

• ₱50 → registration of aircraft, regardless of type
• ₱10 each → registration of engines, propellers and/or appliances. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

The distractors simply reverse or alter the amounts.

Board tip: Numerical questions become easier when the number is memorized together with the object being charged.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 52 of RA 776 in the supplied material?
questions.explanation:
Section 52 is identified as DISPOSITION OF RECEIPT. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

It follows Section 51, Other Fees, and precedes Section 53, Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions.

Memory sequence:
51 → Fees
52 → Receipt
53 → Separability
54 → Effectivity
55 → Appropriation
56 → Effectivity.

questions.question: A question asks which section deals with the disposition of receipts rather than the amount of fees. What is the correct answer?
What happens under the provision identified as Section 53 of RA 776?
choices: The Act establishes a system for aircraft registration
The Act addresses separability of unconstitutional provisions
The Act establishes additional aircraft registration fees
The Act appropriates ₱60,000 from the National Treasury

questions.question: Which section of the supplied RA 776 material is associated with the separability of unconstitutional provisions?
A court determines that one provision of the Act is unconstitutional. Which statutory concept is intended to prevent that determination from necessarily invalidating the entire Act?
What is the subject of Section 54 of RA 776 in the supplied material?
Which section comes immediately after Section 53, Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions?
questions.explanation:
The supplied sequence is:

Section 51 → Other Fees
Section 52 → Disposition of Receipt
Section 53 → Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions
Section 54 → Effectivity
Section 55 → Appropriation
Section 56 → Effectivity. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}

This is a straightforward sequence question with neighboring sections as distractors.

questions.question: What amount is identified in the supplied material under Section 55, Appropriation?
Where does the ₱60,000 appropriation identified in the supplied Section 55 material come from?
questions.explanation:
The supplied material states under Section 55 that ₱60,000 is appropriated from funds in the National Treasury. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}

The key combination to remember is:
Section 55 → Appropriation → ₱60,000 → National Treasury.

Board trap: The distractors use aviation-related sources of money, but the supplied provision specifically identifies funds in the National Treasury.

questions.question: Which pairing is CORRECT under the supplied Sections 53–56 material?
questions.explanation:
The supplied sequence identifies:

• Section 53 → Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions
• Section 54 → Effectivity
• Section 55 → Appropriation
• Section 56 → Effectivity. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}

Therefore, Section 55 → Appropriation is the only correctly paired choice.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 56 in the supplied RA 776 material?
questions.explanation:
Section 56 is identified as EFFECTIVITY. The supplied material further states: 'This Act shall take effect upon its approval' and gives the date of approval as June 20, 1952. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

Memory hook:
55 → ₱60,000 Appropriation
56 → Effectivity

Board tip: Do not confuse Section 54, which is also labeled Effectivity in the supplied material, with the final Section 56 effectivity provision.

questions.question: When did RA 776 take effect according to the supplied material?
choices: Upon the appointment of the first Administrator
Upon the organization of the Civil Aeronautics Board
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 56 material states that the Act shall take effect upon its approval. It identifies the date of approval as June 20, 1952. :contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}

Board tip: Do not substitute the usual modern assumptions concerning publication and effectivity when the question is specifically asking for the wording contained in the supplied material.

questions.question: On what date was RA 776 approved according to the supplied material?
Which sequence correctly represents Sections 51 through 56 in the supplied material?
choices: Other Fees → Disposition of Receipt → Separability → Effectivity → Appropriation → Effectivity
Other Fees → Appropriation → Disposition of Receipt → Effectivity → Separability → Finality
Disposition of Receipt → Other Fees → Effectivity → Appropriation → Separability → Finality
Appropriation → Other Fees → Disposition of Receipt → Separability → Effectivity → General Penalty
questions.answerText: Other Fees → Disposition of Receipt → Separability → Effectivity → Appropriation → Effectivity
questions.explanation:
The supplied material gives the sequence exactly as:

• Section 51 → Other Fees
• Section 52 → Disposition of Receipt
• Section 53 → Separability of Unconstitutional Provisions
• Section 54 → Effectivity
• Section 55 → Appropriation
• Section 56 → Effectivity. :contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}

This is a high-value memorization sequence because the last two sections are especially easy to reverse.

questions.question: A candidate answers that Section 55 concerns Effectivity because it comes near the end of RA 776. What is the correct correction based on the supplied material?
choices: Section 55 concerns Appropriation, while Section 56 concerns Effectivity
Section 55 concerns Other Fees, while Section 56 concerns Appropriation
Section 55 concerns Separability, while Section 56 concerns Disposition of Receipt
Section 55 concerns General Penalty, while Section 56 concerns Judicial Review
questions.answerText: Section 55 concerns Appropriation, while Section 56 concerns Effectivity
questions.explanation:
The supplied material clearly identifies Section 55 as APPROPRIATION and Section 56 as EFFECTIVITY. :contentReference[oaicite:20]{index=20}

This is a deliberately tricky neighboring-section question.

Memory hook:
54 = Effectivity
55 = ₱60,000 Appropriation
56 = Effectivity.

The repeated 'Effectivity' makes Section 55 particularly easy to skip or misremember.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the supplied Sections 51–56 material?
questions.explanation:
Section 55 is identified as APPROPRIATION, not Finality of Decision. :contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}

The correct sequence is:
51 → Other Fees
52 → Disposition of Receipt
53 → Separability
54 → Effectivity
55 → Appropriation
56 → Effectivity.

Board tip: The 'NOT' wording means you should look for the single incorrect pairing rather than simply identifying a correct one.

questions.question: What is the official short title of Republic Act No. 9497?
choices: Philippine Civil Aviation Regulation Act of 2008
questions.explanation:
Republic Act No. 9497 is known as the Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008.

Memory hook: RA 9497 → CAAA 2008.

Board trap: Do not confuse the name of the law with the name of the agency it created. The law is the Civil Aviation Authority Act, while the authority created under it is the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP).

questions.question: When was Republic Act No. 9497 approved?
questions.explanation:
The supplied laws material identifies March 4, 2008 as the date associated with RA 9497. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

Do not confuse this with the date July 23, 2007, which appears in the reviewer as the date the legislative session was begun and held in Manila.

Memory hook:
RA 776 → 20 June 1952
PD 1570 → 11 June 1978
RA 9497 → 04 March 2008.

questions.question: When was Republic Act No. 776, otherwise known as the Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines, approved?
questions.explanation:
RA 776, the Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines, was approved on June 20, 1952.

The date is significant because RA 776 is the foundational Philippine civil aviation law from which many later aviation regulatory developments evolved.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 → 06/20/52.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse RA 776 with PD 1570 (1978) or RA 9497 (2008).

questions.question: What is the official title of Republic Act No. 776?
choices: The Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines
questions.answerText: The Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines
questions.explanation:
RA 776 is entitled 'The Civil Aeronautics Act of the Philippines.'

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 = Civil Aeronautics Act.
RA 9497 = Civil Aviation Authority Act of 2008.
PD 1570 = Philippine Aeronautical Decree.

🎯 Board Tip:
The titles of RA 776 and RA 9497 are intentionally easy to mix up.

questions.question: What is the principal purpose of RA 776 as stated in Section 2?
choices: To reorganize the CAB and CAA, define their powers and duties, adjust funds and personnel, and regulate civil aeronautics
To regulate only international air transportation
To establish the Professional Regulation Commission
questions.answerText: To reorganize the CAB and CAA, define their powers and duties, adjust funds and personnel, and regulate civil aeronautics
questions.explanation:
Section 2 states the purpose and scope of the Act. It includes the reorganization of the Civil Aeronautics Board and Civil Aeronautics Administration, defining their powers and duties, making adjustments of funds and personnel, and regulating civil aeronautics.

💡 Memory Hook:
REORGANIZE → DEFINE → ADJUST → REGULATE.

🎯 Board Tip:
The question asks for the overall purpose, not merely the name of an agency created by later legislation.

questions.question: Under Section 2 of RA 776, to what extent does the Act apply to military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and foreign countries?
choices: It applies fully to all military aircraft and airmen
It does not apply, except with respect to air traffic rules
It applies only to Philippine military aircraft
It applies only to foreign military aircraft
questions.answerText: It does not apply, except with respect to air traffic rules
questions.explanation:
Section 2 provides that the Act shall not apply to military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and of foreign countries, except with respect to air traffic rules.

💡 Memory Hook:
Military aviation → generally OUT; air traffic rules → EXCEPTION.

🎯 Board Tip:
The word 'except' is the trap. The Act is not completely irrelevant to military aircraft because air traffic rules remain applicable.

questions.question: Which category is expressly excluded from the general application of RA 776, subject to the statutory exceptions?
questions.explanation:
Section 2 specifically addresses military aircraft and airmen of the Philippines and foreign countries, stating that the Act does not apply to them except with respect to air traffic rules.

💡 Memory Hook:
Military = excluded, but traffic rules remain.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not extend this exclusion to domestic civil air carriers.

questions.question: Under Section 3 of RA 776, what does 'air commerce' include?
choices: Only carriage of passengers for compensation
Air transportation for pay or hire, navigation in furtherance of a business, or navigation from one place to another for conducting a business
questions.answerText: Air transportation for pay or hire, navigation in furtherance of a business, or navigation from one place to another for conducting a business
questions.explanation:
Section 3 defines air commerce broadly. It includes air transportation for pay or hire, navigation of aircraft in furtherance of a business, and navigation from one place to another for operation in the conduct of a business.

💡 Memory Hook:
AIR COMMERCE = AIR + BUSINESS.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not equate air commerce exclusively with passenger transportation. The statutory definition is broader.

questions.question: A company uses an aircraft to travel between two locations as part of conducting its business, even though the flight is not simply the carriage of passengers for hire. Which defined term under Section 3 is most applicable?
questions.explanation:
The definition of air commerce includes navigation of aircraft from one place to another for operation in the conduct of a business. Therefore, the statutory concept is broader than commercial passenger carriage for hire.

💡 Memory Hook:
Business use of aircraft → think AIR COMMERCE.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'for pay or hire' is only one part of the definition. Business navigation can independently fall within air commerce.

questions.question: What is 'air transportation' under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: Service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft
A radio station located aboard an aircraft
A locality adapted for aircraft landing
questions.answerText: Service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft
questions.explanation:
Section 3 defines air transportation as the service or carriage of persons, property, or mail, in whole or in part, by aircraft.

💡 Memory Hook:
Transportation = PEOPLE + PROPERTY + MAIL.

🎯 Board Tip:
Compare this with 'air commerce,' which is a broader business-related concept.

questions.question: Which distinction BEST separates 'air commerce' from 'air transportation' under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: Air commerce is limited to military operations, while air transportation is civil
Air transportation concerns carriage or service of persons, property, or mail, while air commerce encompasses that and broader business-related aircraft navigation
Air commerce concerns only mail, while air transportation concerns only passengers
There is no distinction between the two terms
questions.answerText: Air transportation concerns carriage or service of persons, property, or mail, while air commerce encompasses that and broader business-related aircraft navigation
questions.explanation:
The statutory definitions overlap but are not identical.

Air transportation focuses on service or carriage of persons, property, or mail by aircraft. Air commerce is broader and includes air transportation for pay or hire as well as aircraft navigation in furtherance of business.

💡 Memory Hook:
Transportation = CARRIAGE.
Commerce = CARRIAGE + BUSINESS.

🎯 Board Tip:
When two statutory definitions appear similar, look for the additional scope contained in one definition.

questions.question: What does the term 'airway' mean under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: Any runway located at an airport
A path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width and designated or approved as suitable for air commerce or air transportation
A radio frequency assigned to an aircraft
A locality used exclusively for emergency landings
questions.answerText: A path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width and designated or approved as suitable for air commerce or air transportation
questions.explanation:
Section 3 defines an airway as a path through navigable airspace identified by an area of specified width on the surface of the Earth and designated or approved by the Administrator as suitable for air commerce or air transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
AIRWAY = PATH + WIDTH + APPROVAL.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse an airway with a physical runway. An airway is associated with navigable airspace.

questions.question: Under the definition of 'citizen of the Philippines' in Section 3 of RA 776, what minimum percentage of voting interest must be owned or controlled by Philippine citizens for a qualifying corporation or association?
questions.explanation:
Section 3 provides that a qualifying corporation or association must have at least sixty per centum of its voting interest owned or controlled by persons who are citizens of the Philippines. The definition also contains requirements concerning its organization, directing head, Board of Directors, and managing officers.

💡 Memory Hook:
RA 776 citizenship definition → 60% voting interest.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the 60% voting-interest requirement with the separate two-thirds Board requirement stated in the same definition.

questions.question: A corporation organized under Philippine law has a Filipino directing head and at least two-thirds of its Board and managing officers are Filipino. What additional ownership requirement appears in the Section 3 definition of a Philippine citizen?
choices: At least 25% of voting interest must be Filipino-owned
At least 40% of voting interest must be Filipino-owned
At least 60% of voting interest must be owned or controlled by Philippine citizens
100% of voting interest must be owned by one Filipino
questions.answerText: At least 60% of voting interest must be owned or controlled by Philippine citizens
questions.explanation:
The statutory definition contains multiple conditions. For a corporation or association, it includes organization under Philippine law, a Filipino directing head, at least two-thirds of the Board and other managing officers being Philippine citizens, and at least 60% of voting interest being owned or controlled by Philippine citizens.

💡 Memory Hook:
BOARD = 2/3.
VOTING = 60%.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic percentage trap: 2/3 applies to Board/managing officers, while 60% applies to voting interest.

questions.question: Who is considered a 'domestic air carrier' under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: Any air carrier operating within the Philippines
An air carrier who is a citizen of the Philippines
Any foreign air carrier with a Philippine route
Any air carrier registered with ICAO
questions.answerText: An air carrier who is a citizen of the Philippines
questions.explanation:
Section 3 defines a domestic air carrier as an air carrier who is a citizen of the Philippines.

💡 Memory Hook:
DOMESTIC AIR CARRIER = CITIZEN OF PHILIPPINES.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not assume that simply operating a route within Philippine territory automatically makes an air carrier a 'domestic air carrier' under this definition.

questions.question: What is a 'landing field' under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: Only a paved runway with passenger terminals
A locality on land or water adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by that airway
Any airport regardless of its location or function
questions.answerText: A locality on land or water adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by that airway
questions.explanation:
The statutory definition of landing field is broader than a conventional paved runway. It may be on land or water and is adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft, located along an airway and intermediate to airports connected by that airway. Facilities for shelter, servicing, repair, passengers, or cargo are not required by the definition.

💡 Memory Hook:
LANDING FIELD = LAND/WATER + LAND/TAKEOFF + AIRWAY.

🎯 Board Tip:
The absence of passenger or maintenance facilities does not automatically prevent a locality from being a landing field under the definition.

questions.question: Which statement about a landing field under Section 3 of RA 776 is CORRECT?
choices: It must always be located on land
It must have passenger and cargo facilities
It may be located on water or land
It must contain aircraft repair facilities
questions.answerText: It may be located on water or land
questions.explanation:
Section 3 expressly allows a landing field to be a locality either on water or on land adapted for landing and taking off of aircraft.

The definition does not require facilities for shelter, servicing, repair, receiving passengers, or discharging cargo.

💡 Memory Hook:
Landing field = WATER or LAND.

🎯 Board Tip:
The words 'whether or not facilities are provided' are important when distinguishing a landing field from a fully equipped airport.

questions.question: Under Section 3 of RA 776, what is meant by 'reasonable charges'?
choices: Any amount selected by the operator
Charges that ensure a just and reasonable return on capital invested while considering construction, operation, maintenance costs, and non-aeronautical revenue
Charges based solely on passenger demand
Charges determined exclusively by foreign aviation authorities
questions.answerText: Charges that ensure a just and reasonable return on capital invested while considering construction, operation, maintenance costs, and non-aeronautical revenue
questions.explanation:
The definition of reasonable charges considers a just and reasonable return on capital invested, taking into account the cost of construction, operation, and maintenance and the non-aeronautical revenue of the affected air navigation facility. The charges are also intended to be uniform.

💡 Memory Hook:
REASONABLE = RETURN + COSTS + NON-AERO REVENUE.

🎯 Board Tip:
The definition is not simply 'whatever the operator considers reasonable.' It contains specific economic considerations.

questions.question: What does the term 'general sales agent' describe under Section 3 of RA 776?
choices: A bona fide employee of an air carrier who performs maintenance
A person who is not a bona fide employee of an air carrier and, pursuant to authority from an airline, sells or offers air transportation or arranges such transportation
A government official who regulates airfares
A person who directly operates aircraft for cargo transportation
questions.answerText: A person who is not a bona fide employee of an air carrier and, pursuant to authority from an airline, sells or offers air transportation or arranges such transportation
questions.explanation:
A general sales agent is a person who is not a bona fide employee of an air carrier but, pursuant to authority from an airline, sells or offers air transportation or negotiates for, solicits, advertises, provides, furnishes, contracts, or arranges such transportation.

💡 Memory Hook:
GENERAL SALES AGENT = SELLS/ARRANGES AIR TRANSPORTATION.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'not a bona fide employee' is an important part of the statutory definition.

questions.question: How many members compose the Civil Aeronautics Board under Section 5 of RA 776 as presented in the statutory material?
questions.explanation:
Section 5 provides for a five-member Civil Aeronautics Board in the material.

The composition includes:
• Chairman — DOTC Secretary or representative
• Vice-Chairman — Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation
• PAF Commanding General
• Two appointed members

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB = 5.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the five-member CAB under RA 776 with the seven-member CAAP Board under RA 9497.

questions.question: Who serves as Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board under Section 5 of RA 776 as presented in the material?
questions.explanation:
The material identifies the DOTC Secretary or representative as Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB Chairman = DOTC Secretary/Representative.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the CAB Chairman with the Assistant Secretary for Air Transportation, who is identified as Vice-Chairman.

questions.question: Under Section 6 of RA 776, where is the principal office of the Civil Aeronautics Board?
questions.explanation:
Section 6 identifies Metro Manila as the principal office of the Civil Aeronautics Board.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB principal office → Metro Manila.

🎯 Board Tip:
Location questions are often easy points, but the choices may use major aviation locations such as Clark or Cebu as distractors.

questions.question: What constitutes a quorum of the Civil Aeronautics Board under Section 6 of RA 776?
choices: Two members plus either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman
The Chairman and all appointed members
questions.answerText: Two members plus either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman
questions.explanation:
Section 6 provides that a quorum consists of two members plus either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.

💡 Memory Hook:
CAB quorum = 2 + C/VC.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not simply count three members. The composition of the quorum has a specific requirement involving the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.

questions.question: A meeting of the Civil Aeronautics Board has three members present, but neither the Chairman nor the Vice-Chairman is present. Under Section 6 of RA 776, what is the best conclusion?
choices: A quorum automatically exists because three members are present
A quorum does not exist because either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman must be present with two members
A quorum exists only if the PAF representative is present
The meeting automatically becomes a special meeting
questions.answerText: A quorum does not exist because either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman must be present with two members
questions.explanation:
Section 6 does not define quorum merely by the number of members present. It requires two members plus either the Chairman or Vice-Chairman.

Thus, three ordinary members without the Chairman or Vice-Chairman do not satisfy the stated quorum requirement.

💡 Memory Hook:
COUNT + POSITION.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is a classic PRC-style trap: the numerical count alone is insufficient.

questions.question: What does CPCN stand for under Section 11 of RA 776?
choices: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.answerText: Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
questions.explanation:
CPCN stands for Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. Section 11 describes it as a permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN = Public Convenience + Necessity.

🎯 Board Tip:
The word 'Necessity' is easy to omit when recalling the acronym.

questions.question: What does a CPCN issued under Section 11 of RA 776 authorize?
choices: A person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic
questions.answerText: A person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, foreign and/or domestic
questions.explanation:
Section 11 defines the CPCN as a permit issued by the Board authorizing a person to engage in air commerce and/or transportation, whether foreign and/or domestic.

💡 Memory Hook:
CPCN = AUTHORIZATION TO ENGAGE.

🎯 Board Tip:
The statutory wording is broad: both air commerce and transportation, and both foreign and domestic activities, are contemplated.

questions.question: Under Section 12 of RA 776, who may engage in domestic air commerce and/or transportation?
questions.explanation:
Section 12 establishes the citizenship requirement for domestic air commerce and/or transportation. The provision states that such activities are for Filipinos only.

💡 Memory Hook:
Domestic air commerce → Filipinos ONLY.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse this with the broader concept of operating within Philippine airspace. The question is specifically about domestic air commerce and/or transportation.

questions.question: A foreign-owned air carrier wishes to engage in domestic air transportation in the Philippines. Which requirement presents the primary issue under Section 12 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 12 establishes a citizenship restriction for domestic air commerce and/or transportation. The provision states that such activities are for Filipinos only.

💡 Memory Hook:
§12 = WHO may engage domestically.

🎯 Board Tip:
The trap is to focus on whether the carrier has an aircraft or permit. Section 12 asks first whether the citizenship requirement is satisfied.

questions.question: What is the principal subject of Section 13 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 13 is entitled 'Conduct of Proceedings.' It begins the procedural provisions governing matters brought before the Civil Aeronautics Board.

💡 Memory Hook:
§13 = Proceedings begin.

🎯 Board Tip:
Sections 13 through 24 are largely procedural and permit-related. Knowing their sequence prevents section-number confusion.

questions.question: Under Section 14 of RA 776, what may be delegated?
choices: The existence of the Civil Aeronautics Board
questions.explanation:
Section 14 is specifically concerned with the delegation of authority to conduct hearings.

💡 Memory Hook:
§14 = Delegate HEARINGS.

🎯 Board Tip:
The provision does not mean that the CAB itself is transferred or abolished. It concerns authority connected with conducting hearings.

questions.question: Which section of RA 776 specifically addresses the application for a permit?
questions.explanation:
Section 15 is entitled 'Application of Permit.' It follows the provisions concerning the conduct of proceedings and delegation of authority to conduct hearings.

💡 Memory Hook:
13 = Conduct.
14 = Delegate hearings.
15 = Apply.

🎯 Board Tip:
The section sequence itself can be used as a memory aid.

questions.question: An applicant seeks authority from the Board to engage in an activity requiring a permit. Which provision is most directly associated with the applicant's submission of the permit request?
questions.explanation:
Section 15 specifically addresses the application for a permit.

The later sections address matters such as notice, non-appearance, hearings, issuance, modification, transfer, and duration.

💡 Memory Hook:
15 = APPLICATION.
21 = ISSUANCE.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not jump to Section 21 merely because the question involves a permit. Determine whether the question concerns applying for or actually issuing the permit.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 16 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 16 concerns notice in connection with the Board's proceedings.

💡 Memory Hook:
§15 = Apply.
§16 = Notice.
§17 = Time and Place.

🎯 Board Tip:
These procedural provisions are consecutive, making them excellent targets for section-number questions.

questions.question: Under Section 17 of RA 776, what matter is specifically addressed?
questions.explanation:
Section 17 is entitled 'Time and Place of Meeting.' It follows the notice provision and precedes the provision concerning non-appearance.

💡 Memory Hook:
15 Apply → 16 Notice → 17 Time/Place.

🎯 Board Tip:
When a question asks for a section number, reconstruct the procedural sequence instead of guessing.

questions.question: What statutory matter is covered by Section 18 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 18 is entitled 'Non-Appearance.' It follows the provisions on notice and the time and place of meetings.

💡 Memory Hook:
16 = Notice.
17 = Meeting.
18 = No-show.

🎯 Board Tip:
The progression mirrors a proceeding: notice → meeting → non-appearance.

questions.question: Which procedural device is the subject of Section 19 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 19 is entitled 'Deposition.' It is part of the Board's procedural provisions governing proceedings.

💡 Memory Hook:
§18 = Non-appearance.
§19 = Deposition.
§20 = Hearing/Records.

🎯 Board Tip:
The sequence from Sections 16–20 is highly testable because each section has a distinct procedural subject.

questions.question: Under Section 20 of RA 776, what are specifically addressed together?
questions.explanation:
Section 20 addresses hearings and records of proceedings.

💡 Memory Hook:
§19 = Deposition.
§20 = Hearing + Record.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse Section 20 with Section 14. Section 14 concerns delegation of authority to conduct hearings, while Section 20 concerns hearings and their records.

questions.question: A proceeding has been heard before the Board and the resulting proceedings must be documented. Which provision is most directly associated with this matter?
questions.explanation:
Section 20 specifically covers hearings and records of proceedings.

💡 Memory Hook:
Hear it → Record it → §20.

🎯 Board Tip:
The presence of the word 'hearing' can tempt you toward Section 14. But Section 14 is about delegation of authority to conduct hearings, while Section 20 addresses the hearings and records themselves.

questions.question: What happens under Section 21 of RA 776?
choices: The applicant is automatically granted citizenship
questions.explanation:
Section 21 is entitled 'Issuance of Permit.' It follows the procedural provisions concerning the application, notice, meetings, non-appearance, depositions, and hearings.

💡 Memory Hook:
15 = Apply.
21 = Issue.

🎯 Board Tip:
Application and issuance are separated by several procedural provisions. Do not treat them as the same statutory step.

questions.question: Which action is covered by Section 22 of RA 776?
choices: Modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit
questions.answerText: Modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit
questions.explanation:
Section 22 addresses modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit.

💡 Memory Hook:
§21 = ISSUE.
§22 = CHANGE/STOP/CANCEL.

🎯 Board Tip:
A permit does not simply have an all-or-nothing existence. Section 22 recognizes modification, suspension, and revocation as separate actions.

questions.question: A carrier's existing permit needs to be altered rather than completely cancelled. Which provision of RA 776 is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation:
Section 22 expressly covers modification, suspension, or revocation of a permit. Therefore, alteration of an existing permit falls within Section 22.

💡 Memory Hook:
Existing permit + alteration = §22.

🎯 Board Tip:
Section 21 concerns issuance, while Section 22 concerns what may happen to an already existing permit.

questions.question: Under Section 23 of RA 776, may a permit be transferred freely from one holder to another?
choices: Yes, provided the transfer is verbally reported
No; prior approval of the Board is required
No; permits can never be transferred under any circumstance
questions.answerText: No; prior approval of the Board is required
questions.explanation:
Section 23 provides that no permit may be transferred without the prior approval of the Board.

This means the provision does not state that transfer is absolutely impossible; rather, Board approval must be obtained beforehand.

💡 Memory Hook:
§23 = TRANSFER → PRIOR APPROVAL.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'cannot be transferred' would be too absolute. The statutory rule is that transfer requires prior Board approval.

questions.question: A permit holder transfers the permit to another party before obtaining approval from the Civil Aeronautics Board. Which statement BEST describes the situation under Section 23 of RA 776?
choices: The transfer is valid because approval can be obtained later
The transfer violates the requirement for prior Board approval
The transfer is automatically valid if both parties agree
The transfer is governed only by aircraft registration law
questions.answerText: The transfer violates the requirement for prior Board approval
questions.explanation:
Section 23 expressly requires prior approval of the Board before a permit may be transferred.

The key word is PRIOR. Approval after the transfer does not satisfy the literal timing requirement stated in the provision.

💡 Memory Hook:
TRANSFER FIRST? ❌
APPROVAL FIRST?

✅

🎯 Board Tip:
PRC-style questions often hide the answer in a single timing word such as 'prior.'

questions.question: When does a permit become effective under Section 24 of RA 776?
choices: From the date specified in the permit
questions.answerText: From the date specified in the permit
questions.explanation:
Section 24 provides that a permit becomes effective from the date specified therein. It continues until suspended or revoked, or until the Board certifies that the operation under it has ceased.

💡 Memory Hook:
§24 = DATE SPECIFIED.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the effective date with the 90-day inauguration rule or the 25-year maximum duration.

questions.question: A service authorized by a permit has not been inaugurated within the required period. What may the Board do under Section 24 of RA 776?
choices: It may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of the service concerned
It must automatically extend the permit for another 25 years
It must transfer the permit to another carrier
It may convert the permit into an aircraft certificate
questions.answerText: It may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of the service concerned
questions.explanation:
Section 24 provides that if any service authorized by a permit is not inaugurated within ninety days, the Board may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of such service.

💡 Memory Hook:
90 days = START THE SERVICE.

🎯 Board Tip:
The provision concerns the service authorized by the permit. It does not automatically mean that every part of a permit must disappear in every case.

questions.question: How long, at most, may a permit be issued under Section 24 of RA 776?
questions.explanation:
Section 24 expressly provides that no permit shall be issued for a period of more than twenty-five years.

💡 Memory Hook:
§24 → MAX = 25 YEARS.

🎯 Board Tip:
Remember the distinction between the two major numbers in Section 24:
• 90 days → service inauguration
• 25 years → maximum permit period

questions.question: Which pair of time limits is correctly associated with Section 24 of RA 776?
choices: 30 days for inauguration and 10 years maximum duration
60 days for inauguration and 20 years maximum duration
90 days for inauguration and 25 years maximum duration
120 days for inauguration and 30 years maximum duration
questions.answerText: 90 days for inauguration and 25 years maximum duration
questions.explanation:
Section 24 contains two important numerical limits:

• If authorized service is not inaugurated within 90 days, the Board may direct that the permit cease to be effective to the extent of that service.
• No permit shall be issued for more than 25 years.

💡 Memory Hook:
90 → START.
25 → MAX.

Board tip: Do not add a specialized aeronautical-engineering requirement when the statute gives a broader aviation supervisory/management requirement.

questions.question: A 34-year-old Filipino degree holder has six years of aviation management experience and unquestionable integrity. Which qualification prevents appointment as Director General under Section 9?
A 35-year-old applicant has only four years of supervisory experience in aviation. Assuming all other qualifications are satisfied, what is the deficiency under Section 9?
What is the regular meeting frequency of the CAAP Board under Section 10 of RA 9497?
Who may call a special CAAP Board meeting to consider urgent matters under Section 10?
choices: The Chairman or upon the initiative of four members
Any single Board member without limitation
questions.answerText: The Chairman or upon the initiative of four members
questions.explanation:
The supplied Section 10 material states that the Board may hold special meetings for urgent matters upon the call of the Chairman OR upon the initiative of FOUR (4) members. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}

Board trap: Do not confuse the four members required to initiate a special meeting with the three-member vote required for adoption of a Board act under Section 8.

questions.question: Four CAAP Board members initiate a special meeting because an urgent matter requires immediate consideration. Under the supplied Section 10 material, is this sufficient to initiate the meeting?
choices: No, all seven members must initiate it
No, only the Director General may initiate it

questions.question: Which section of RA 9497 governs the per diem of Board members?
questions.explanation:
Section 11 is identified as PER DIEM. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}

The nearby sections are:
• Section 8 → Quorum
• Section 9 → Director General Qualifications
• Section 10 → Board Meetings
• Section 11 → Per Diem
• Section 12 → Personnel

Board tip: This is a section-identification item designed around consecutive organizational provisions.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 12 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 12 is identified as PERSONNEL. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}

The sequence is:
10 → Board Meetings
11 → Per Diem
12 → Personnel
13 → Principal Office
14 → Capitalization
15 → Fiscal Autonomy
16 → Exemption from Taxes, Customs and Tariff Duties.

Memory hook: Meetings → Per Diem → Personnel → Office → Capital → Fiscal → Tax.

questions.question: Where is the subject of the Authority's principal office addressed in RA 9497?
How much is the authorized capital stock of the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines under Section 14 of RA 9497?
A question asks for the numerical value of the authorized capital stock of CAAP expressed in pesos. Which answer is correct under Section 14?
What principle is addressed by Section 15 of RA 9497?
Which section of RA 9497 provides for exemption from taxes, customs and tariff duties?
Which of the following is included among the items identified in the supplied Section 16 exemption provision?
choices: Imported equipment, machinery, spare parts and accessories
Personal automobiles of all CAAP employees
Private residential properties of Board members
All consumer goods imported by airline passengers
questions.answerText: Imported equipment, machinery, spare parts and accessories

questions.question: Which sequence correctly identifies Sections 13–16 of RA 9497?
choices: Principal Office → Capitalization → Fiscal Autonomy → Exemption from Taxes, Customs and Tariff Duties
Capitalization → Principal Office → Exemption → Fiscal Autonomy
Fiscal Autonomy → Principal Office → Capitalization → Exemption
Principal Office → Fiscal Autonomy → Capitalization → Per Diem
questions.answerText: Principal Office → Capitalization → Fiscal Autonomy → Exemption from Taxes, Customs and Tariff Duties
questions.explanation:
The supplied material identifies the sequence as: :contentReference[oaicite:22]{index=22}

Section 13 → Principal Office
Section 14 → Capitalization
Section 15 → Fiscal Autonomy
Section 16 → Exemption from Taxes, Customs and Tariff Duties.

This is a useful four-section chain because the provisions move from organizational location to financial structure.

questions.question: Under Section 17 of RA 9497, how often may the Authority revise its schedule of fees and fines at most?
questions.explanation:
Section 17 limits the frequency of revision of the Authority's schedule of fees and fines. It shall NOT be revised more often than once every three (3) years.

• The key phrase is "not more often than once every three years."
• This establishes a minimum interval between revisions.

Memory hook: FEES = 3 YEARS.

Board tip: Watch the wording. "Every three years" and "not more often than once every three years" test the same statutory limitation, but choices such as 1, 2, or 5 years are common traps.

questions.question: A proposed revision of CAAP's schedule of fees and fines is made only 18 months after the previous revision. Under Section 17 of RA 9497, which is the BEST conclusion?
choices: It is permissible because the Director General approved it
It is permissible if the Board votes unanimously
It is not permissible because the schedule may not be revised more often than once every three years
It is permissible provided the revision concerns only fines
questions.answerText: It is not permissible because the schedule may not be revised more often than once every three years
questions.explanation:
Section 17 establishes a three-year restriction on revision of the schedule of fees and fines. A revision after only 18 months would be more frequent than the law permits.

• Board approval does not erase the statutory limitation.
• The restriction applies to the schedule of fees AND fines.

Memory hook: 18 months < 3 years = TOO SOON.

Board tip: The trap is assuming that administrative approval can override a statutory time limitation.

questions.question: Which statement BEST captures the restriction imposed by Section 17 of RA 9497?
choices: Fees and fines must be revised every three years
Fees and fines may be revised only once during the entire three-year period
The schedule of fees and fines shall not be revised more often than once every three years
The Authority is prohibited from changing fees and fines for three years after every violation
questions.answerText: The schedule of fees and fines shall not be revised more often than once every three years
questions.explanation:
Section 17 specifically limits how frequently the Authority may revise its schedule of fees and fines. The statutory limitation is that revision shall not occur more often than once every three years.

Memory hook: NOT MORE OFTEN = 3 YEARS.

Board tip: "Must be revised every three years" is stronger than what the provision says and is therefore a tempting but incorrect choice.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 18 of RA 9497?
choices: Compensation and other emoluments of Authority personnel
questions.answerText: Compensation and other emoluments of Authority personnel
questions.explanation:
Section 18 is entitled "Compensation and Other Emoluments of Authority Personnel."

It concerns the compensation framework for personnel of the Authority.

Memory hook: Section 17 = FEES; Section 18 = PAY.

Board tip: Sections 17 and 18 are adjacent. Do not confuse the Authority's external fees and fines with compensation paid to its personnel.

questions.question: Which of the following is covered specifically by Section 18 of RA 9497?
choices: Compensation and other emoluments of Authority personnel
Compensation of passengers for delayed flights
questions.answerText: Compensation and other emoluments of Authority personnel
questions.explanation:
Section 18 deals with the compensation and other emoluments of personnel of the Authority.

The other choices concern different regulatory or operational matters and do not identify the subject of Section 18.

Memory hook: EMOLUMENTS = EMPLOYEE COMPENSATION.

Board tip: "Emoluments" is a favorite vocabulary trap. In this context, it refers to compensation or benefits received by Authority personnel.

questions.question: Under Section 19 of RA 9497, what happened to the funds, appropriations, records, equipment, and property of the Air Transportation Office?
choices: They were transferred to the Civil Aeronautics Board
They were transferred to the Authority
They were transferred to the Department of Finance
They remained permanently under the abolished ATO
questions.answerText: They were transferred to the Authority
questions.explanation:
Section 19 provides for the transfer of the funds and appropriations, records, equipment, and property of the Air Transportation Office to the Authority.

Memory hook: ATO → CAAP.

Board tip: RA 9497 abolished the ATO while establishing CAAP. Do not confuse the transfer of ATO assets with the status of the Civil Aeronautics Board, which was not abolished by the Act.

questions.question: A question asks which government aviation entity's funds, records, equipment, and property were transferred to the Authority upon the establishment of CAAP. What is the correct answer?
questions.explanation:
Section 19 specifically provides for the transfer of the funds, appropriations, records, equipment, and property of the Air Transportation Office to the Authority.

Memory hook: ATO was abolished → its institutional resources moved to CAAP.

Board tip: CAB is the dangerous distractor. RA 9497 expressly did NOT abolish the Civil Aeronautics Board.

questions.question: Which item is LEAST consistent with the transfer contemplated by Section 19 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 19 concerns the transfer of the funds and appropriations, records, equipment, and property of the Air Transportation Office to the Authority. It does not transfer or abolish the Civil Aeronautics Board.

Memory hook: SECTION 19 = ATO RESOURCES, NOT CAB.

Board tip: A choice may mention a real aviation institution but still be wrong because it is outside the scope of the particular section.

questions.question: When is the annual report of the Authority required to be submitted under Section 20 of RA 9497?
choices: At the beginning of every calendar year
At the close of each calendar year
Only upon request of the President
questions.answerText: At the close of each calendar year
questions.explanation:
Section 20 requires the Authority to prepare and submit an annual report on its accomplishments at the close of each calendar year.

Memory hook: ANNUAL REPORT = YEAR-END.

Board tip: The phrase "at the close of each calendar year" is the important statutory timing language.

questions.question: To whom must the Authority submit its annual report under Section 20 of RA 9497?
choices: President, Senate, and House of Representatives
Senate and House of Representatives only
questions.answerText: President, Senate, and House of Representatives
questions.explanation:
Section 20 requires the Authority to prepare and submit its annual report to the President, to the Senate, and to the House of Representatives.

Memory hook: REPORT = P + S + H.

Board tip: "President only" is an easy trap because executive agencies commonly report to the President, but this provision expressly includes both Houses of Congress.

questions.question: The annual report required by Section 20 primarily concerns the Authority's:
questions.explanation:
Section 20 states that the Authority shall prepare and submit an annual report on its accomplishments at the close of each calendar year.

Memory hook: ANNUAL REPORT = ACCOMPLISHMENTS.

Board tip: Do not substitute the general subject of an agency's operations for the specific subject identified by the section.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly matches Sections 17 through 20 of RA 9497 with their principal subjects?
choices: Fees and fines → compensation → transfer of properties → annual report
Compensation → fees and fines → annual report → transfer of properties
Fees and fines → annual report → compensation → transfer of properties
Transfer of properties → compensation → fees and fines → annual report
questions.answerText: Fees and fines → compensation → transfer of properties → annual report
questions.explanation:
The sequence is:

• Section 17 — Schedule of Fees and Charges
• Section 18 — Compensation and Other Emoluments of Authority Personnel
• Section 19 — Transfer of Properties
• Section 20 — Annual Report

Memory hook: 17 FEES → 18 PAY → 19 PROPERTY → 20 REPORT.

Board tip: Sequential-section questions are dangerous because the choices often contain individually correct concepts arranged in the wrong order.

questions.question: A CAAP official argues that the Authority may revise its fee schedule twice within a three-year period because the statute merely recommends a three-year interval. Is the argument consistent with Section 17?
choices: Yes, because the three-year period is advisory only
Yes, provided the Board approves both revisions
No, because Section 17 establishes that revision shall not occur more often than once every three years
No, but only because fee revisions are completely prohibited
questions.answerText: No, because Section 17 establishes that revision shall not occur more often than once every three years
questions.explanation:
Section 17 is a statutory limitation, not merely a recommendation. The schedule of fees and fines shall not be revised more often than once every three years.

Memory hook: SHALL NOT = LEGAL LIMIT.

Board tip: Pay attention to mandatory statutory wording. A provision limiting administrative action cannot be treated as a mere suggestion.

questions.question: Which pair is CORRECTLY matched under Sections 17–20 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 20 concerns the annual report of the Authority. The other pairings shift the subjects of Sections 17–19.

Correct sequence:
• §17 — Schedule of fees and charges
• §18 — Compensation and other emoluments
• §19 — Transfer of properties
• §20 — Annual report

Memory hook: 17-18-19-20 = FEES-PAY-PROPERTY-REPORT.

questions.question: What is the principal subject identified for Section 21 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 21 is identified as "Policies."

The surrounding sections should be distinguished carefully:
• §20 — Annual Report
• §21 — Policies
• §22 — Powers and Functions
• §23 — Corporate Powers
• §24 — Powers of the Board

Memory hook: REPORT → POLICY → POWERS → CORPORATE → BOARD.

questions.question: Which section of RA 9497 immediately follows the provision on the Authority's policies and deals with its powers and functions?
questions.explanation:
Section 21 concerns Policies, while Section 22 concerns Powers and Functions.

Memory hook: 21 = POLICY; 22 = POWER.

Board tip: This is a sequential-number trap. The subject is straightforward, but the neighboring section numbers are deliberately close.

questions.question: Which of the following is the subject of Section 23 of RA 9497 rather than Section 22?
questions.explanation:
Section 23 is entitled "Corporate Powers," while Section 22 concerns the Authority's Powers and Functions.

Memory hook: §22 = WHAT IT DOES; §23 = CORPORATE POWERS.

Board tip: The words "powers and functions" and "corporate powers" look similar, but they belong to different sections.

questions.question: A question asks specifically for the provision dealing with the powers of the CAAP Board, not the general powers and functions of the Authority. Where should the examinee look?
questions.explanation:
Section 24 is identified as "Powers of the Board."

This distinction is important:
• Section 22 — Powers and Functions of the Authority
• Section 23 — Corporate Powers
• Section 24 — Powers of the Board

Memory hook: 22 AUTHORITY → 23 CORPORATE → 24 BOARD.

Board tip: A question can deliberately switch between the powers of the Authority and the powers of its Board. Read the subject carefully before choosing.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly identifies Sections 21, 22, 23, and 24 of RA 9497?
choices: Policies → Powers and Functions → Corporate Powers → Powers of the Board
Policies → Corporate Powers → Powers of the Board → Powers and Functions
Powers and Functions → Policies → Corporate Powers → Powers of the Board
Corporate Powers → Policies → Powers and Functions → Powers of the Board
questions.answerText: Policies → Powers and Functions → Corporate Powers → Powers of the Board
questions.explanation:
The statutory sequence identified in the source is:

• §21 — Policies
• §22 — Powers and Functions
• §23 — Corporate Powers
• §24 — Powers of the Board

Memory hook: POLICY → AUTHORITY → CORPORATE → BOARD.

Board tip: This is exactly the kind of neighboring-section sequence that can appear deceptively simple in a board examination.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT supported by the identified subjects of Sections 17–24 of RA 9497?
choices: Section 17 concerns the schedule of fees and charges
questions.explanation:
Section 24 concerns the Powers of the Board, not the annual budget. The annual budget is identified later under Section 30.

The sequence is:
• §17 — Fees and Charges
• §18 — Compensation and Emoluments
• §19 — Transfer of Properties
• §20 — Annual Report
• §21 — Policies
• §22 — Powers and Functions
• §23 — Corporate Powers
• §24 — Powers of the Board

Memory hook: 24 = BOARD, not BUDGET.

Board tip: This question uses a later-section concept as a distractor. Always verify the section number before answering.

questions.question: Under Section 25 of RA 9497, what is the principal authority granted to the Board concerning civil aviation regulation?
choices: To issue aircraft registration certificates exclusively
To determine the nationality of every aircraft
questions.explanation:
Section 25 concerns the issuance of rules and regulations by the Authority.

• The purpose is to establish regulatory requirements within the scope of the Authority's mandate.
• This should not be confused with Section 27, which deals specifically with rules of procedure and practice.

Memory hook: §25 = RULES; §27 = PROCEDURE.

Board tip: Both sections involve rules, but the statutory subjects are different.

questions.question: Which provision of RA 9497 specifically concerns the issuance of rules and regulations?
questions.explanation:
Section 25 is identified as "Issuance of Rules and Regulations."

Section 24 concerns the powers of the Board, while Section 27 concerns the issuance of rules of procedure and practice.

Memory hook: 24 = BOARD → 25 = RULES → 27 = PROCEDURE.

questions.question: A newly issued CAAP requirement establishes a general regulatory standard for civil aviation activities. Which statutory provision is most directly associated with the issuance of such rules and regulations?
questions.explanation:
Section 25 deals with the issuance of rules and regulations.

The question describes a general regulatory requirement rather than a procedural rule for conducting a particular hearing or proceeding.

Memory hook: GENERAL REGULATORY RULE = §25.

Board tip: If the question emphasizes "procedure and practice," think §27 instead.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 26 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 26 concerns the setting of charges and fees.

Do not confuse this with Section 17, which limits how frequently the schedule of fees and fines may be revised.

Memory hook: §17 = HOW OFTEN; §26 = SETTING CHARGES/FEES.

Board tip: Two sections can concern the same general subject while addressing different legal issues.

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes Section 17 from Section 26 of RA 9497?
choices: Section 17 concerns personnel compensation, while Section 26 concerns annual reports
Section 17 limits revision of the schedule of fees and fines, while Section 26 concerns setting charges and fees
Section 17 concerns appellate powers, while Section 26 concerns Board meetings
Section 17 concerns delegation, while Section 26 concerns annual budgeting
questions.answerText: Section 17 limits revision of the schedule of fees and fines, while Section 26 concerns setting charges and fees
questions.explanation:
Section 17 provides that the schedule of fees and fines shall not be revised more often than once every three years. Section 26 is separately identified as concerning the setting of charges and fees.

Memory hook: §17 = REVISION INTERVAL; §26 = SETTING.

Board tip: This is a classic distinction question. Similar words do not mean identical statutory subjects.

questions.question: Under Section 27 of RA 9497, what does the Authority issue specifically for the conduct of its proceedings?
questions.explanation:
Section 27 is specifically identified as "Issuance of Rules of Procedure and Practice."

These are distinct from the broader issuance of rules and regulations under Section 25.

Memory hook: §25 = REGULATORY RULES; §27 = PROCEDURE & PRACTICE.

Board tip: When the stem contains "procedure" or "practice," §27 should immediately stand out.

questions.question: Which phrase is most closely associated with Section 27 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 27 deals with the issuance of rules of procedure and practice.

The other choices correspond to different sections of RA 9497.

Memory hook: PROCEDURE = §27.

questions.question: A Board examination question asks for the section governing the Authority's appellate powers. What should be selected?
questions.explanation:
Section 28 is identified as "Appellate Powers."

Memory hook: §28 = APPEAL.

Board tip: Section 28 follows the provisions on rules, charges, and procedural rules, making section-number confusion a likely trap.

questions.question: What does the term "appellate powers" in Section 28 most directly indicate?
choices: The power to establish airport physical standards
The power associated with reviewing matters on appeal
The power to collect taxes from airlines
The power to appoint foreign airline executives
questions.answerText: The power associated with reviewing matters on appeal
questions.explanation:
Section 28 is specifically identified as concerning appellate powers. The essential concept is authority connected with appellate review.

Memory hook: APPELLATE = APPEAL/REVIEW.

Board tip: Do not confuse appellate authority with original regulatory authority. The word "appellate" signals review of a matter rather than simply making the initial regulation.

questions.question: Which section of RA 9497 grants the Authority the power to administer oaths?
questions.explanation:
Section 29 is identified as "Power to Administer Oaths."

Memory hook: §28 = APPEAL → §29 = OATH.

Board tip: The neighboring section numbers are easy to mix up, so memorize the sequence rather than isolated numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the principal subject of Section 29 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 29 concerns the power to administer oaths. Annual budgeting belongs to Section 30.

Memory hook: §29 = OATH; §30 = BUDGET.

Board tip: This is a neighboring-section trap. When two subjects appear consecutively, examiners can switch them deliberately.

questions.question: At what section does RA 9497 address the Authority's annual budget?
questions.explanation:
Section 30 is identified as "Annual Budget."

Memory hook: §29 = OATHS → §30 = BUDGET → §31 = DELEGATION.

Board tip: Memorizing the sequence makes these questions substantially easier.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly matches Sections 28, 29, and 30 of RA 9497?
choices: Appellate Powers → Power to Administer Oaths → Annual Budget
Annual Budget → Appellate Powers → Delegation of Functions
Power to Administer Oaths → Annual Budget → Appellate Powers
Delegation of Functions → Annual Budget → Power to Administer Oaths
questions.answerText: Appellate Powers → Power to Administer Oaths → Annual Budget
questions.explanation:
The sequence is:

• §28 — Appellate Powers
• §29 — Power to Administer Oaths
• §30 — Annual Budget

Memory hook: APPEAL → OATH → BUDGET.

Board tip: Sequence questions are useful because they test whether you actually know the organization of the statute rather than simply recognizing isolated terms.

questions.question: What is the principal subject of Section 31 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 31 is identified as "Delegation of Functions."

The concept concerns the delegation of functions within the Authority's statutory framework.

Memory hook: §30 = BUDGET → §31 = DELEGATE → §32 = LIMIT.

questions.question: A Director General assigns a particular function to another authorized official pursuant to the Authority's statutory framework. Which section is most directly associated with the subject of delegation?
questions.explanation:
Section 31 concerns delegation of functions.

The scenario describes the transfer or assignment of a function within the Authority's legal framework, making Section 31 the relevant provision.

Memory hook: DELEGATE = §31.

Board tip: Do not assume that every delegation is automatically valid. The existence of a delegation provision does not eliminate statutory limitations.

questions.question: Which section immediately follows the provision on delegation of functions and deals with limitation of powers?
questions.explanation:
Section 31 concerns Delegation of Functions, while Section 32 concerns Limitation of Powers.

Memory hook: §31 = DELEGATE → §32 = LIMIT.

Board tip: The two concepts logically relate to one another, which makes the section-number distinction especially testable.

questions.question: What is the principal subject of Section 32 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 32 is identified as "Limitation of Powers."

Memory hook: §31 = DELEGATION → §32 = LIMITATION.

Board tip: The word "powers" also appears in Sections 22–24, but Section 32 is specifically about limitations on those powers.

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes Section 24 from Section 32 of RA 9497?
choices: Section 24 concerns powers of the Board, while Section 32 concerns limitations of powers
Section 24 concerns annual budgeting, while Section 32 concerns personnel compensation
Section 24 concerns fees, while Section 32 concerns annual reports
Section 24 concerns appellate powers, while Section 32 concerns rules of procedure
questions.answerText: Section 24 concerns powers of the Board, while Section 32 concerns limitations of powers
questions.explanation:
Section 24 is identified as "Powers of the Board," whereas Section 32 is identified as "Limitation of Powers."

Memory hook: §24 = WHAT THE BOARD CAN DO; §32 = LIMITS ON POWERS.

Board tip: The repeated word "powers" is deliberate. Always identify whose powers and what aspect of those powers the question is asking about.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences is CORRECT for Sections 25 through 32 of RA 9497?
choices: Rules and Regulations → Charges and Fees → Rules of Procedure and Practice → Appellate Powers → Administer Oaths → Annual Budget → Delegation → Limitation
Rules and Regulations → Appellate Powers → Charges and Fees → Annual Budget → Delegation → Procedure → Oaths → Limitation
Charges and Fees → Rules and Regulations → Procedure → Appellate Powers → Annual Budget → Oaths → Delegation → Limitation
Rules of Procedure → Rules and Regulations → Charges and Fees → Oaths → Appellate Powers → Delegation → Budget → Limitation
questions.answerText: Rules and Regulations → Charges and Fees → Rules of Procedure and Practice → Appellate Powers → Administer Oaths → Annual Budget → Delegation → Limitation
questions.explanation:
The correct sequence is:

• §25 — Issuance of Rules and Regulations
• §26 — Setting of Charges and Fees
• §27 — Issuance of Rules of Procedure and Practice
• §28 — Appellate Powers
• §29 — Power to Administer Oaths
• §30 — Annual Budget
• §31 — Delegation of Functions
• §32 — Limitation of Powers

Memory hook: RULE → FEE → PROCEDURE → APPEAL → OATH → BUDGET → DELEGATE → LIMIT.

Board tip: This is a high-value memorization sequence because each section has a short, distinct subject.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST reason an examinee should distinguish Section 25 from Section 27?
choices: Both concern rules, but Section 25 concerns rules and regulations while Section 27 specifically concerns rules of procedure and practice
Section 25 concerns fees while Section 27 concerns taxes
Section 25 concerns appeals while Section 27 concerns oaths
Section 25 concerns budgeting while Section 27 concerns delegation
questions.answerText: Both concern rules, but Section 25 concerns rules and regulations while Section 27 specifically concerns rules of procedure and practice
questions.explanation:
Sections 25 and 27 are deliberately similar in wording but address different subjects.

• §25 — Issuance of Rules and Regulations
• §27 — Issuance of Rules of Procedure and Practice

Memory hook: GENERAL RULES = 25; PROCEDURAL RULES = 27.

Board tip: When two choices seem almost identical, look for the exact statutory qualifier. Here, "procedure and practice" is the key.

questions.question: Under Section 33 of RA 9497, who is responsible for drawing the organizational structure of the Authority?
choices: The Board, in consultation with the Director General
questions.answerText: The Board, in consultation with the Director General
questions.explanation:
Section 33 provides for the organizational structure of the Authority. The Board, in consultation with the Director General, draws the organizational structure of the Authority.

Memory hook: BOARD DRAWS + DG CONSULTED.

Board tip: The trap is choosing the Director General alone because the DG is the chief executive. Organizational structure, however, involves the Board acting in consultation with the DG.

questions.question: Within how many days from the appointment and acceptance of the Director General shall the organizational structure of the Authority be drawn under Section 33 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 33 provides that the organizational structure shall be drawn within fifteen (15) days from the appointment and acceptance of the Director General.

Memory hook: ORGANIZATION START = 15 DAYS.

Board tip: Do not confuse this with the six-month deadline associated with the final organizational structure.

questions.question: What is the latest period specified in Section 33 of RA 9497 for finalizing the organizational structure of the Authority?
choices: 30 days from appointment of the Board
Six months from the effectivity of the Act
One year from appointment of the Director General
questions.answerText: Six months from the effectivity of the Act
questions.explanation:
Section 33 provides a later deadline for the final organizational structure: it shall be finalized no later than six (6) months from the effectivity of the Act.

The provision therefore contains two important time references:
• Initial drawing: within 15 days from appointment and acceptance of the DG.
• Final structure: no later than 6 months from effectivity.

Memory hook: 15 DAYS → 6 MONTHS.

Board tip: This is a classic numerical trap because both periods belong to the same section.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a permanent office or service under the organizational structure of the Authority?
questions.explanation:
Section 33 identifies permanent offices within the Authority's organizational structure, including the Air Traffic Service.

The source also identifies:
• Air Navigation Service
• Aerodrome Development and Management Service
• Administrative and Finance Service

Memory hook: ATC → AIR NAV → AERODROME → ADMIN/FINANCE.

questions.question: How many permanent offices or services are specifically identified in the organizational structure listed under Section 33 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
The source identifies four permanent offices/services under Section 33:

1. Air Traffic Service
2. Air Navigation Service
3. Aerodrome Development and Management Service
4. Administrative and Finance Service

Memory hook: 4 CORE SERVICES.

Board tip: Do not count the Board or the Office of the Director General as one of these four listed permanent offices.

questions.question: Which service is NOT one of the four permanent offices identified under Section 33 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
The four permanent offices/services identified are Air Traffic Service, Air Navigation Service, Aerodrome Development and Management Service, and Administrative and Finance Service.

Aircraft Registration is associated with the aviation safety/registration functions addressed later in the Act, not with the four permanent offices listed in Section 33.

Memory hook: ATC + NAV + AERODROME + ADMIN/FINANCE.

questions.question: What is the principal subject of Section 34 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 34 concerns Training Schools.

Memory hook: §33 = ORGANIZATION → §34 = TRAINING.

Board tip: The section follows the organizational provisions, so it is easy to accidentally associate it with another administrative function.

questions.question: A question asks specifically about the statutory provision concerning training schools under RA 9497. Which section should be consulted?
questions.explanation:
Section 34 is identified as "Training Schools."

Memory hook: 34 = TRAINING.

Board tip: Section 35 concerns the powers and functions of the Director General, while Section 36 concerns the Office of Enforcement and Legal Service.

questions.question: Under Section 35 of RA 9497, the Director General serves as the:
choices: Chief executive and operating officer of the Authority
Chairman of the Congressional Oversight Committee
Chief Justice of the aviation regulatory system
Head of the Civil Aeronautics Board
questions.answerText: Chief executive and operating officer of the Authority
questions.explanation:
Section 35 identifies the Director General as the chief executive and operating officer of the Authority.

Memory hook: DG = CEO + COO.

Board tip: Do not confuse the Director General of CAAP with the Chairman of the CAAP Board or the Civil Aeronautics Board.

questions.question: Which description BEST distinguishes the Director General's position under Section 35 of RA 9497?
choices: He or she is merely an adviser to the Board
He or she is the chief executive and operating officer of the Authority
He or she serves only as the Authority's legal counsel
He or she serves only as head of aircraft registration
questions.answerText: He or she is the chief executive and operating officer of the Authority
questions.explanation:
Section 35 establishes the Director General as the chief executive and operating officer of the Authority.

This reflects the DG's central executive role in administering the Authority.

Memory hook: DG = EXECUTIVE + OPERATIONS.

Board tip: The Board exercises its statutory powers, while the DG serves as the Authority's chief executive and operating officer.

questions.question: What office is established under Section 36 of RA 9497 to implement the civil aviation regulatory, supervisory, and administrative mandates of the Director General?
choices: Office of Enforcement and Legal Service
questions.answerText: Office of Enforcement and Legal Service
questions.explanation:
Section 36 establishes the Office of Enforcement and Legal Service. It implements the civil aviation regulatory, supervisory, and administrative mandates of the Director General.

Memory hook: §36 = ENFORCEMENT + LEGAL.

Board tip: Do not confuse this office with the FSIS, which is concerned primarily with certification and ongoing inspections.
