CAB → not abolished by the Act.

🎯 Board Tip:
The ATO-versus-CAB distinction is one of the most important traps in this portion of RA 9497.

questions.question: Following the abolition of the ATO under RA 9497, where were the powers, duties, and rights exercised by the ATO transferred?
choices: To the Civil Aeronautics Board exclusively
questions.explanation:
The transitory provisions provide for the transfer of powers, duties, and rights vested by law in and exercised by the ATO to the Authority. The material also states that ATO assets, properties, funds, revenues, contracts, records, and documents are transferred to the Authority. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

💡 Memory Hook:
ATO OUT → CAAP IN.

🎯 Board Tip:
The important concept is continuity: abolition of the ATO did not mean that its functions simply disappeared.

questions.question: Under Section 86 of RA 9497, what is the principal subject of the provision?
choices: Transfer of personnel of the Air Transportation Office
questions.answerText: Transfer of personnel of the Air Transportation Office
questions.explanation:
Section 86 is specifically entitled 'Transfer of Personnel of Air Transportation Office.' It forms part of the transitory provisions following the abolition of the ATO.

💡 Memory Hook:
85 = ATO abolished.
86 = ATO personnel.

🎯 Board Tip:
The section numbers are consecutive for a reason. Think of Section 85 as the institutional change and Section 86 as the personnel consequence.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the relationship between Sections 85 and 86 of RA 9497?
choices: Section 85 abolishes the ATO, while Section 86 addresses the transfer of its personnel
Section 85 transfers personnel, while Section 86 abolishes the ATO
questions.answerText: Section 85 abolishes the ATO, while Section 86 addresses the transfer of its personnel
questions.explanation:
Sections 85 and 86 address connected transitory matters:

• §85 → Abolition of ATO.
• §86 → Transfer of ATO personnel.

💡 Memory Hook:
ABOLISH → TRANSFER.

🎯 Board Tip:
If the question asks about people, think Section 86. If it asks about the institution itself, think Section 85.

questions.question: For persons who availed themselves of the applicable retirement or resignation benefits under the transitory provisions, what reemployment restriction is identified in the material?
questions.explanation:
The material states that persons who availed themselves of the applicable benefits are subject to a prohibition on reemployment to the Authority within seven years from the date of retirement or resignation. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

💡 Memory Hook:
ATO transition → 7-year reemployment restriction.

🎯 Board Tip:
The number seven is easy to confuse with other statutory periods in RA 9497. Always connect the seven years specifically with this transitory reemployment restriction.

questions.question: What is the principal function of the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel under Section 89 of RA 9497?
choices: To act as the external legal counsel of the Authority
questions.answerText: To act as the external legal counsel of the Authority
questions.explanation:
Section 89 is the Legal Clause. It provides that the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel (OGCC) shall act as the external legal counsel of the Authority, without prejudice to deputation or designation involving the Authority's in-house counsel. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

💡 Memory Hook:
OGCC = External Legal Counsel.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse external legal counsel with the Authority's in-house counsels under the Office of Enforcement and Legal Service.

questions.question: Under Section 90 of RA 9497, within what period shall the implementing rules and regulations be issued?
questions.explanation:
Section 90 concerns the Implementing Rules and Regulations and provides for implementation of the provisions of the Act within sixty days from the date of its approval. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

💡 Memory Hook:
90 → 60 days.

🎯 Board Tip:
This is another statutory-number trap. Do not confuse the 60-day IRR period with the 15-day publication period associated with effectivity.

questions.question: Which body is established under Section 91 of RA 9497 for congressional oversight?
choices: Aircraft Accident Investigation and Inquiry Board
questions.explanation:
Section 91 establishes the Congressional Oversight Committee, referred to as the 'Committee.'

The provision places the Committee within the legislative oversight framework for implementation of RA 9497. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

💡 Memory Hook:
91 = Oversight.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the Congressional Oversight Committee with the CAAP Board or the AAI&IB. They serve entirely different functions.

questions.question: How long shall the Congressional Oversight Committee under Section 91 of RA 9497 remain in existence?
questions.explanation:
The material states that the Congressional Oversight Committee shall be in existence for five years. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

💡 Memory Hook:
91 → 5 years.

🎯 Board Tip:
Keep the major statutory periods separate:
• §84 → 4 years for inflation adjustment.
• §90 → 60 days for IRR.
• §91 → 5 years for oversight committee.
• §94 → 15 days for effectivity after publication.

questions.question: Who serves as members of the Congressional Oversight Committee under Section 91 of RA 9497?
choices: Only members of the CAAP Board
The Senate Committee on Public Services chair, the House Committee on Transportation chair, and four additional members from each House designated by the respective presiding officers
Only the President and the Director General
The Director General and the heads of CAAP offices
questions.answerText: The Senate Committee on Public Services chair, the House Committee on Transportation chair, and four additional members from each House designated by the respective presiding officers
questions.explanation:
Section 91 identifies the composition of the Congressional Oversight Committee as including the Chairmen of the Senate Committee on Public Services and House Committee on Transportation, plus four additional members from each House designated by the Senate President and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, respectively. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

💡 Memory Hook:
2 committee chairs + 4 Senate + 4 House.

🎯 Board Tip:
The phrase 'four additional members from each House' is the detail most likely to be overlooked.

questions.question: Which section contains the Separability Clause of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 92 is the Separability Clause.

A separability clause generally preserves the remaining provisions of an Act if a particular provision is declared invalid, subject to the language and legal effect of the statute.

💡 Memory Hook:
91 = Oversight.
92 = Separability.
93 = Repealing.
94 = Effectivity.

🎯 Board Tip:
The final four sections form a clean sequence worth memorizing.

questions.question: What is the subject of Section 93 of RA 9497?
questions.explanation:
Section 93 is the Repealing Clause of RA 9497.

The final sequence is:
§91 → Congressional Oversight Committee
§92 → Separability Clause
§93 → Repealing Clause
§94 → Effectivity

💡 Memory Hook:
OVERSIGHT → SEPARATE → REPEAL → EFFECT.

🎯 Board Tip:
Questions asking for the section immediately preceding effectivity are likely testing whether you remember Section 93.

questions.question: When does RA 9497 take effect under Section 94?
choices: Fifteen days after its complete publication in at least newspapers of general circulation
Sixty days after the issuance of the implementing rules
questions.answerText: Fifteen days after its complete publication in at least newspapers of general circulation
questions.explanation:
Section 94 provides that RA 9497 shall take effect fifteen days after its complete publication in at least newspapers of general circulation. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}

💡 Memory Hook:
94 → 15 days + complete publication.

🎯 Board Tip:
Do not confuse the 15-day effectivity period with the 60-day period for implementing rules under Section 90.

chapters/pcar-part-1.json.title: PCAR | Part 1 General Policies, Procedure and Definition

questions.question: What does the term SHALL mean in PCAR Part 1?
questions.explanation: SHALL indicates a mandatory requirement under PCAR regulations.

questions.question: Which term refers to a recommended practice in PCAR Part 1?
questions.explanation: SHOULD refers to a recommended practice.

questions.question: What does MAY indicate in PCAR Part 1?
questions.explanation: MAY means discretion can be used when performing an act.

questions.question: How often does the PCAR amendment cycle occur?
questions.explanation: The amendment cycle occurs every January and July.

questions.question: During which months are PCAR amendments normally issued?
questions.explanation: PCAR amendments are scheduled every January and July.

questions.question: Which document must be displayed in the aircraft cabin or flight deck entrance?
questions.explanation: The Certificate of Airworthiness must be displayed in the cabin or flight deck entrance.

questions.question: Which certificate must always be carried onboard the aircraft?
questions.explanation: The Certificate of Registration must always be carried onboard.

questions.question: Within how many days must a change of address be reported to the Authority?
questions.explanation: License holders must notify the Authority within 30 days.

questions.question: For how many days may a facsimile copy temporarily replace a lost license?

questions.question: Who may issue exemptions under PCAR Part 1?
questions.explanation: Only the Director General may issue exemptions.

questions.question: How many days in advance should exemption applications normally be submitted?
questions.explanation: Applications for exemptions should be submitted at least 60 days in advance.

questions.question: What is the minimum condition before granting an exemption?
choices: It is approved by the operator
It is not prejudicial to flight safety
questions.answerText: It is not prejudicial to flight safety
questions.explanation: Exemptions may only be granted if flight safety is not compromised.

questions.question: Which MEL category allows a 10-day deferral?

questions.question: Which MEL category allows the longest deferral period?
questions.explanation: Category D items may be deferred for up to 120 days.

questions.question: What is the deferral period for MEL Category D?
questions.explanation: Category D MEL items may be deferred for 120 days.

questions.question: When an approved MEL authorizes an operator extension for an eligible Category B or C item, what notification is required?

questions.question: Who may approve an eligible Category B or C MEL repair-interval extension when the approved MEL grants continuing authority?
choices: The Quality Department in all cases
questions.explanation: The approved MEL can authorize the operator to exercise continuing approval for eligible Category B/C extensions, with CAAP notification within 24 hours. The reviewer does not set a first/second-extension hierarchy. Basis: supplied AIRLAWS summary, p. 6; CAAP AC 08-017.

questions.question: Which term means approved by or on behalf of Civil Aviation?
questions.explanation: Approved means approved by or on behalf of Civil Aviation.

questions.question: Which document confirms maintenance was completed according to standards?

questions.question: According to PCAR Part 1, what is a NOTAM?
choices: A telecommunicated notice with timely information essential to flight operations
A maintenance release issued after each flight
A weather forecast valid for 24 hours
questions.answerText: A telecommunicated notice with timely information essential to flight operations
questions.explanation: Part 1 defines a NOTAM as a notice distributed by telecommunication containing timely information essential to flight operations. The reviewer also shows “Notice to Airmen” as the expansion. Basis: supplied AIRLAWS summary, p. 6.

questions.question: Which aircraft has priority over all others?

questions.question: Which aircraft category derives lift mainly from fixed surfaces?

questions.question: What administrative action confirms corrective actions taken?

questions.question: How soon must a change of address be reported?
