A correctly aligned ring gap always indicates a worn or defective ring.
The rings will not be seated.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Ring gaps aligned at one instant have little or no effect on a differential-pressure compression check because the rings rotate in service and the test measures overall cylinder leakage.

**Engineering principle**
A leak-down result is interpreted by listening at the intake, exhaust, and crankcase; one ring-gap position is not by itself a defect.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Gap alignment is not a reliable diagnosis.

**Memory hook**
Gap alignment is not a reliable diagnosis.

**Board tip**
Listen for leakage location and compare the pressure drop with service limits.

chapters/reciprocating-induction-carbure.title: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: If fuel/air ratio is proper and ignition timing is correct, the combustion process should be completed
choices: When the exhaust valve opens at the end of the power stroke.
Before top center on the compression stroke.
Just after top center at the beginning of the power stroke.
20 to 30° before top center at the end of the compression stroke.
questions.answerText: Just after top center at the beginning of the power stroke.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Ignition begins before top dead center so the flame has time to develop while the piston is near the end of compression. Peak pressure then occurs just after TDC, when it can push the piston down through the power stroke. Ignition timing is not the same instant as completed combustion.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: When is the fuel/air mixture ignited in a conventional reciprocating engine?
choices: When the piston reaches top dead center on the compression stroke.
After the piston passes top dead center on the power stroke.
When the piston has reached top dead center of the intake stroke.
Shortly before the piston reaches the top of the compression stroke.
questions.answerText: Shortly before the piston reaches the top of the compression stroke.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The spark is timed shortly before TDC on the compression stroke. The burning mixture takes finite time to reach peak pressure, so starting combustion before TDC places peak pressure just after TDC for useful expansion work.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: The primary purpose in setting proper valve timing and overlap is to
choices: obtain the best volumetric efficiency and lower cylinder operating temperatures.
Eliminate the need to coordinate ignition timing with valve movement.
Permit the best possible charge of fuel/air mixture into the cylinders.
Gain more thorough exhaust gas scavenging.
questions.answerText: obtain the best volumetric efficiency and lower cylinder operating temperatures.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Correct valve timing lets the intake charge continue filling the cylinder and helps clear hot exhaust gas during overlap. Better volumetric efficiency improves charge mass, while effective scavenging reduces retained hot gas and cylinder temperature. Excessive overlap or mistiming can instead cause reversion.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Into what part of a reciprocating engine induction system is deicing alcohol normally injected?
choices: Into the fuel bowl downstream of the throttle plate.
The airstream ahead of the carburetor.
The low-pressure area ahead of the throttle valve.
questions.answerText: The airstream ahead of the carburetor.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Alcohol is injected into the airstream ahead of the carburetor so it can reach the inlet and carburetor passages where ice may form. The alcohol lowers water's freezing point; it is not sprayed into the cylinders as a combustion additive.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: During full power output of an unsupercharged engine equipped with a float-type carburetor, in which of the following areas will the highest pressure exist?
choices: Downstream of the throttle valve in the intake manifold.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
In a normally aspirated induction system at full power, the carburetor air scoop is exposed to ram pressure and is upstream of the pressure drop across the carburetor venturi and throttle. Thus it has the highest pressure among the listed locations.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Augmenter tubes are part of which reciprocating engine system?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Augmenter tubes use the high-velocity exhaust flow to induce additional cooling air through the engine compartment. They are part of the exhaust arrangement and use an ejector effect; they are not fuel-metering tubes.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Which of the following assists in removing heat from the metal walls and fins of an air-cooled cylinder assembly?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Baffles and the cowling direct cooling air across cylinder fins instead of letting it bypass the hot surfaces. The metal fins increase heat-transfer area, and forced airflow carries heat away. A missing or poorly sealed baffle can cause localized overheating.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: If the intake valve is opened too early in the cycle of operation of a four-stroke cycle engine, it may result in
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
If the intake valve opens too early while cylinder pressure is still high, combustion gases can escape backward into the induction passage. Correct valve timing keeps the intake event coordinated with piston motion and exhaust pressure.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the purpose of a power check on a reciprocating engine?
choices: To determine if the fuel/air mixture is adequate.
To determine whether the engine develops its specified power under the test conditions.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A power check compares the engine's measured indications and output with specified performance limits. It can reveal inadequate power or abnormal operation, but it is a performance assessment rather than a single-component diagnosis.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Backfiring through the carburetor generally results from the use of _____.
choices: equal amount of fuel and air
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A lean mixture can burn slowly and irregularly; flame may continue into the intake event and ignite mixture in the induction passage, causing backfire. A rich mixture more commonly causes roughness, fouling, or reduced power.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: The following are the major components of a normally aspirated engine except _____.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The listed major engine systems include induction, fuel metering, ignition, lubrication, cooling, and exhaust. An ice-removal system is an accessory or installation feature, not a fundamental engine component system present on every reciprocating engine.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: A fuel ratio of 11:1 normally refers to _____.
choices: 1 part of fuel, 11 parts of air
1.1 part of fuel, 1 part of air
questions.answerText: 1 part of fuel, 11 parts of air
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A ratio written fuel-to-air as 11:1 means one unit of fuel for eleven units of air. Always read which material is named first; reversing the order changes the mixture interpretation.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Reciprocating engine power will be decreased at all altitudes if _____.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Higher humidity means more water vapor occupies part of the inducted gas mixture, displacing some oxygen for a given volume. With less oxygen available for combustion, power decreases, particularly in a normally aspirated engine.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: The device that controls the volume of the fuel/air mixture to the cylinders is called a _____.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The throttle valve regulates the amount of mixture or air admitted to the engine and therefore controls power. The mixture control changes fuel-to-air proportion; it is not the primary airflow-volume control.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: How does a float-type carburetor normally meter fuel into the airstream?
choices: Fuel drains by gravity into the exhaust
A pressure difference draws fuel from a metering discharge nozzle
A high-pressure injector sprays fuel at each spark plug
questions.answerText: A pressure difference draws fuel from a metering discharge nozzle
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Fuel flows from the float chamber through a metering path because pressure at the discharge nozzle is lower than the fuel supply pressure. The pressure difference draws and atomizes fuel into the moving airstream; the float maintains a nearly constant fuel level.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the purpose of the carburetor venturi?
choices: Increase local air velocity and lower static pressure to promote fuel discharge
Heat the fuel above its boiling point
questions.answerText: Increase local air velocity and lower static pressure to promote fuel discharge
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The venturi narrows the passage, increasing airflow velocity and lowering local static pressure. That pressure drop helps draw fuel through the discharge nozzle. It does not raise pressure to force fuel into the airstream.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Why is mixture leaned as altitude increases in a carbureted engine?
choices: Air density decreases, so less fuel is needed to maintain the proper mixture
questions.answerText: Air density decreases, so less fuel is needed to maintain the proper mixture
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
As altitude increases, air density and oxygen mass per intake volume decrease. The same fuel flow would make the mixture too rich, so the pilot reduces fuel with the mixture control to preserve the proper fuel-air ratio.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the function of an accelerator pump in a carburetor?
choices: Temporarily enrich the mixture when the throttle is opened rapidly
questions.answerText: Temporarily enrich the mixture when the throttle is opened rapidly
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Rapid throttle opening increases airflow immediately, while fuel delivery may lag. The accelerator pump supplies a brief extra shot of fuel to prevent a transient lean stumble; it is not the normal steady-state metering circuit.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What does a carburetor economizer or power-enrichment system do at high power?
choices: Adds fuel to provide the richer mixture required for high-power operation
questions.answerText: Adds fuel to provide the richer mixture required for high-power operation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
At high power the engine needs a richer mixture for detonation margin and cooling. The economizer or power-enrichment circuit adds fuel when the throttle reaches the high-power region; it does not lean the mixture for cruise.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the purpose of an idle system in a carburetor?
choices: Meter fuel when airflow through the main venturi is too low for normal main-nozzle operation
questions.answerText: Meter fuel when airflow through the main venturi is too low for normal main-nozzle operation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
At idle, airflow through the main venturi is too small to create enough pressure drop for the main discharge nozzle. The idle circuit supplies metered fuel through ports near the throttle plate, where local pressure conditions support flow.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is a common effect of carburetor icing?
choices: A gradual loss of power and possible roughness as ice restricts airflow
questions.answerText: A gradual loss of power and possible roughness as ice restricts airflow
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Ice can form in the carburetor throat as pressure and temperature fall during fuel vaporization. Accumulating ice restricts airflow and may cause gradual RPM or manifold-pressure loss and roughness. Carburetor heat warms the inlet air to melt or prevent this ice.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Why does carburetor heat usually reduce engine power when applied?
choices: Heated air is less dense and may also bypass the normal intake path
questions.answerText: Heated air is less dense and may also bypass the normal intake path
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Heated induction air has lower density, so each cylinder receives less oxygen mass at a given volume. Carburetor heat can also add intake restriction. The immediate power reduction is expected and is distinct from the power recovery after ice melts.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: In a pressure-injection carburetor, what provides the pressure for fuel delivery?
choices: A fuel pump and metering unit
Only gravity in a float bowl
questions.answerText: A fuel pump and metering unit
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A pressure-injection carburetor uses a pump and metering unit to pressurize and regulate fuel delivery. Fuel flow is controlled by pressure differentials and metering components rather than being drawn solely from a float-bowl level.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: An air-to-fuel mass ratio of 12:1 means what?
choices: Twelve units of pressure per fuel unit
Twelve parts air by mass for one part fuel by mass
Twelve parts fuel by mass for one part air
questions.answerText: Twelve parts air by mass for one part fuel by mass
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An air-to-fuel mass ratio of 12:1 specifies twelve units of air mass for each one unit of fuel mass. It is a mass ratio, not a volume ratio, and the order is air first, fuel second.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an intake manifold?
choices: Distribute the combustible charge to the engine cylinders
questions.answerText: Distribute the combustible charge to the engine cylinders
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The intake manifold carries and distributes the combustible charge from the carburetor or fuel-metering system to individual cylinders. Unequal distribution can produce different cylinder mixtures and temperatures.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What can an induction leak downstream of a carburetor cause?
choices: A lower compression ratio by design
An excessively lean mixture and uneven cylinder operation
An enriched mixture in all cases
questions.answerText: An excessively lean mixture and uneven cylinder operation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A leak downstream of the carburetor admits unmetered air. Since the fuel system does not add fuel for that extra air, the affected cylinders run lean and may operate unevenly, especially at idle.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: How does a fuel-injection system differ from a float carburetor at the cylinder?
choices: It meters oil instead of fuel
Fuel is metered under pressure and distributed through injector nozzles
Fuel is mixed only in a float bowl
questions.answerText: Fuel is metered under pressure and distributed through injector nozzles
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Fuel injection meters fuel under pressure and routes it through injector nozzles near the intake ports or cylinders. A float carburetor meters fuel into the common airflow using venturi pressure changes and a float-controlled supply.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Why are alternate-air doors provided on some induction systems?
choices: Provide an alternate source of induction air if the normal inlet is obstructed
questions.answerText: Provide an alternate source of induction air if the normal inlet is obstructed
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An alternate-air door lets the engine draw air from another source if the normal inlet or filter is blocked. The alternate path preserves airflow but may be unfiltered or warmer, depending on the installation.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: What is the effect of a restricted air filter on a normally aspirated engine?
choices: Reduced induction airflow and available power
Higher volumetric efficiency in all conditions
questions.answerText: Reduced induction airflow and available power
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A restricted filter limits the mass of air entering a normally aspirated engine. Less oxygen is available to burn fuel, reducing maximum power; a sufficiently severe restriction may also cause rough operation.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Why is fuel vaporization important before combustion?
choices: It helps produce a combustible mixture that can burn consistently
It prevents the fuel from mixing with air
It raises the engine’s mechanical compression ratio
It removes the need for ignition
questions.answerText: It helps produce a combustible mixture that can burn consistently
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Fuel must be atomized and vaporized sufficiently to mix with air and burn steadily. Poor vaporization can cause uneven distribution, incomplete combustion, and difficulty operating, especially during cold conditions.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: During a bench test, an engine receives 900 lb of air per hour and 75 lb of fuel per hour. What is the air-to-fuel mass ratio?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Air-to-fuel mass ratio = air mass flow / fuel mass flow = 900 lb/hr / 75 lb/hr = 12. The hourly units cancel, so the ratio is 12:1 by mass.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: An engine requires an air-to-fuel mass ratio of 15:1. If air flow is 1,200 lb/hr, what fuel flow is required?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
For an air-to-fuel ratio of 15:1, fuel flow = air flow / 15 = 1,200 lb/hr / 15 = 80 lb/hr. Check: 15 x 80 = 1,200 lb/hr of air.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: A test cell measures 180 kg/hr of air and 15 kg/hr of fuel. Find the air-to-fuel ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Air-to-fuel mass ratio = 180 kg/hr / 15 kg/hr = 12. The flow units cancel; this means 12 kg of air per kilogram of fuel.
tags: Reciprocating Induction, Carburetion, and Fuel Metering

questions.question: Which of the following will decrease volumetric efficiency in a reciprocating engine? 1. Full throttle operation. 2. Low cylinder head temperatures. 3. Improper valve timing. 4. Sharp bends in the induction system. 5. High carburetor air temperatures.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Improper valve timing and sharp induction bends reduce the volume of fresh charge reaching the cylinders. High carburetor-air temperature lowers air density, also reducing inducted mass. Wide-open throttle and a cooler cylinder head generally support, rather than reduce, volumetric efficiency in the conditions assumed by this question.

questions.question: The five events of a four-stroke cycle engine in the order of their occurrence are
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A four-stroke piston engine proceeds through intake, compression, power, and exhaust strokes. Ignition is timed during compression shortly before top dead center; it is not itself a separate piston stroke, even though exam shorthand may list it as an event.

questions.question: Cam-ground pistons are installed in some aircraft engines to
choices: equalize the wear on all pistons.
provide a better fit at operating temperatures.
act as a compensating feature so that a compensated magneto is not required.
questions.answerText: provide a better fit at operating temperatures.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A cam-ground piston is intentionally machined slightly out-of-round and tapered when cold. Because different areas expand differently as they heat, the piston approaches a more nearly cylindrical shape with suitable running clearance at operating temperature.

**Engineering principle**
Cold shape compensates for thermal growth; the goal is proper hot clearance rather than a perfect cold circle.

💡 **Memory hook:** Machined oval cold, fitted round hot.

🎯 **Board tip:** Relate the machining shape to temperature-dependent expansion.

questions.question: How many of the following are factors in establishing the maximum compression ratio limitations of an aircraft engine? 1. Detonation characteristics of the fuel used. 2. Design limitations of the engine. 3. Degree of supercharging. 4. Spark plug reach.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The compression-ratio limit depends on fuel detonation resistance, engine design and cooling, and induction pressure from supercharging. Spark-plug reach does not establish the allowable compression ratio.

**Engineering principle**
Higher compression or boost raises end-of-compression temperature and pressure, increasing detonation risk; fuel grade and engine design set the permitted limits.

**Memory hook:** Compression limit follows knock resistance and engine design.

**Board tip:** Count only listed factors that affect combustion pressure or engine capability.

questions.question: Engine ignition system belongs to ATA Chapter _____.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
In the ATA chapter numbering system used by the question, engine ignition is Chapter 74. ATA chapter numbers classify aircraft systems for documentation and maintenance; they do not describe the operating sequence.

questions.question: A rocket engine is a powerplant, self-contained, which depends _____.
choices: on the oxidizer and fuel for operation
on the ignition system installed, as necessary, for operation
questions.answerText: on the oxidizer and fuel for operation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A rocket carries both fuel and oxidizer, so combustion does not depend on oxygen in the surrounding atmosphere. This permits operation in space, unlike an air-breathing jet engine.

**Engineering principle**
Air-breathing engines ingest atmospheric oxygen; rockets carry their oxidizer as part of the propellant system.

💡 **Memory hook:** Rocket brings its oxygen.

🎯 **Board tip:** Identify whether the engine depends on ambient air.

questions.question: Why can a magneto continue producing ignition with the aircraft battery switch off?
choices: It generates ignition energy from engine rotation
It is powered by the cabin lighting circuit
It uses exhaust heat to make a spark
questions.answerText: It generates ignition energy from engine rotation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A magneto is mechanically driven by the engine and generates its own electrical energy. The aircraft battery switch therefore does not normally disable magneto ignition; the magneto is stopped by grounding its primary circuit.

questions.question: What does grounding a magneto primary circuit do?
choices: Stops the magneto from producing a spark
questions.answerText: Stops the magneto from producing a spark
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Grounding the magneto primary circuit collapses the primary magnetic field and prevents the secondary winding from producing ignition voltage, stopping the spark.

**Engineering principle**
The magneto generates its own ignition energy; the P-lead stops it by grounding the primary circuit.

**Memory hook:** Ground the P-lead; kill the spark.

**Board tip:** A disconnected P-lead can leave the magneto live, so follow safe grounding procedures.

questions.question: Why are two independent magnetos commonly used on aircraft piston engines?
choices: Provide ignition redundancy and improve combustion with two spark plugs
Eliminate the need for a battery
questions.answerText: Provide ignition redundancy and improve combustion with two spark plugs
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Two independent magnetos provide redundancy: if one fails, the other can continue ignition. Two plugs per cylinder also initiate flame propagation at two points, supporting smoother and more complete combustion.

**Engineering principle**
Each magneto supplies a separate ignition circuit and ordinarily fires one of the two plugs in each cylinder.

**Memory hook:** Two mags, two spark paths.

**Board tip:** Redundancy and combustion quality are both reasons for dual ignition.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an impulse coupling on a magneto?
choices: Spin the magneto faster during starting and retard the spark for easier starting
questions.answerText: Spin the magneto faster during starting and retard the spark for easier starting
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An impulse coupling temporarily winds and releases a spring to spin the magneto faster during cranking, producing a hotter starting spark. It also retards spark timing to reduce kickback; it disengages once the engine runs.

questions.question: What does a high-tension ignition lead carry?
choices: Engine oil to a rocker arm
High voltage from the magneto distributor to a spark plug
questions.answerText: High voltage from the magneto distributor to a spark plug
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A high-tension ignition lead carries the magneto distributor's high voltage to the spark plug. Its insulation contains the voltage so it does not leak to ground or adjacent conductors.

**Engineering principle**
The primary circuit is low voltage; the magneto secondary circuit and ignition leads carry the high-voltage pulse.

**Memory hook:** High-tension lead = high voltage to the plug.

**Board tip:** Trace the path from magneto distributor to cylinder spark plug.

questions.question: Why is a magneto drop check performed during an engine run-up?
choices: Check operation of each ignition system independently
questions.answerText: Check operation of each ignition system independently
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A magneto drop check briefly selects each ignition system separately during run-up. A normal RPM drop shows that the selected system was contributing and that the other remains capable of firing; excessive drop or roughness requires troubleshooting.

questions.question: What does spark-plug fouling commonly cause?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A fouled plug cannot reliably bridge its electrodes with a spark, so that cylinder may misfire and the engine may run rough. Deposits can shunt current across the insulator nose or obstruct the spark gap.

**Engineering principle**
Fouling is different from incorrect ignition timing or a failed magneto; inspect the plug and cylinder condition to identify the cause.

**Memory hook:** Fouled gap, weak or missing spark.

**Board tip:** Use approved cleaning and service limits before returning a plug to service.

questions.question: Why are aircraft spark plugs often installed with specified reach and gasket requirements?
choices: Ensure correct electrode position, heat transfer, and thread engagement
questions.answerText: Ensure correct electrode position, heat transfer, and thread engagement
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Specified spark-plug reach places the electrodes at the designed position in the combustion chamber. Correct gasket and thread engagement also support heat transfer and avoid damaging the head.

**Engineering principle**
A plug that is too long can contact the piston or valves; one that is too short can impair ignition and heat transfer.

**Memory hook:** Correct reach puts the spark where designed.

**Board tip:** Match plug reach, gasket, heat range, and thread to the engine data.

questions.question: What is the function of the starter motor?
choices: Rotate the engine through initial cycles until it can run independently
questions.answerText: Rotate the engine through initial cycles until it can run independently
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The starter motor turns the engine through the initial cycles until combustion can sustain operation. After the engine accelerates beyond starter speed, the starter disengages to prevent damage.

questions.question: Why is a starter relay or contactor used?
choices: Allow a low-current control circuit to switch high starter current
questions.answerText: Allow a low-current control circuit to switch high starter current
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A starter contactor lets a low-current switch circuit control the much larger current required by the starter motor. This protects cockpit wiring and provides a controlled high-current path.

questions.question: What does a generator or alternator do after the engine starts?
choices: Supplies electrical power and recharges the battery
Creates the magneto spark in all systems
questions.answerText: Supplies electrical power and recharges the battery
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
After start, a generator or alternator supplies the electrical loads and replenishes battery charge. The battery provides stored energy and usually supports starting; the charging source supports operation once driven.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a voltage regulator?
choices: Maintain generator or alternator output voltage within the system range
questions.answerText: Maintain generator or alternator output voltage within the system range
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A voltage regulator controls generator or alternator field output to keep bus voltage within the system's allowable range as engine speed and electrical load vary. It regulates voltage rather than directly regulating battery capacity.

questions.question: Why should ignition leads be routed and clamped correctly?
choices: Prevent chafing, cross-firing, and electrical interference
questions.answerText: Prevent chafing, cross-firing, and electrical interference
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Correct routing and clamping prevent ignition leads from chafing, contacting hot parts, or coupling high-voltage pulses into other wiring. Poor insulation or separation can cause leakage, crossfire, radio interference, or misfire.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a starter-generator?
choices: Combine engine-starting and electrical-generation functions in one machine
Combine fuel pump and oil cooler functions
questions.answerText: Combine engine-starting and electrical-generation functions in one machine
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A starter-generator combines a motor function for engine starting with a generator function after the engine is running. One unit serves both roles, subject to the aircraft system's switching and control design.

questions.question: What is the likely effect of incorrect ignition timing that is too advanced?
choices: The engine becomes a two-stroke cycle
Combustion pressure rises too early and can cause roughness or damaging stress
questions.answerText: Combustion pressure rises too early and can cause roughness or damaging stress
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
If ignition is too advanced, combustion pressure rises while the piston is still approaching top dead center. This opposes the piston, increases temperature and mechanical stress, and can promote detonation or rough operation.

questions.question: Why are ignition timing checks made at the specified crankshaft position?
choices: The spark must occur at the prescribed point relative to piston position
The timing mark sets oil temperature
It sets the propeller blade track
questions.answerText: The spark must occur at the prescribed point relative to piston position
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Ignition timing is specified relative to crankshaft position so the spark occurs at the intended point in the compression stroke. The correct timing supports combustion pressure at the proper point in piston travel.

**Engineering principle**
Timing too early can promote detonation or kickback; timing too late reduces power and can increase exhaust temperature.

**Memory hook:** Spark timing is referenced to piston position.

**Board tip:** Set and verify timing using the manufacturer's crankshaft marks and procedure.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a capacitor in a magneto primary circuit?
choices: Reduce arcing across breaker points and help collapse the magnetic field rapidly
questions.answerText: Reduce arcing across breaker points and help collapse the magnetic field rapidly
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The capacitor across magneto breaker points limits arcing as the points open and helps the primary magnetic field collapse rapidly. The rapid field change induces the high voltage needed for a strong spark.

questions.question: What does a dual-bus electrical architecture help provide?
choices: Separate distribution paths and improved continuity for essential loads
questions.answerText: Separate distribution paths and improved continuity for essential loads
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Separate electrical buses provide alternate distribution paths, helping preserve selected essential loads if one bus is isolated or faulted.

**Engineering principle**
Redundancy works only when feeds, protection, and transfer paths avoid a shared single point of failure.

**Memory hook:** Two paths can preserve essential power.

**Board tip:** Trace bus ties and sources on the aircraft wiring diagram.

questions.question: Why must a magneto be checked for proper grounding during shutdown?
choices: A failed P-lead can leave the magneto live and the propeller capable of starting the engine
questions.answerText: A failed P-lead can leave the magneto live and the propeller capable of starting the engine
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The magneto P-lead grounds the primary circuit when the ignition switch is OFF. If the lead or switch fails open, the magneto can remain live and a propeller movement can start the engine, so shutdown grounding is safety-critical.

questions.question: What is the role of a spark plug’s insulator nose?
choices: Electrically isolate the center electrode from the shell
questions.answerText: Electrically isolate the center electrode from the shell
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The spark-plug insulator electrically separates the center electrode from the grounded shell while exposing the electrode tip in the combustion chamber.

**Engineering principle**
The insulator also transfers heat from the firing end according to the plug heat range; it must remain free of cracks and conductive deposits.

**Memory hook:** Insulator keeps the spark path across the gap.

**Board tip:** Distinguish electrical insulation from heat-range function.

questions.question: Why does a turbine ignition exciter store electrical energy before firing?
choices: Produce a high-energy ignition pulse for starting
questions.answerText: Produce a high-energy ignition pulse for starting
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A turbine ignition exciter stores electrical energy and releases it as a high-energy pulse to the igniter. This supports reliable ignition during starting or relight despite the high pressure and airflow environment.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an igniter plug in a turbine engine?
choices: Provide ignition during starting or relight when commanded
Continuously ignite every gas molecule in normal operation
questions.answerText: Provide ignition during starting or relight when commanded
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An igniter plug provides the spark that lights the fuel-air mixture during turbine starting or a commanded relight. Unlike a piston spark plug, it is usually not firing continuously throughout normal turbine operation.

questions.question: Why are aircraft batteries rated for both capacity and discharge capability?
choices: Loads need stored energy over time and sufficient current for high-demand events
questions.answerText: Loads need stored energy over time and sufficient current for high-demand events
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Thermodynamic questions depend on the system boundary, process constraint, and sign convention. Apply conservation of energy and the ideal-gas/process relation that matches the stated condition; use absolute temperature and absolute pressure in gas-law ratios.

**Engineering principle**
Adiabatic means no heat transfer; isentropic additionally requires reversibility. Specific heat at constant pressure differs from constant volume, and work done by a system has the opposite sign from work done on it.

💡 **Memory hook:** Name the process before choosing the equation.

🎯 **Board tip:** Check absolute versus gauge pressure and state the work sign convention.

questions.question: What is the function of a circuit breaker in an aircraft powerplant electrical circuit?
choices: Interrupt excessive current to protect wiring and equipment
questions.answerText: Interrupt excessive current to protect wiring and equipment
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A circuit breaker opens the circuit when current exceeds its protective rating, limiting wire and equipment overheating. It should not be repeatedly reset when it trips; the cause of the overcurrent must be found.

**Engineering principle**
A breaker protects wiring from excessive current; a switch only commands normal operation.

💡 **Memory hook:** Trip protects the wire.

🎯 **Board tip:** Never use a breaker as a routine switch or defeat its rating.

questions.question: Why should spark-plug leads be tested for insulation breakdown?
choices: Leakage can divert high voltage and weaken or prevent the spark
It changes the engine’s compression ratio
questions.answerText: Leakage can divert high voltage and weaken or prevent the spark
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Testing ignition leads for insulation breakdown finds paths where high voltage can leak to ground instead of reaching the spark plug. Leakage weakens or prevents the spark and can cause misfiring.

**Engineering principle**
The ignition lead must contain the secondary voltage along its full length; damaged insulation creates an alternate current path.

**Memory hook:** Leaking voltage means a weaker spark.

**Board tip:** Inspect routing, terminals, and insulation using the approved test method.

questions.question: How are the piston pins of most aircraft engines lubricated?
choices: By the action of the oil control ring and the series of holes drilled in the ring groove directing oil to the pin and piston pin boss.
By the scavenge pump sending return oil through the piston pin.
By pressure oil through a drilled passageway in the heavy web portion of the connecting rod.
By oil which is sprayed or thrown by the master or connecting rods.
questions.answerText: By oil which is sprayed or thrown by the master or connecting rods.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Pressure oil splashed or thrown by the master or connecting rods reaches the piston-pin bearing surfaces. The motion of the crankshaft and rods distributes oil without a separate pressure line to every pin.

**Engineering principle**
This splash system depends on correct oil quantity and moving parts; it differs from a dedicated pressure-fed bearing.

**Memory hook**
Follow the path from oil source to pin.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: If the oil pressure gauge fluctuates over a wide range from zero to normal operating pressure, the most likely cause is.
choices: broken or weak pressure relief valve spring.
air lock in the scavenge pump intake.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A wide swing from zero to normal pressure is consistent with a pickup intermittently uncovering as oil sloshes, especially when the supply is low.

**Engineering principle**
The gauge reports pressure at its sender, not the amount of oil remaining; a fluctuating indication requires the approved procedure.

**Memory hook**
Erratic pressure can point to an uncovered pickup.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What are the main functions of engine lubricating oil?
choices: Reduce friction and wear, carry heat, and help clean and protect internal parts
questions.answerText: Reduce friction and wear, carry heat, and help clean and protect internal parts
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Engine oil forms a lubricating film, reduces friction and wear, carries heat away, suspends or transports contaminants, and protects metal surfaces.

**Engineering principle**
The oil system supports several functions at once; a pressure indication alone does not prove that all are being met.

**Memory hook**
Oil lubricates, cools, cleans, and protects.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is a principal difference between wet-sump and dry-sump systems?
choices: A dry-sump system stores most oil in a separate tank
A wet sump has no oil pump
A dry sump has no scavenge pump
A wet sump stores oil only in a remote tank
questions.answerText: A dry-sump system stores most oil in a separate tank
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A wet-sump engine stores most of its oil in the engine crankcase or sump. A dry-sump system stores most oil in a separate tank.

**Engineering principle**
A dry-sump system uses pressure and scavenge stages and can keep the engine sump shallow.

**Memory hook**
Wet sump: oil in engine; dry sump: oil in tank.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a scavenge pump in a dry-sump system?
choices: Return oil from the engine sump to the external tank
questions.answerText: Return oil from the engine sump to the external tank
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The scavenge pump removes oil collected in the engine sump and returns it to the remote tank.

**Engineering principle**
Dry-sump systems commonly scavenge at a greater capacity than the pressure pump to prevent oil accumulating in the case.

**Memory hook**
Pressure pump sends oil out; scavenge pump brings it back.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why can a dry-sump system use a larger oil supply than the engine sump alone?
choices: It eliminates the need for lubrication
The oil is consumed during every stroke
A remote tank can hold the required quantity while the sump remains shallow
questions.answerText: A remote tank can hold the required quantity while the sump remains shallow
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A remote tank can carry the required oil quantity while the engine sump remains shallow, helping prevent oil starvation during aircraft attitudes and maneuvers.

**Engineering principle**
The external reservoir separates storage capacity from the crankcase volume.

**Memory hook**
Dry sump separates storage from collection.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What does an oil pressure relief valve do?
choices: Limit maximum system pressure by bypassing excess pump output
questions.answerText: Limit maximum system pressure by bypassing excess pump output
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The pressure-relief valve limits maximum system pressure by diverting excess pump output when pressure reaches its setting.

**Engineering principle**
It protects the system from excessive pressure; it does not regulate engine oil temperature or guarantee adequate pressure if stuck open.

**Memory hook**
Relief valve limits the high side.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What does a thermostatic oil cooler bypass do during cold operation?
choices: Allow oil to bypass or limit flow through the cooler until warm
questions.answerText: Allow oil to bypass or limit flow through the cooler until warm
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
When oil is cold and viscous, the thermostatic bypass limits flow through the cooler so the oil can warm without excessive restriction.

**Engineering principle**
As the oil reaches its operating range, the thermostat routes more flow through the cooler.

**Memory hook**
Cold: bypass cooler; warm: use cooler.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why is oil viscosity important to an aircraft engine?
choices: It affects film strength, flow, and lubrication across the operating temperature range
questions.answerText: It affects film strength, flow, and lubrication across the operating temperature range
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Viscosity affects how readily oil flows and how well it maintains a lubricating film. The correct grade must work across the engine temperature range.

**Engineering principle**
Too-viscous oil can circulate poorly when cold; too-thin hot oil may not maintain the required film.

**Memory hook**
Choose viscosity for the full temperature range.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What can a clogged main oil filter bypass valve permit?
choices: All oil flow to stop in every design
Oil flow to continue around the filter, though unfiltered
The oil pump to reverse direction
Fuel to enter the sump by design
questions.answerText: Oil flow to continue around the filter, though unfiltered
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A filter bypass allows oil to continue circulating when the main filter is restricted, but the bypassed oil may be unfiltered.

**Engineering principle**
Maintaining flow can prevent immediate oil starvation; bypass operation still requires inspection and corrective maintenance.

**Memory hook**
Bypass preserves flow, not cleanliness.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why are oil screens and filters inspected for debris?
choices: Debris can indicate wear or internal damage
questions.answerText: Debris can indicate wear or internal damage
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Debris captured by screens and filters can reveal abnormal wear or internal damage. Identify the material and source before deciding the engine is serviceable.

**Engineering principle**
A particle is a symptom, not a diagnosis; the approved limits and inspection procedure determine disposition.

**Memory hook**
Inspect the debris and find its source.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the function of an oil cooler?
choices: Remove heat from circulating engine oil
Cool intake air in every engine
questions.answerText: Remove heat from circulating engine oil
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An oil cooler rejects heat from circulating oil to cooling air or another heat sink. It helps keep viscosity and lubrication within the operating range.

**Engineering principle**
The cooler removes heat; a thermostatic bypass controls how much oil passes through it.

**Memory hook**
The cooler carries heat away.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of oil jets directed at piston undersides in some engines?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Oil jets spray the piston underside to remove heat and provide lubrication to the piston and cylinder assembly.

**Engineering principle**
The jet flow depends on the engine lubrication circuit and must be clear and correctly aimed.

**Memory hook**
Oil jets cool the piston from below.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why is crankcase breather flow maintained?
choices: Relieve internal pressure and remove blow-by vapors
questions.answerText: Relieve internal pressure and remove blow-by vapors
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The crankcase breather releases blow-by gases and limits pressure buildup inside the crankcase. It also helps carry vapors away.

**Engineering principle**
A blocked breather can cause pressure, leakage, or seal problems; excessive flow can signal blow-by.

**Memory hook**
The breather vents crankcase pressure.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is a likely cause of low oil pressure with normal oil temperature?
choices: Low oil quantity, pump wear, leakage, or a pressure-control fault
questions.answerText: Low oil quantity, pump wear, leakage, or a pressure-control fault
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Low pressure with normal oil temperature can result from low quantity, pump wear, leakage, a worn bearing clearance, or a pressure-control fault.

**Engineering principle**
An indication alone does not identify one cause; use the manufacturer troubleshooting sequence and confirm quantity safely.

**Memory hook**
Low pressure is a symptom with several possible causes.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why can excessively high oil temperature reduce lubrication effectiveness?
choices: Hot oil becomes less viscous and may not maintain the intended film
It increases oil pressure without limit
questions.answerText: Hot oil becomes less viscous and may not maintain the intended film
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Hotter oil has lower viscosity and may not maintain the designed lubricating film, especially at loaded bearings. High temperature can also accelerate oil oxidation.

**Engineering principle**
The effect depends on oil grade, pressure, clearances, and temperature limit; investigate an abnormal indication promptly.

**Memory hook**
Heat thins oil and speeds deterioration.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What does an oil temperature bulb sense?
choices: Oil temperature at the point where the sensor is installed
questions.answerText: Oil temperature at the point where the sensor is installed
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An oil-temperature bulb or probe senses temperature at the point where it is installed in the oil circuit. The reading is not necessarily the temperature everywhere in the engine.

**Engineering principle**
Sensor location and flow path affect the indicated value.

**Memory hook**
The bulb reports local oil temperature.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why are oil lines routed away from hot exhaust parts?
choices: Avoid overheating, damage, and fire risk if oil leaks
questions.answerText: Avoid overheating, damage, and fire risk if oil leaks
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Oil lines are kept away from hot exhaust parts to reduce heat damage and the chance that leaking oil will ignite.

**Engineering principle**
Support and routing must also prevent chafing, vibration fatigue, and interference.

**Memory hook**
Keep fluid lines clear of hot and moving parts.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the role of cylinder fins on an air-cooled engine?
choices: Increase surface area for heat transfer to cooling air
questions.answerText: Increase surface area for heat transfer to cooling air
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Cylinder fins increase exposed surface area so heat can transfer from the cylinder metal to cooling air.

**Engineering principle**
Fins add area; baffles and cowl geometry direct air across that area.

**Memory hook**
More fin area improves heat transfer.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: How do cowl flaps influence cylinder cooling?
choices: They change cooling-air exit area and pressure distribution
questions.answerText: They change cooling-air exit area and pressure distribution
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Cowl flaps change the cooling-air exit opening and pressure distribution through the cowling, which changes airflow over the cylinders.

**Engineering principle**
Their effect depends on the inlet, baffles, outlet, and aircraft speed; they regulate airflow rather than produce cooling by themselves.

**Memory hook**
Cowl flaps control cooling-air exit flow.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What can cause an air-cooled cylinder to run hotter than the others?
choices: Restricted cooling airflow, mixture imbalance, or abnormal combustion
questions.answerText: Restricted cooling airflow, mixture imbalance, or abnormal combustion
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A cylinder may run hotter because cooling air is restricted, mixture is uneven, combustion is abnormal, or an engine component is failing.

**Engineering principle**
Compare cylinder indications and inspect airflow, mixture distribution, ignition, and engine condition; do not assume one cause.

**Memory hook**
Hot cylinder: check both airflow and combustion.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why should an engine be allowed to warm before high-power operation?
choices: It prevents the starter from disengaging
Cold oil circulates less readily and clearances have not reached operating conditions
questions.answerText: Cold oil circulates less readily and clearances have not reached operating conditions
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Allowing warm-up lets cold, viscous oil circulate more readily and lets engine clearances approach their intended operating condition before high loads are applied.

**Engineering principle**
Follow the manufacturer warm-up limits; excessive idling can also cause poor temperature control or plug fouling.

**Memory hook**
Warm the oil before applying high power.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a pressure-oil passage in a crankshaft?
choices: Deliver oil to bearings and journals through internal drillings
Carry induction air to the cylinders
questions.answerText: Deliver oil to bearings and journals through internal drillings
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Internal crankshaft drillings route pressure oil to journals and bearing surfaces. The passages must remain clean so oil reaches the loaded interfaces.

**Engineering principle**
A blocked passage can starve a bearing even when the main pressure indication appears normal.

**Memory hook**
Drilled crankshafts deliver oil inside the shaft.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why are oil seals installed at rotating shafts?
choices: Hold the piston rings in place
Limit lubricant leakage while allowing shaft rotation
questions.answerText: Limit lubricant leakage while allowing shaft rotation
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A rotating-shaft seal limits lubricant leakage while allowing the shaft to turn. The seal must suit shaft speed, temperature, pressure, and movement.

**Engineering principle**
A seal controls leakage; it does not eliminate the need for correct lubrication or shaft condition.

**Memory hook**
Seal the leak path while allowing rotation.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What does foaming or aeration in engine oil tend to do?
choices: Reduce the oil pump’s ability to provide a stable lubricating flow
Increase oil film strength in every case
questions.answerText: Reduce the oil pump’s ability to provide a stable lubricating flow
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Air entrained in foamy oil makes pump delivery less stable and can reduce the effective lubricating flow to bearings.

**Engineering principle**
Aeration can result from low quantity, return-flow issues, or other system faults; follow approved troubleshooting.

**Memory hook**
Foam makes oil delivery unreliable.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why is oil quantity checked using the aircraft manufacturer’s specified procedure?
choices: Oil expands only when the engine runs
The quantity is set by fuel level
Oil drains back and system configuration affects the indicated quantity
questions.answerText: Oil drains back and system configuration affects the indicated quantity
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Oil drains back after shutdown and system configuration affects the dipstick or sight indication. The specified timing and procedure make the quantity reading repeatable.

**Engineering principle**
A reading taken too soon or in the wrong aircraft attitude can misstate the available oil.

**Memory hook**
Check quantity using the prescribed procedure.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an oil-pressure warning switch?
choices: Warn when pressure falls below a specified threshold
questions.answerText: Warn when pressure falls below a specified threshold
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
An oil-pressure warning switch closes or changes state when pressure crosses its set threshold, activating a warning circuit.

**Engineering principle**
It is a threshold warning device, not a calibrated pressure gauge.

**Memory hook**
Switch warns at a limit; gauge shows a value.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the function of a propeller governor oil passage in a hydraulically controlled propeller system?
choices: Route oil pressure used to change blade pitch
questions.answerText: Route oil pressure used to change blade pitch
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
In a hydraulically controlled propeller, governor oil pressure is routed through passages to move the piston that changes blade angle.

**Engineering principle**
The governor regulates RPM by controlling oil flow and pressure to the propeller mechanism.

**Memory hook**
Oil pressure moves the propeller piston.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Why are oil analysis trends more useful than a single sample alone?
choices: Trends set the engine’s firing order
Changes over time can reveal developing wear or contamination
A single sample cannot contain oil
questions.answerText: Changes over time can reveal developing wear or contamination
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A single oil sample shows one condition; a trend reveals whether wear metals or contaminants are increasing over time.

**Engineering principle**
Compare results with consistent sampling, engine hours, and laboratory limits before deciding that wear is abnormal.

**Memory hook**
Trend the sample; do not overread one result.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a cylinder-head temperature indication?
choices: Monitor the thermal condition of the cylinder head
questions.answerText: Monitor the thermal condition of the cylinder head
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Cylinder-head temperature indication monitors the thermal condition near the installed probe. It can reveal overheating during changes in power, mixture, cooling airflow, or combustion.

**Engineering principle**
The sensor measures local head temperature, not exhaust-gas temperature or oil temperature.

**Memory hook**
CHT measures the cylinder head near its probe.

**Board tip**
Use the engine maker?s specified operating limits and maintenance procedure for a real discrepancy.

questions.question: Compression ratio is the ratio between the
choices: Combustion chamber pressure on the combustion stroke and on the exhaust stroke.
Cylinder volume with piston at bottom dead center and at top dead center.
Piston travel on the compression stroke and on the intake stroke.
Cylinder pressure at bottom dead center divided by pressure at top dead center.
questions.answerText: Cylinder volume with piston at bottom dead center and at top dead center.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Volume is an extensive thermodynamic property: it scales with the amount of matter. If 'bulk property' is being used to mean a macroscopic/extensive property, volume is in fact a bulk property; the question may instead intend an intensive-property contrast. The wording needs clarification before scoring.

**Engineering principle**
Volume is extensive; temperature and pressure are intensive. 'Bulk property' is not a precise synonym for 'not extensive' in standard thermodynamics usage.

💡 **Memory hook:** Double the system amount → double the volume (at same state per unit mass).

🎯 **Board tip:** Check the source’s definition of 'bulk property'; as written, the keyed item is ambiguous.

questions.question: Excessive valve clearances will cause the duration of valve opening to
choices: decrease for intake valves and increase for exhaust valves.
increase for both intake and exhaust valves.
decrease for both intake and exhaust valves.
questions.answerText: decrease for both intake and exhaust valves.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Excessive valve lash means the cam must take up more clearance before moving the valve, so opening occurs later and closing earlier. This shortens open duration and usually reduces lift.

questions.question: Most exhaust system failures result from thermal fatigue cracking in the areas of stress concentration. This condition is usually caused by
choices: the low exhaust-gas pressure encountered during cruise.
the drastic temperature change which is encountered at altitude.
the high temperatures at which the exhaust system operates.
questions.answerText: the high temperatures at which the exhaust system operates.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Exhaust components experience repeated thermal cycles, vibration, and stress concentration at bends, joints, and supports. Thermal fatigue initiates cracks at those locations; inspect them closely.

questions.question: On which strokes are both valves on a four-stroke cycle reciprocating engine open?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
During overlap near the exhaust/intake transition, both valves are briefly off their seats. This helps scavenge exhaust and fill the cylinder; it is measured in crankshaft degrees.

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding a four-stroke cycle aircraft engine?
choices: The intake valve closes on the intake stroke.
The intake valve closes on the compression stroke.
The intake valve closes on the exhaust stroke.
The exhaust valve opens on the exhaust stroke.
questions.answerText: The intake valve closes on the compression stroke.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The intake valve closes after the piston passes bottom dead center and begins compression. The incoming charge continues moving into the cylinder, so the valve closes after BDC.

questions.question: Valve overlap is defined as the number of degrees of crankshaft travel
choices: only while the intake valve is open.
during which both valves are on their seats.
during which both valves are off their seats.
between the closing of the intake valve and the opening of the exhaust valve.
questions.answerText: during which both valves are off their seats.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Valve overlap is the crankshaft interval around the exhaust/intake transition when both valves are off their seats. It is an angular interval, not a time or lift value.

questions.question: If the exhaust valve of a four-stroke cycle engine is closed and the intake valve is just closed, the piston is on the
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
With intake and exhaust valves closed and the piston rising after the intake valve closes, the charge is being compressed. That is the compression stroke.

questions.question: Which of the following will be caused by excessive valve clearance of a cylinder on a reciprocating aircraft engine?
choices: Intake and exhaust valves will open early and close late.
A power increase by shortening the exhaust event.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Excessive clearance delays valve opening and advances closing, reducing the period both valves are off their seats. This shortens overlap and can reduce scavenging and volumetric efficiency.

questions.question: To what altitude will a turbocharged engine maintain sea level pressure?
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Critical altitude is the highest altitude at which the turbocharger can maintain the specified sea-level manifold pressure under its limits. Above it, manifold pressure begins to fall.

questions.question: One cause of afterburning in an aircraft engine is _____.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The keyed phrase afterburning is ambiguous in a piston-engine context. In a reciprocating engine, an excessively rich mixture can leave unburned fuel that ignites in the exhaust (afterfiring). A turbine-engine afterburner is a separate, intentional thrust-augmentation system.

**Engineering principle**
The event's location and engine type distinguish exhaust afterfire from a turbine afterburner.

**Memory hook:** Piston exhaust afterfire is unintended; turbine afterburning is designed.

**Board tip:** Confirm which engine and definition the source intends before scoring this terminology.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a wastegate in a turbocharged piston-engine installation?
choices: Regulate exhaust gas flow through the turbine and control boost
questions.answerText: Regulate exhaust gas flow through the turbine and control boost
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The wastegate meters exhaust flow through the turbine. Opening it bypasses exhaust energy and reduces boost; closing it directs more gas through the turbine to increase compressor output within limits.

questions.question: What drives the compressor of an exhaust-driven turbocharger?
choices: A turbine powered by engine exhaust gas
A belt from the propeller hub only
questions.answerText: A turbine powered by engine exhaust gas
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Exhaust gas turns the turbocharger turbine, which is mechanically coupled by a shaft to the intake compressor. Exhaust energy therefore supplies compressor drive.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a supercharger?
choices: Raise induction-air pressure above the pressure available from normal aspiration
questions.answerText: Raise induction-air pressure above the pressure available from normal aspiration
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A supercharger raises induction pressure so the cylinders receive more air mass than ambient pressure alone would provide. It can offset altitude power loss or increase charge density.

questions.question: What is a principal difference between a mechanically driven supercharger and an exhaust turbocharger?
choices: The supercharger uses no induction air
The two terms always describe an identical drive source
The supercharger is driven mechanically by the engine; the turbocharger uses exhaust energy
questions.answerText: The supercharger is driven mechanically by the engine; the turbocharger uses exhaust energy
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A mechanically driven supercharger is powered from the engine crankshaft. An exhaust turbocharger uses exhaust gas to drive a turbine connected to its compressor, recovering exhaust energy.

questions.question: Why can excessive turbocharger boost damage a piston engine?
choices: It lowers air density to zero
It stops oil circulation by definition
It reduces the fuel-air ratio automatically
It can raise cylinder pressure and temperature beyond approved limits
questions.answerText: It can raise cylinder pressure and temperature beyond approved limits
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Excess boost raises charge density, cylinder pressure, and temperature. Beyond approved limits this can cause detonation or excessive mechanical and thermal stress.

questions.question: What does a pressure controller do in a turbocharger system?
choices: Schedules wastegate operation to control manifold pressure
questions.answerText: Schedules wastegate operation to control manifold pressure
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A pressure controller schedules wastegate position to maintain commanded manifold pressure within limits. It controls boost through exhaust flow, rather than changing ignition timing or fuel mixture directly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an intercooler or aftercooler in a boosted induction system?
choices: Remove heat from compressed air and increase its density
Heat fuel to its flash point
questions.answerText: Remove heat from compressed air and increase its density
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Compressed induction air is hot. An intercooler/aftercooler removes heat, increasing air density for a given pressure and reducing thermal stress and detonation tendency.

questions.question: Why can a turbocharged engine maintain higher manifold pressure at altitude than a normally aspirated engine?
choices: Its cylinders grow larger at altitude
The compressor raises intake pressure using exhaust energy
questions.answerText: The compressor raises intake pressure using exhaust energy
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Gas-turbine components condition the flow in sequence. The compressor raises pressure; the diffuser slows air and converts velocity to static pressure before combustion; the combustor adds heat; the turbine extracts work; and the nozzle accelerates exhaust for thrust.

**Engineering principle**
A rotor adds energy to the flow; a stator redirects and diffuses it. Nozzle guide vanes accelerate and direct gas into the turbine rotor. Compressor bleed or variable vanes help maintain stable operation away from design conditions.

💡 **Memory hook:** Compressor raises pressure; diffuser slows flow; nozzle speeds exhaust.

🎯 **Board tip:** Track whether the question asks about pressure rise, velocity change, or flow direction.

questions.question: What can an exhaust leak near a turbine inlet cause?
choices: A lower compression ratio in every cylinder
Loss of turbine-driving energy and local overheating or damage
questions.answerText: Loss of turbine-driving energy and local overheating or damage
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Thermodynamic questions depend on the system boundary, process constraint, and sign convention. Apply conservation of energy and the ideal-gas/process relation that matches the stated condition; use absolute temperature and absolute pressure in gas-law ratios.

**Engineering principle**
Adiabatic means no heat transfer; isentropic additionally requires reversibility. Specific heat at constant pressure differs from constant volume, and work done by a system has the opposite sign from work done on it.

💡 **Memory hook:** Name the process before choosing the equation.

🎯 **Board tip:** Check absolute versus gauge pressure and state the work sign convention.

questions.question: Why are exhaust-system joints and supports inspected for cracks?
choices: Thermal cycling and vibration can initiate fatigue cracks
They control the fuel metering pressure
questions.answerText: Thermal cycling and vibration can initiate fatigue cracks
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Exhaust components experience high temperature gradients and repeated heating/cooling, while engine vibration adds cyclic mechanical stress. Stress concentrations at joints, welds, and supports can therefore initiate fatigue cracks.

**Engineering principle**
Thermal fatigue arises from repeated temperature-driven strain; vibration fatigue comes from repeated mechanical loading. Both can act together.

💡 **Memory hook:** Heat cycles plus vibration → fatigue risk.

🎯 **Board tip:** Inspect attachment points and hot spots for cracks, leakage, and fretting.

questions.question: What is exhaust backfire in a reciprocating engine?
choices: Combustion or unburned mixture ignites in the induction system
Fuel vapor condenses in the tank
questions.answerText: Combustion or unburned mixture ignites in the induction system
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A reciprocating-engine exhaust backfire is combustion that propagates backward into the induction system, often after an abnormal mixture or valve/timing condition. The stored answer describes that induction-system event rather than an exhaust event.

**Engineering principle**
An intake backfire is heard or observed in the induction path; afterfiring is combustion in the exhaust after the charge leaves the cylinder.

**Memory hook:** Backfire into intake; afterfire in exhaust.

**Board tip**
The question's phrase exhaust backfire conflicts with the keyed induction-system definition; verify the original wording.

questions.question: What is afterfiring in the exhaust system?
choices: Oil pressure rises above the limit
Unburned fuel-air mixture ignites in the exhaust after leaving the cylinder
questions.answerText: Unburned fuel-air mixture ignites in the exhaust after leaving the cylinder
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Afterfiring is continued or delayed combustion in the exhaust system after the charge has left the cylinder. Unburned fuel-air mixture can ignite in hot exhaust gases.

**Engineering principle**
This differs from an induction backfire, which propagates into the intake system, and from a turbine afterburner, which is a designed thrust-augmentation device.

**Memory hook:** Afterfire occurs after the cylinder, in the exhaust.

**Board tip:** Identify where combustion occurs before naming the event.

questions.question: A turbocharger compressor raises absolute inlet pressure from 60 kPa to 150 kPa. Find compressor pressure ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Compressor pressure ratio = discharge absolute pressure/inlet absolute pressure = 150 kPa/60 kPa = 2.5. The kPa units cancel; use absolute pressures.

questions.question: A turbo system has 80 kPa absolute inlet pressure and 160 kPa absolute manifold pressure. Find pressure ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Pressure ratio = 160 kPa absolute/80 kPa absolute = 2. The compressor doubles inlet absolute pressure.

questions.question: A normally aspirated engine takes in air at 90 kPa absolute while a turbocharger supplies 135 kPa absolute. Find pressure ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Pressure ratio = 135 kPa absolute/90 kPa absolute = 1.5. The result is dimensionless; do not use gauge pressure in a ratio.

questions.question: A turbocharger increases inlet pressure from 70 kPa to 140 kPa absolute. Find the pressure ratio.
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Pressure ratio = 140 kPa absolute/70 kPa absolute = 2. Always divide outlet absolute pressure by inlet absolute pressure.

questions.question: A compressor receives air at 100 kPa and delivers it at 180 kPa absolute. What is the pressure ratio?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Compressor pressure ratio = 180 kPa/100 kPa = 1.8. Both pressures are absolute, so the ratio is valid and unitless.

questions.question: Exhaust gas transfers 12 kJ of energy per second to a turbine. How much energy is transferred in 5 seconds?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Power is energy per time: 12 kJ/s. In 5 s, transferred energy = 12 kJ/s x 5 s = 60 kJ; seconds cancel.

questions.question: A turbocharger shaft turns at 90,000 rpm. How many revolutions does it make in 2 seconds?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
90,000 rev/min / 60 = 1,500 rev/s. Over 2 s, revolutions = 1,500 x 2 = 3,000 rev.

questions.question: A controller limits manifold pressure to 40 inHg absolute. The sensed pressure is 36 inHg. How far below the limit is it?
questions.explanation:
**Worked solution**
Pressure margin below the limit = 40 inHg - 36 inHg = 4 inHg. Both readings are absolute pressures, so subtract directly.

chapters/gas-turbine-theory-and-engine-t.title: Gas Turbine Theory and Engine Types

questions.question: Some high-volume turboprop and turbojet engines are equipped with two-spool or split compressors. When these engines are operated at high altitudes, the
choices: low-pressure rotor will decrease in speed as the compressor load decreases in the lower density air.
low-pressure rotor will increase in speed as the compressor load decreases in the lower density air.
the high-pressure rotor will always overspeed as inlet-air density decreases.
throttle must be retarded to prevent overspeeding of the high-pressure rotor due to the lower density air.
